item_011.source_text:
Demotic: Spiegelberg 1917 is public domain (author died 1930). Two scans are on archive.org: dergyptischemy01leyduoft (about 220 pages; may lack the plates or glossary, as the 1994 Olms reprint runs to 430 pages) and dergyptischemy01rijk.
Greek P.Lond.Lit. 192 (= P. BM 274): Reitzenstein 1923 is public domain (author died 1931) and open on archive.org (diegriechischete0000brit, 42 pages).
The standard modern edition, de Cenival 1988 (Demotische Studien 9), is in copyright, as are Hoffmann & Quack 2018 and West 1969 (JEA). The TLA online transliteration and translation may be openly licensed (TLA data is usually CC BY-SA), but I could not verify this. papyri.info was down when I checked.
item_011.research_yield: Articles on: how a Demotic text was rendered into Greek (Leiden text against P.Lond.Lit. 192); the Lion and the Mouse between the Egyptian and Aesopic traditions; the Myth as an Egyptian frame narrative and its links to Greek fiction and the Nectanebo/Alexander Romance material; and a methodological critique of uncontrolled AI pseudo-translations (the WLA case).
item_011.recommendation: Keep, at moderate priority. The gap is real only for Russian: no complete Russian translation exists, and the Russian fables are popular adaptations. English, French, German and Italian versions exist, and the Demotic is hard to validate. Best first unit: the Greek version (P.Lond.Lit. 192, from Reitzenstein's public-domain text) with the Demotic passages it parallels, rendered via Spiegelberg's transliteration and checked against de Cenival and Hoffmann & Quack.

item_012.ru_found:
No scholarly Russian translation of any SA.GIG tablet was found. Only isolated entries appear, quoted second-hand.
(1) HSE IOCS student anthology "Гадательные практики Древней Месопотамии: материалы для антологии" (2020), supervised by R. M. Nurullin; the diagnostic section is by A. M. Musaeva (https://iocs.hse.ru/mirror/pubs/share/374762450.pdf). Its preface describes Sakikkû and quotes the Tablet 1-2 incipit «если заклинатель идет в дом больного». It translates only the Old Babylonian diagnostic texts TLB 2, 21 and CUSAS 18, 15, not SA.GIG. The companion PDF 482110251 has no diagnostic texts.
(2) Russian edition of Ch. Fossey, «Ассирийская магия» (pub. «Евразия»; scan at archive.org/details/20220814_20220814_1526). The editor's appendix translates the Exorcist's Manual KAR 44, which lists SA.GIG only by section titles such as «Симптомы болезни». The editor is probably V. V. Emelianov, but this is not verified.
(3) Popular and textbook material: Sorokina-type «История медицины» textbook (bibliotekar.ru/421/15.htm) quotes one or two entries; a Habr article (2017) paraphrases the pig omen from Tablet 1.
(4) ru.wikipedia has no article for Сакикку or Эсагил-кин-апли.
Searches run: Google ×4 (Сакикку диагностический трактат; Эсагил-кин-апли/Эсагиль-кин-апли; «заклинатель» «в дом больного»; «Гадательные практики Древней Месопотамии»). Bing ×5 (SA.GIG перевод; вавилонские диагностические тексты перевод; ассиро-вавилонская медицина перевод; диагностический справочник Эсагил; «Когда в дом больного заклинатель идет»). Also ru.wiki ×2. Gaps: the CyberLeninka API returned 0 even for generic queries, and Yandex/Google blocked further queries with a captcha, so elibrary/CyberLeninka could not be properly checked.
item_012.en_found:
English coverage is near-complete, but the colleague's evidence is wrong for the pilot unit.
(1) Scurlock, Sourcebook for Ancient Mesopotamian Medicine (SBL WAW 36, 2014), ch. 1, pp. 13-272, gives transliteration and English translation of DPS 3-14, 15-17, 18-23, 26-30, 31-32, 33-34, 36-37, 39 and 40. It explicitly excludes "the purely divinatory material contained in the first two tablets". The full book PDF is free at sbl-site.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/SourcebookAncientMesoMed_Scurlock_SBL.pdf but marked "All rights reserved".
(2) Tablet 1 IS in English: A. R. George, "Babylonian Texts from the Folios of Sidney Smith, Part Two: Prognostic and Diagnostic Omens, Tablet I", RA 85 (1991) 137-167. It is a reconstructed edition with full English translation, e.g. "If he sees a black pig: that patient will die". Free copies on Academia.edu (25634891) and SOAS repository; JSTOR 23281884.
(3) Tablet 2: no English translation found.
(4) Other English: Scurlock & Andersen, Diagnoses (2005), entries arranged by disease; Stol, Epilepsy in Babylonia (1993), Tablets 26-30; Stol 2000, Tablets 36-37; Wee, PhD 2012 and Brill 2019, Sa-gig commentaries including Tablet 1 (CCP 4.1.1.A-D, ccp.yale.edu/P348448); Schmidtchen 2018, Esagil-kin-apli catalogue (open-access De Gruyter volume).
item_012.other_found:
FRENCH: Labat, Traité akkadien de diagnostics et pronostics médicaux (1951). Complete for the material known then, including Tablets 1-2. Commentary on Tablet 1: Durand, RA 73 (1979) 153-170. Tablet 40: Cadelli 1997.
GERMAN: Heeßel, Babylonisch-assyrische Diagnostik (AOAT 43, 2000): scored edition with translation of Tablets 15-23, 26-31 and 33. Heeßel, "Wenn ein Mann zum Haus des Kranken geht…", AfO 48/49 (2001/02) 24-49: edition of Tablet 2 with translation. Heeßel in TUAT NF 5 (2010/11) 8-31: selections from Tablets 1, 4, 9, 13, 16, 26, 33, 36 and 40. Volk 1999: Tablet 40.
ONLINE: tianmu.org "Good Works Library" (2026) offers an English rendering of Tablet 7 (K.261) built from eBL data. Not relevant to Tablets 1-2.
No Italian or Spanish translations found.
item_012.source_text:
There is no public-domain critical text. Every modern edition is in copyright:
- Labat 1951: René Labat died 1974, so protected until about 2044; archive.org copy is lending-only.
- Heeßel 2000 and 2001 (AfO).
- George 1991 (RA): free PDF, but not openly licensed.
- Scurlock 2014: free PDF, all rights reserved.
Best working sources for the pilot unit: Tablet 1 from George 1991 (composite transliteration, freely posted); Tablet 2 from Heeßel 2001 (AfO 48/49). The cuneiform tablets themselves are public domain, with CDLI photos. The eBL Fragmentarium (CC BY 4.0) transliterates some SA.GIG manuscripts, e.g. K.261 (Tablet 7), but not the key Tablet 1 manuscript BM 38362 (eBL record has no transliteration). eBL has no Sakikkû corpus edition. CCP commentary editions are online but the site footer says "All rights reserved".
item_012.research_yield: Babylonian diagnostic omens compared with the Hippocratic Prognostic (after Geller); intertext between SA.GIG Tablet 2 and Šumma ālu; colour and animal symbolism in medical prognosis; first Russian-language overview of Mesopotamian diagnostic science. All of this depends on Akkadian expertise rather than Greek or Latin.
item_012.recommendation: Drop, or keep only as a low-priority Russian-only gap. The proposed Tablets 1-2 unit is not untranslated: Tablet 1 has a full English translation (George 1991), and the rest of the preserved text is in Scurlock 2014. If kept, the best first unit is Tablet 2 (base: Heeßel 2001), the only part without English, translated into both Russian and English.

item_013.title_short: Persepolis Fortification Tablets (Elamite), Hallock Q texts (travel rations)
item_013.ru_found:
The claim of "none" is refuted. Russian selections exist, but only as excerpts.
(1) M.A. Dandamaev, transl. and comm., "20. Эламские документы", in Хрестоматия по истории Древнего Востока, ч. 2, ed. M.A. Korostovtsev et al. (Moscow: Vysshaya shkola, 1980), pp. ~39–43. It covers about 13 PF/Fort. texts and 3 PTT texts, translated from Hallock 1969 and Cameron 1948. The PF/Fort. texts are PF 6, 1795, Fort. 6764, PF 1943, 662, 664, 668. It also includes 6 of the proposed Q texts: PF 1383, 1385, 1397, 1404, 1547 and 1565. I verified this in the OCR of the volume (archive.org/details/11980-583202508).
(2) The same selection is reprinted in История Древнего Востока. Тексты и документы, ed. V.I. Kuzishchin (Moscow, 2002), sect. III.2 no. 17, pp. ~404–407 (archive.org/details/2002-3166120250814). It is also online at biblicalstudy.ru/Lib/Epigraph/27.html.
(3) M.A. Dandamaev, "Новые документы царского хозяйства в Иране (509–494 гг. до н.э.) (Обзор текстов, изданных Р.Т. Халлоком)", ВДИ 1972 no. 1, pp. 3–26 (PDF at elib.gsu.by). This is a review that paraphrases and partly quotes dozens of texts, including many Q texts such as PF 1259, 1272, 1287, 1321, 1397, 1404, 1418, 1455, 1477, 1552, 1555 and 1560. It is not a translation corpus.
(4) Studies that cite PF texts by number with little or no translation: Dandamaev's monographs, including Ахеменидская империя (SPb 2013) and, with Lukonin, Культура и экономика древнего Ирана (1980; not opened); T.Yu. Shashlova, Известия Саратовского ун-та 2014; E.V. Rung; V.P. Orlov (Kazan).
Searches: Bing (ru) for персепольские таблички крепостной стены / Хрестоматия Дандамаев / диссертация / Тексты и документы / перевод персепольских табличек; CyberLeninka API (персепольские таблички, персепольский архив, эламские документы Персеполя, Фарнак Персеполь, Hallock). No full or category-level Russian translation was found.
item_013.en_found:
For the proposed unit the English status is FULL, not "partial". R.T. Hallock, Persepolis Fortification Tablets (OIP 92, Chicago 1969) gives a transliteration and English translation of every published text, PF 1–2087. That includes all Q texts, which are PF 1285–1579 and 2049–2057 (304 texts), as I verified in the OIP 92 table of contents and the Q section heading (p. 365).
Further English: Hallock 1978, "Selected Fortification Texts", CDAFI 8:109–136 (33 texts). W. Henkelman's collated editions of the Hallock Nachlass (NN) and PFa texts with English translations, on Achemenet and the ISAC OCHRE PFA database; Henkelman 2008, The Other Gods Who Are (Achaemenid History 14). A. Arfaee 2008, Persepolis Fortification Tablets: Fort. and Teh. Texts (Tehran). A. Kuhrt 2007, The Persian Empire: A Corpus of Sources (selected PF texts). Q texts in all number 719, including NN and Fort. texts (Makvandi 2013). The "95% unpublished" part of the archive is mostly fragments, is not accessible, and much of it is being edited in English by the PFA Project.
item_013.other_found:
French: W. Henkelman, L'univers des Achéménides: les tablettes de l'Archive des Fortifications de Persépolis (HDR, EPHE 2020, HAL tel-03967878); P. Briant's works; Achemenet (French interface); Giovinazzo's "Les documents de voyage dans les textes de Persépolis" (core.ac.uk), which deals with travel texts specifically.
German: H. Koch, Verwaltung und Wirtschaft im persischen Kernland zur Zeit der Achämeniden (Wiesbaden: Reichert 1990), and her popular Es kündet Dareios der König (1992), both with many translated tablets.
Persian: Arfaee 2008, and Makvandi's studies of the Q texts (Pazand 2013; JARCS).
Italian and Spanish: no dedicated translations found (not exhaustively checked).
item_013.source_text: Hallock, OIP 92 (1969): free PDF from ISAC (isac.uchicago.edu/publications/persepolis-fortification-tablets, DOI 10.83354/9b6c-t494), licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. A scan is also at archive.org/details/oip92. CDLI hosts Hallock's PF transliterations; I did not check their licence. The OCHRE PFA database has images and editions of NN/Fort. texts. The standard edition is in copyright (US publication 1969; renewal was automatic for works of that period). It is openly available only under the NC-ND licence. Non-commercial reuse of the transliterations is acceptable, but Hallock's English translations must not be adapted. A Russian translation made through Hallock's English would in practice be a derivative of his translation.
item_013.research_yield: A Russian-commented Q corpus would support articles on the Achaemenid road and courier system against Herodotus 5.52–54 and 8.98 and Xenophon's Cyropaedia 8.6. Other possible articles: travellers from Sardis, India, Bactria and Arabia; Yaunā in Persian service; and how court logistics compare with the Alexander historians. Yield for Russian readers is moderate; the work would not be first-ever.
item_013.recommendation: Drop it as a "first-ever translation", or keep it only as a low-priority Russian-only project. All the published texts, the Q unit included, are fully in English (Hallock 1969). The Elamite is outside the editor's Greek/Latin competence and LLMs know little Elamite, so the translation would in practice be made from Hallock's English. If pursued, the best first unit is the roughly 30 long-distance Q texts (Sardis, India, Arachosia, Bactria, Egypt) that Dandamaev did not translate, as a commented Russian dossier set against the Greek sources.

item_014.title_short: Murašû archive, Nippur (texts naming Ctesian nobles / BE 10)
item_014.ru_found: REFUTED: the "none" claim is wrong. Russian translations of Murašû texts exist; I checked them in the archive.org OCR full texts. (1) Хрестоматия по истории Древнего Востока, ч. 1, ред. М.А. Коростовцев, И.С. Кацнельсон, В.И. Кузищин (М.: Высшая школа, 1980). Section VII «Рабство в Вавилонии в VII–IV вв. до н.э.», translation and commentary by М.А. Дандамаев, includes 5 Murašû texts: no. 17 = PBS 2/1 [UM II/1] 106, no. 18 = BE 10 54, no. 25 = PBS 2/1 118, no. 26 = BE 10 104, no. 27 = PBS 2/1 131. They form the dossier of Ribat son of Bel-riba, slave of Rimut-Ninurta, pp. c. 227–230. https://archive.org/details/11980-583202508. (2) История Древнего Востока. Тексты и документы, ред. В.И. Кузищин (М.: Высшая школа, 2002). Section III.2, no. 18 «Вавилонские документы», translation and commentary by М.А. Дандамаев, pp. c. 408–417, includes c. 16 Murašû texts: BE 9 7, 11, 32a, 48, 54, 73, 75; BE 10 50, 85, 111; PBS 2/1 5, 103, 144, 201; and Krückmann TuM 2/3 147 and 185. These overlap the proposed pilot unit directly: they include the tax receipt under the seal of Manuštanu (= Ctesias' Menostanes), plus texts on Aršama's herds, Parysatis' estate, Ipradata son of prince Achaemenes, and Bagamihi. I found no Artoxares or Arbarius text in either selection. https://archive.org/details/2002-3166120250814. Negative checks: Струве, Хрестоматия по истории древнего мира т. I (1950), none; Крушкол, Хрестоматия (1987), none; CyberLeninka searches for Мурашу / Ниппур / «Мурашу Ниппур архив» found no translation articles; ru.wikipedia API search for «Мурашу» returns only passing mentions. Not checked: Dandamaev's Russian monographs (e.g. Рабство в Вавилонии, 1974), which probably quote further passages, and ВДИ. Method note: the WebSearch quota was used up, and Bing, DuckDuckGo, Yandex and Google either served CAPTCHAs or returned unrelated results. The Russian checks therefore used CyberLeninka's API, the ru.wikipedia API, archive.org metadata search, and full-text grep of the four Russian readers.
item_014.en_found: Confirmed by full-text OCR. Hilprecht & Clay, BE 9 (1898), has a section "Translations of selected texts" with transliteration and English translation of c. 12 texts. Clay, BE 10 (1904), does the same for c. 12–13 texts, including BE 10 54 and an Aršama sheep-and-goat rental text. The "complete transliteration and translation in Series C" promised in both volumes never appeared. Clay, PBS 2/1 (1912), has hand copies only and no translations. Stolper, Entrepreneurs and Empire (Naples 1985; archive.org stolper-1985-murashus-persia-babylonia) gives copies and transliterations of the 1893 University Museum and British Museum texts (Appendix II), with English renderings of many passages in the chapters. Known from the literature but not re-verified this session: Donbaz & Stolper, Istanbul Murašû Texts (PIHANS 79, 1997); Stolper's JCS and RA text publications; selections in A. Kuhrt, The Persian Empire: A Corpus of Sources (2007); Dandamaev, Slavery in Babylonia (1984) and Iranians in Achaemenid Babylonia (1992), which have English renderings or summaries (both on archive.org). There is no complete English translation of the archive.
item_014.other_found: German: J. Augapfel, Babylonische Rechtsurkunden aus der Regierungszeit Artaxerxes I. und Darius II. (Denkschriften der Kaiserlichen Akademie der Wissenschaften in Wien, phil.-hist. Kl. 59/3, Wien 1917). It gives transcription and German translation of a large selection (pp. 1–98, roughly 100+ texts) from BE 9, BE 10 and PBS 2/1, with a glossary. It is public domain and on archive.org: babylonische-rechtsurkunden.-artaxerxes-i.-und-darius-ii. French: G. Cardascia, Les archives des Murašû (Paris 1951), a legal study with translations of many texts; I did not inspect it this session. I did not search Italian or Spanish.
item_014.source_text: Public domain hand copies (autographs): BE 9 (Hilprecht & Clay 1898; archive.org businessdocumen00hilpgoog), BE 10 (Clay 1904; archive.org business-documents-of-murashu-sons-of-nippur-dated-in-the-reign-of-darius-ii-1904) and PBS 2/1 (Clay 1912; archive.org businessdocument00clay). The candidate file overstates their usability: only c. 25 texts are transliterated in BE 9/10. The only sizeable public domain transliteration is Augapfel 1917 (c. 100+ texts), and its readings are outdated, especially for Iranian names and loanwords. The standard modern editions are all in copyright: Cardascia 1951, Stolper 1985 (IUO Napoli; the archive.org scan does not change this), Donbaz–Stolper 1997 (NINO), and Stolper's later articles. Some transliterations may be on CDLI, but I did not confirm coverage or licence. An LLM cannot reliably work from the cuneiform hand copies, so modern transliterations are required and will have to be cited and checked.
item_014.research_yield: Prosopography linking Ctesias' Persika to the tablets (Menostanes/Manuštanu, Artoxares, Parysatis, Arsames); the 424/423 succession crisis; land-for-service (hatru); Iranian onomastics; Judeans at Nippur. The topics are good, but Stolper, Lewis and Dandamaev have already covered much of this ground.
item_014.recommendation: Drop the "untranslated in Russian" label: Dandamaev has already published Russian versions of c. 21 texts (1980, 2002), including a Manuštanu text, and the editor cannot validate Akkadian himself. Keep it only as a low-priority specialist item with an Assyriologist reviewer. Best first unit: the Ctesian-noble dossier (Manuštanu, Artaḫaršu, Arbareme) minus the texts Dandamaev already covers, translated from Stolper's and Augapfel's transliterations.

item_015.title_short: Aramaic Documents from Ancient Bactria (Khalili), Akhvamazda letters + C1/C4
item_015.ru_found: I found no Russian translation of any ADAB document, either in full or in excerpt. Russian scholars cite the corpus only by siglum or paraphrase it. (1) M. M. Kholod, "Империя Александра Великого: сатрапии и зависимые территории (ч. IV)", Проблемы истории, филологии, культуры 2025, n. 57: discusses C1 ("first year of Artaxerxes", the Bessus question) without translating it. (2) E. V. Rung, "Правовая система империи Ахеменидов в библейской традиции", Учёные записки Казанского ун-та 2025: cites Naveh & Shaked and paraphrases the term *ništāvana*, with no translated passage. (3) An academia.edu article, "К топонимии Хутталя" (author not verified), cites C4 (15 Sivan, year 7 of Alexander = 8 June 324 BCE) for one toponym. (4) A magisteria.ru lecture on the history of Syriac carries only an image caption ("Письмо Ахвамазды к Багаванту"). (5) Uzbek-language works mention the Akhvamazda–Bagavant correspondence (TSUOS 2018 conference volume, Termiz 2025, ZiyoNET), and the TSUOS volume reports that G. A. Koshelenko analysed the documents; I could not trace that Koshelenko work, and I saw no translations in these works. Searches run: about 15 CyberLeninka API queries (Ахвамазда, Багавант, арамейские документы Бактрии, Naveh Shaked, Khalili Bactria, among others); RSL full-text search ("Ахвамазда": 0 hits); Russian Wikipedia API (no article on the corpus; "Ахвамазда" and "Багавант": 0 hits); and 5 Russian Google queries before a CAPTCHA blocked further searches.
item_015.en_found: Full: J. Naveh & S. Shaked, Aramaic Documents from Ancient Bactria (Fourth Century BCE) from the Khalili Collections (London: Khalili Family Trust / Khalili Collections, 2012; 294 pp.; ISBN 978-1-874780-74-8). It gives the Aramaic text with English translation, introduction, commentary and glossary (khalilicollections.org/portfolio/aramaic-documents-from-ancient-bactria-fourth-century-bce/; reviewed in JAOS 136.3, DOI 10.7817/jameroriesoci.136.3.0629). The publisher offers the PDF free of charge after registration. The per-object pages at khalilicollections.org give English summaries only; for example the Akhvamazda-to-Bagavant letter catalogued as IA5 corresponds to ADAB A6. Partial or secondary English treatments: Lemaire 2010 (A9 revisited); Tavernier 2017; Daniels 2020; Gzella 2021 (Wiley Companion to the Achaemenid Persian Empire); Folmer 2023 (the Aramaic of the Akhvamazda letters). It is plausible, but I did not verify, that Kuhrt's The Persian Empire (2007) includes letters from the preliminary publication.
item_015.other_found: French: S. Shaked, Le satrape de Bactriane et son gouverneur. Documents araméens du IVe s. avant notre ère provenant de Bactriane (Persika 4; Paris: De Boccard, 2004; 62 pp.; Collège de France lectures of May 2003). This preliminary study presents the archive and probably renders selected letters in French; I did not verify how much it translates. Uzbek: the corpus is discussed in Uzbek scholarship, but I saw no translations. I found no German, Italian or Spanish translation; German is not verified (the TUAT Neue Folge letter volumes were not checked).
item_015.source_text: There is no public-domain or openly licensed text. The only complete edition is Naveh & Shaked 2012, in copyright (© Khalili Family Trust / Khalili Collections, all rights reserved). It can be downloaded as a free PDF after registration at khalilicollections.org, and the collection's object pages carry photographs, but these are also rights-reserved. A9 is re-edited by Lemaire 2010, also in copyright. Practical route: translate from the Naveh & Shaked readings, cite ADAB numbers, and publish without reproducing their transcription or photographs. Alternatively, ask the Khalili Collections for permission to reprint the Aramaic text and images.
item_015.research_yield: Articles possible from this unit: C1 ('year 1 of Artaxerxes') and the Bessus question; C4 ('year 7 of Alexander') and Macedonian rule in Bactria in 324 BCE, read against Arrian and Curtius; Akhvamazda–Bagavant chancery practice compared with the Arshama letters; Iranian names and toponyms; Russian terms for Achaemenid administration.
item_015.recommendation: Keep, with priority raised from 3 to 4: the Russian gap is confirmed, the corpus is small, and it bears directly on the editor's Alexander research. A full English translation exists, and Imperial Aramaic needs an outside Aramaist to check the work. Best first unit: the eight Akhvamazda–Bagavant letters (in the A series) plus C1 and C4. Note that the Alexander-dated text is the account C4, not a letter.

item_016.title_short: Anon., Demotic Magical Papyrus of London and Leiden (PDM/PGM xiv = GEMF 16), cols. i–v
item_016.ru_found: I found no full or scholarly Russian translation. What exists: (1) An anonymous Russian popular article about the "Лейденский/Лондонский медицинский папирус", probably copied from an older printed article (OCR hyphenation). It was reposted on VK in the group "Храм Сехмет / Древний Египет" on 22 Nov 2015 (https://vk.com/topic-36402672_33328727). It gives a Russian summary of all columns and translated excerpts of the medical and magical recipes: recto col. XIX (the spell against a love-potion, dog bite, bone stuck in the throat), col. XX (scorpion sting), and verso cols. IV, V, VIII–XI and XX. The translation was probably made from Griffith & Thompson's English; I could not trace the original source. (2) Quotations in the Russian translation of Stratton-Kent / Rankine / Agrippa, «В мире духов и демонов» (2022, archive.org 20220903_20220903_1553), citing the "Лейденский папирус" by column. (3) A Scribd fragment "Греческие магические папирусы. Перевод 34%/52%" (uploader tancuram136, July 2025, about 151 words): an amateur rendering of the start of Betz's GMPT, with no PDM text. Occultism.ru (Тэлим) offers summaries only and states there is no full Russian translation of the corpus; Russian texts online are third-hand renderings of Betz's English. Anna Blaze's PGM excerpts (greek.thesaurusdeorum.com) and a-guru.com contain no PDM. Searches with no result: CyberLeninka API (6 queries, incl. «демотический магический папирус», «Лейденский папирус магический», «Лондонско-Лейденский папирус», «PDM xiv»), ru.wikipedia (which mentions the papyrus only in «Демотическое письмо»), egyptology.ru thematic bibliographies (texts, religion, language: no PDM xiv), and archive.org Russian full text. ВДИ has only Францов on Leiden I 384, which is a different papyrus. The proposed pilot unit (cols. i–v, vessel/lamp divination) has no Russian translation at all.
item_016.en_found: There are three complete English translations. (1) F. Ll. Griffith & H. Thompson, The Demotic Magical Papyrus of London and Leiden, 3 vols (London/Oxford 1904, 1905, 1909); public domain. On archive.org as demoticmagicalpa01grifuoft and b29003519_0001; also on sacred-texts.com/egy/dmp; Dover reprint as "The Leyden Papyrus: An Egyptian Magical Book" (1974). (2) Janet H. Johnson, translation of PDM xiv 1–1227 in H. D. Betz (ed.), The Greek Magical Papyri in Translation (Chicago 1986; 2nd ed. 1992), with the Greek parts translated by Grese. (3) New and missed by the sweep: GEMF 16 in C. A. Faraone & S. Torallas Tovar (eds.), Greek and Egyptian Magical Formularies: Text and Translation, vol. I (California Classical Studies 9, Berkeley 2022). This is a full re-edition with facing English translation, re-edited by Jacco Dieleman with E. Love, M. Escolano-Poveda, A. Singer and K. Dosoo. It is open access via eScholarship. Partial: J. Dieleman, Priests, Tongues, and Rites (Brill 2005), which translates many passages.
item_016.other_found: The GEMF 16 introduction (2022) lists the translations, and I confirmed several on archive.org. German: J. F. Quack, «Demotische magische und divinatorische Texte», TUAT NF 4 (2008) 331–385, with PDM xiv selections at pp. 333–350; G. Roeder, Der Ausklang der ägyptischen Religion (Artemis, Zürich 1961) 185–213, Text B7 «Der demotische Zauberpapyrus in London und Leiden» (selections); J. J. Hess, Der gnostische Papyrus von London (1892), with col. 1 only; Preisendanz, PGM XIV (Greek parts only). French: F. Lexa, La magie dans l'Égypte antique II (1925) 122–150, «Le grimoire démotique de Londres et de Leyde». It gives 32 extracts, including the pilot-unit passages 3/5–35, 4/1–22 and 6/1–8/11, as well as 16/1–30 and 17–29; on archive.org. Spanish: Calvo Martínez & Sánchez Romero, Textos de magia en papiros griegos (Gredos 1987) 311–312 (Greek parts only). Italian: E. Bresciani, «I grandi testi magici demotici» (1987), probably excerpts (not checked). The Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (Vittmann) has the Demotic text; whether it includes a German translation is not checked. Result: partial in French and German; nothing complete outside English.
item_016.source_text: Best public-domain source: Griffith & Thompson 1904–09 (hand-copy facsimile, transliteration, English translation, glossary). Griffith died in 1934 and Thompson in 1944, so it is public domain worldwide. Archive.org: demoticmagicalpa01grifuoft, b29003519_0001, the-demotic-magical-papyrus-of-london-and-leiden-v.-1 / v.-2. The first editions are also public domain (Leemans 1839 for Leiden I 383; Hess 1892 for BM EA 10070). The standard modern edition is GEMF 16 (Faraone & Torallas Tovar 2022, California Classical Studies 9). It is free online but © 2022 the editors; I found no Creative Commons statement in the text, so treat it as in copyright. Betz/Johnson GMPT (U. Chicago Press 1986/1992) is in copyright. Caveat: the source is Demotic (only about 27 Greek lines, plus Old Coptic glosses), not Greek or Latin.
item_016.research_yield: Russian articles possible on: Nectanebo's lekanomancy in the Alexander Romance read against the PDM xiv bowl/lamp rites with a boy medium (the editor's own field); the Theban Magical Library; Greek–Egyptian bilingualism, cipher and Old Coptic glosses; medical-magical recipes.
item_016.recommendation: Downgrade, and keep only as a Russian-gap item: English is covered three times, most recently by the open-access GEMF 16 (2022), and there are partial French and German versions. The source is Demotic, outside the editor's Greek/Latin competence and weak for LLMs, so any Russian version would rely heavily on the English translations. If pursued, start with cols. i–v (vessel divination) with an Egyptologist reviewer, framed through the Nectanebo/Alexander Romance link.

item_017.title_short: Edfu temple inscriptions, Edfou I (one naos chapel)
item_017.ru_found: No full or partial Russian translation of any Edfou volume, and nothing at all for Edfou I. Scattered passage translations exist: K.F. Karlova, "Змееборческий миф как часть государственной идеологии в греко-римском Египте" (Индоевропейское языкознание и классическая филология, 2022; CyberLeninka) translates short passages from Edfou VI 130, VI 179, VII 200, III 287 and IV 59. Korostovtsev, "Религия древнего Египта" (1976), is cited by ru.wikipedia and probably quotes Edfu myth texts, but I could not check its contents. ru.wikipedia ("Храм Эдфу") says the complete translation is being done only by the German Edfu-Projekt. Searches run: CyberLeninka API ("Эдфу", "в Эдфу", "храма в Эдфу", "Эдфуского храма", "Гор Бехдетский", "храм Хора Эдфу перевод", "святилище храма Эдфу", "ритуальные сцены птолемеевских храмов", "птолемеевские храмовые надписи"), egyptology.ru thematic and personal bibliographies (Матье, Коростовцев, Тураев, Ладынин; the texts section has no Edfu entry), ru.wikipedia search. WebSearch was unavailable (budget used up), so elibrary.ru and RSL were not checked.
item_017.en_found: Partial and scattered. Most relevant to the pilot unit: M.E.A. Ibrahim, "The Chapel of the Throne of Re of Edfu" (Bibliotheca Aegyptiaca 16, Brussels: FERE, 1975, 71 pp. + pls; reviewed by Murnane, JNES 1980). This is an English monograph on one of the Edfou I chapels, so the proposed unit is already covered for that chapel. Other English work: Blackman & Fairman, "The Myth of Horus at Edfu" (JEA 1942–44; on archive.org), and Fairman, "The Triumph of Horus" (1974), both on Edfou VI. Reymond, "Mythical Origin of the Egyptian Temple" (1969, Edfou VI). Kurth, "The Temple of Edfu: A Guide by an Ancient Egyptian Priest" (AUC 2004, translated selections). P. Wilson, "A Ptolemaic Lexikon" (1997), with many translated phrases. Finnestad, "Image of the World and Symbol of the Creator" (1985). Searches: Open Library ("Edfu", "chapel Edfu", "naos Edfu"), Crossref, archive.org, DNB SRU.
item_017.other_found: This refutes the sweep's claim that "Edfou I–V are largely untranslated in any language". GERMAN complete translations (Kurth et al., Die Inschriften des Tempels von Edfu, Abt. I Übersetzungen; verified in the DNB catalogue): Edfou VIII (Bd 1, 1998), VII (Bd 2, 2004), VI (Bd 3, 2014), V (Bd 4.1, 2019, 848 pp.; Index Bd 4.2, 2020), IV (Bd 5.1, 2021, and Bd 5.2, 2024, covering pp. 202–393). Only Edfou I–III have no complete translation. For Edfou I in particular: W. Waitkus, "Die kulttopographische Inschrift am Sanktuar des Tempels von Edfu" (Begleitheft 7, PeWe 2014, complete translation), and C. Leitz, "Die Gaumonographien in Edfu und ihre Papyrusvarianten" (2014), cover the sanctuary's geographical texts. Kurth, "Treffpunkt der Götter" (1994/1998), gives German selections. FRENCH partial studies: Alliot, "Le culte d'Horus à Edfou" (BdE 20, 1949–54; on archive.org); Cauville, "La théologie d'Osiris à Edfou" (BdE 91, 1983) and "Essai sur la théologie du temple d'Horus à Edfou" (BdE 102, 1987), both likely covering the naos chapels; Labrique, "Stylistique et théologie à Edfou" (OLA 51, 1992); Germond (1986); Baum, "Le temple d'Edfou" (2007); Meeks, "Le grand texte des donations" (1972, Edfou VII).
item_017.source_text: Best source: Le temple d'Edfou I, 2nd edition (Rochemonteix/Chassinat, revised by S. Cauville and D. Devauchelle; IFAO, MMAF 10, 4 fascicles, 1984–87). IFAO offers it as a free PDF (https://www.ifao.egnet.net/uploads/publications/enligne/MMAF010.pdf, 106 MB; verified HTTP 200) under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, as part of its open "Bibliothèque numérique". The other volumes are free too (Edfou II = MMAF011.pdf; Edfou III–XV = MMAF020–032). The first edition of Edfou I (1892–97) and Chassinat's original volumes (Chassinat died 1948) are public domain in the EU. The standard revised 2nd edition is in copyright but openly licensed for non-commercial use. Caveat: the PDF shows typeset hieroglyphs only, with no machine-readable text or transliteration. The Edfu-Explorer database covers only Edfou V–VIII.
item_017.research_yield: A first Russian translation of an Edfou I chapel would support articles on Ptolemaic priestly theology of the naos, cult topography, and royal ideology under the Ptolemies. The sanctuary also holds the naos of Nectanebo II, a link to the Alexander Romance. It would add little internationally beyond Russian-language access.
item_017.recommendation: Drop or defer. Edfou IV–V now have complete German translations, the Chapel of the Throne of Re has an English monograph (Ibrahim 1975), and Ptolemaic hieroglyphs read from page images are beyond reliable LLM reading and outside the editor's Greek/Latin validation range. If kept, the only sensible unit is a Russian-first translation of an Edfou I chapel not covered by Ibrahim, Cauville or Waitkus/Leitz, made from IFAO MMAF010 with an Egyptologist co-editor.

item_018.title_short: Quodvultdeus, Liber promissionum et praedictorum Dei (Part III end + Dimidium temporis)
item_018.ru_found: I found no full or partial Russian translation, but there are a few indirect excerpts. ekzeget.ru carries short Russian passages headed "Книга обетований и предсказаний Бога" with ACCS-style references (for example Gen 40:3 = Lib. prom. 1.28.9, SC 101:240; also Gen 39:22, 42, 46:30, 2:24). These look like the Russian version of the ACCS (Библейские комментарии отцов Церкви…, Герменевтика), so they are second-hand from English and all from Part I. That attribution is likely but unconfirmed, because ekzeget blocks bots. Russian Wikipedia and two encyclopaedia articles list no Russian translation in their bibliographies: Pravenc "КВОДВУЛЬТДЕУС" (pravenc.ru/text/1684079.html) and Древо "Кводвультдей Карфагенский" (drevo-info.ru/articles/7244). The same holds for CyberLeninka (searched under "Кводвультдей", "Кводвультдеус" and "Quodvultdeus"). Урбанович (Вестник ПСТГУ V, 2016) uses no Russian translation. "Signum crucis in vestibus" (Люди и тексты, 2014) only paraphrases one passage in Russian and gives the Latin in a footnote. Azbyka has only a saint's Life. Bing searches in Russian found nothing more, including searches for the Caelestis-temple passage.
item_018.en_found: There is no complete English translation. D. Eastman's bibliography (JACB 9.1, 2024; OpenBU hdl 2144/51257) lists only Braun's French for this work and Finn ACW 60 (2004, creedal homilies only). English Wikipedia, Crossref and Open Library also show no English version. Excerpts do exist. (1) The Oxford Cult of Saints database has two passages translated by R. Wiśniewski (2015): E00975 = Dimidium temporis 5.7 and E00997 = Dimidium temporis 6.81, the Florus/Sossius episode at Naples. (2) ACCS (IVP) volumes contain scattered verse-linked excerpts: 1.3, 1.21.28, 1.28.40, 1.30.42, 1.32.44, 1.33–34, 2.35, 2.37.83, 3.29 and 3.39.46 (Isa 11:6). (3) F. Gumerlock reported, as of 2018, that he had translated Quodvultdeus' comments on Rev 11 and Rev 20 (Dimidium temporis); these were unpublished then and I have not confirmed later publication. Van Slyke's book (2003) and Vopřada's (Brill 2019/20) are studies, not translations. Hermetica II (2018) has a Quodvultdeus chapter, apparently from another work.
item_018.other_found: French: R. Braun, Livre des promesses et des prédictions de Dieu, SC 101–102 (Cerf 1964), with the Latin text. Italian: Promesse e predizioni di Dio (Città Nuova 1989; Open Library credits A. V. Nazzaro); L. Dattrino, Il libro delle promesse e delle predizioni di Dio (LEV 2002, Latin–Italian). German: only Franses' study (1920), no translation. Spanish: none found; González Salinero 2002 is a study. French excerpts of the Caelestis passage appear in the scholarship (Persée, Antiquités africaines 34, 1998).
item_018.source_text: Public domain: Migne PL 51, cols. 733–858 (under Prosper, 1846). The Latin Wikisource transcription comes from the Zurich Corpus Corporum TEI (Roelli 2013): https://la.wikisource.org/wiki/De_promissionibus_et_praedictionibus_Dei. A Documenta Catholica Omnia PDF also exists. The PL text keeps Braun's chapter and paragraph numbering, for example III.38.44 for Caelestis. It runs to about 52k words: Part III ≈8.2k (40 chapters), Dimidium temporis ≈6.5k (20 chapters), Gloria ≈1.6k (14 chapters in PL). The standard critical editions, Braun CCSL 60 (Brepols 1976) and SC 101–102 (Cerf 1964), are in copyright. Translate from PL and check variants against Braun without reproducing his text.
item_018.research_yield: Possible articles: the Caelestis temple dedicated by Aurelius (III.38.44); Serapeum and Stilicho marvels; Gog/Magog as Goths, Moors, Getae and Massagetae, and Vandal-Arian apocalyptic; Carthage portent of 434; a Neapolitan exile's testimony; comparison with De civitate Dei; Delmulle's authorship challenge (RBén 2018).
item_018.recommendation: Keep at top priority: there is no full or partial translation in Russian or English, only scattered excerpts. Fix the pilot unit, because Part III has only 40 chapters and "44" is the paragraph of the Caelestis passage, not a chapter. The best first unit is Part III chs. 33–40 (including ch. 38 §§41–44) plus the whole Dimidium temporis, about 9.5–10k words; adding Gloria sanctorum brings it to about 11k.

item_019.title_short: Ambrosiaster, Quaestiones Veteris et Novi Testamenti (Q.114 Adversus paganos + Q.115 De fato)
item_019.ru_found:
I found no Russian translation of the work, of any whole quaestio, or of Q.114 or Q.115. Russian scholarship only quotes single sentences.

What I checked (the WebSearch budget was used up, so I queried site and catalogue endpoints directly):
- azbyka.ru/otechnik/Amvrosiast/: the Voprosy page has only a PDF of Souter's Latin text (Johnson reprint, 1963), marked "(лат.)". The azbyka Augustine index has no such work, not even among the spuria.
- ru.wikipedia "Амброзиастер" (raw wikitext): no Russian translation is cited. The article itself renders one line in Russian, taken from Lunn-Rockliffe's book ("кто ты такой, чтобы запрещать брак?…"). The "Митраизм" article paraphrases a few words of the Q.114 Mithraic passage.
- CyberLeninka API, queries Амвросиаст, Амброзиастер, «Амвросиаста вопросы», «Против язычников Амвросиаст», Псевдо-Августин, Quaestiones Veteris…: nothing. The only hits are articles that cite the text:
  - М. А. Ведешкин, «Сенаторы-вероотступники» (Индоевропейское языкознание и классическая филология, 2024): Latin plus a Russian paraphrase of Q.114.13.
  - А. В. Данилов (Теологический вестник Смоленской ДС, 2020): one sentence in Latin with a paraphrase.
- MDA journals (Богословский вестник, Метафраст), searched with Амвросиаст, Амброзиастер, «Вопросы Ветхого и Нового Завета», Псевдо-Августин, «О судьбе»: only the studies on the Pauline commentary by свящ. А. Лысевич and еп. Феодорит (Тихонов), 2019–2022, and Лысевич's dissertation (2021). None translates the Quaestiones.
- The pre-revolutionary Kiev Augustine series does not include the work.
- Not checked: elibrary, the RSL catalogue (JavaScript only), and the Russian ACCS Old Testament volumes, which may carry short excerpts.
item_019.en_found:
There is a complete English translation, but it is self-published and was not peer-reviewed:
- John Litteral, "Questions on the Old and New Testaments by Ambrosiaster: English Translation" (CreateSpace, 2018; 452 pp.; ISBN 9781723562723). The Google Books listing says "revised translation in 2026".
- It is freely available on archive.org (ambrosiaster-questions-and-answers-on-the-old-and-new-testaments).
- It is based on PL 35, not on Souter's CSEL text. Both recensions are rearranged by biblical order, with "Polemic" and "Miscellaneous" sections.
- I read the OCR text (about 180k words). It contains "QUESTION 114. AGAINST THE PAGANS", including the Mithraic initiation passage, and "QUESTION 115. CONCERNING FATE", plus Q.101 (Roman deacons), Q.102 (Against Novatian), Q.120 and others. The English is fluent but may be machine-assisted.

So the proposed pilot unit already exists in English. Scholarly English exists only as excerpts, for example the quotations in Lunn-Rockliffe, Ambrosiaster's Political Theology (OUP 2007). The Mithraic passage is often translated in studies of Mithraism. I could not verify whether D. G. Hunter translated Q.127 in full.
item_019.other_found:
The proposed unit has scholarly translations in French and German:
- French: Marie-Pierre Bussières, "Ambrosiaster. Contre les païens (Question 114) et Sur le destin (Question 115)", Sources Chrétiennes 512 (Cerf, 2007; 273 pp.). It gives a revised Latin text, translation and commentary. It grew out of her thesis "Les traités contre les païens et sur le destin de l'Ambrosiaster" (2000).
- German: Dietrich Traugott von Queis, "Ambrosiaster: Quaestiones Veteris et Novi Testamenti. Quaestio 115: De fato. Einleitung, Text, Übersetzung, Kommentar", Basel doctoral thesis, 1972 (218 pp.). Confirmed in Open Library edition records.
- I found no complete scholarly translation in any language.
- The 19th-century French Augustine translations online (bibliotheque-monastique.ch, the Raulx corpus) do not include the work.
- Italian: Città Nuova has Ambrosiaster's Pauline commentaries and Matthew fragments, but no Quaestiones turned up. Spanish: none found. Neither was checked exhaustively.
item_019.source_text:
- Best public-domain text: A. Souter (ed.), Pseudo-Augustini Quaestiones Veteris et Novi Testamenti CXXVII, CSEL 50 (Vienna/Leipzig: Tempsky/Freytag, 1908). It covers the 127-question recension plus an appendix of selected questions from the 150-question recension.
  - Scan: https://archive.org/details/pseudoaugustini00soutgoog
  - Reprints: Johnson 1963 (a PDF is hosted on azbyka) and ÖAW 2013.
- Alternative public-domain text: PL 35, cols. 2213–2416 (Maurist text), on Documenta Catholica Omnia and Corpus Corporum.
- Copyright: Souter's CSEL 50 is still the standard complete edition and is out of copyright. Bussières' revised text of Q.114–115 in SC 512 (2007) is in copyright; use it only as a reference, with the translation made from Souter.
item_019.research_yield: Q.114 on late-Roman paganism, apostate senators and Mithraic initiation; Q.115 Christian anti-astrology (vs Firmicus, Augustine); Q.101 Roman deacons under Damasus; Ambrosiaster–Jerome rivalry; recensions; first Russian annotated edition.
item_019.recommendation: Keep, because no Russian translation exists, but drop the "untranslated" claim: the whole work is in English (Litteral, free online) and Q.114–115 also have scholarly French (SC 512) and German (von Queis) versions. Q.114+115 works as a Russian first, with SC 512 for cross-checking; Q.101+102 would be newer outside English.

item_020.title_short: Origen, Homiliae in Psalmos (Cod. Monac. gr. 314; pilot: 2 hom. Ps 15 + 4 hom. Ps 76)
item_020.ru_found:
The claim of no Russian translation is REFUTED. Anna Grünert has published 7 of the 29 homilies, translated from the Greek of GCS NF 19 with introductions and commentary, in «Библия и христианская древность» (МДА; open-access PDFs at ojs.patristic.ru):
- Беседы I–II на Пс. 36, ч. 1: 2021, № 3(11), pp. 71–124, DOI 10.31802/BCA.2021.11.3.002 (/article/view/161).
- Беседы III–IV на Пс. 36, ч. 2: 2022, № 2(14), pp. 57–105, DOI 10.31802/bca.2022.14.2.002 (/view/224).
- Беседа на Пс. 74: 2024, № 4(24) (issued Jan 2025), pp. 88–106, DOI 10.31802/bca.2024.24.4.003 (/view/377).
- Беседа на Пс. 81: 2025, № 1(25), pp. 55–74, DOI 10.31802/bca.2025.25.1.002 (/view/399).
- Беседа на Пс. 75: 2025, № 3(27), pp. 58–78 (/view/432).
In «Богослов» (2025, DOI 10.62847/bogoslov.2025.13.12.003), Grünert says she plans a Russian translation of ALL the Psalm homilies as a bilingual edition. The proposed pilot unit (Ps 15 hom. 1–2; Ps 76 hom. 1–4) is not yet in Russian: the journal's site search and the current issue, № 3(27) 2025, show nothing else. Nothing further turned up in pravenc.ru (Ориген article, vol. 53), azbyka.ru (no Psalm homilies) or Crossref (10+ Russian queries).
item_020.en_found: Joseph W. Trigg (trans.), Origen: Homilies on the Psalms. Codex Monacensis Graecus 314, Fathers of the Church 141, CUA Press, 15 Jan 2021 (sometimes cited as 2020), 480 pp., ISBN 9780813233192, DOI 10.2307/j.ctv1g4rv8m. It covers all 29 homilies; the per-homily chapter DOIs run from Hom. 1 on Ps 15 to the homily on Ps 81, including Ps 76 hom. 1–4. Separately, FOTC also published Rufinus' Latin Homilies on Psalms 36–38 (CUA 2023, DOI 10.2307/jj.3485521).
item_020.other_found:
ITALIAN, full: L. Perrone (ed. and trans.), Origene, Omelie sui Salmi 1–2, Opere di Origene 9/3a–3b, Città Nuova 2021, 600 + 608 pp., revised Greek text facing, ISBN 9788831195379 / 9788831195386 (ibs.it).
GERMAN: a translation by the Origenes-Forschungsstelle in Münster is in preparation (per Grünert 2025).
FRENCH: a Sources Chrétiennes bilingual edition is in preparation (per Grünert 2025); the SC catalogue site could not be reached.
SPANISH: none found in the Ciudad Nueva listings (todostuslibros).
Rufinus' Latin of Ps 36–38 already has translations: SC 411 (1995, French) and Prinzivalli (Nardini 1991, Italian).
item_020.source_text: The standard edition is L. Perrone et al., Die neuen Psalmenhomilien, GCS NF 19 (De Gruyter 2015). It is in copyright and does not appear to be open access. Perrone's revised Greek text (Città Nuova 2021) is also in copyright. The only public-domain witness of the full Greek is the 12th-century manuscript itself, BSB Cod.graec. 314. I could not check how the MDZ digitization is licensed. Public-domain fallbacks cover only fragments: the catena excerpts in PG 12.1053–1685 and PG 17.105–150, and Rufinus' Latin of Ps 36 (PG 12). A complete text would need rights clearance or a fresh transcription of the manuscript.
item_020.research_yield: Possible articles: the pilot unit's Hexaplaric readings and Jewish exegesis; Origen's late preaching style; Greek against Rufinus for Ps 36. But Perrone's school, Trigg and Grünert have already mapped the field, so yield is moderate. The Russian niche is being actively filled.
item_020.recommendation: Drop. English and Italian are complete, French and German are in preparation, and 7 homilies are already in Russian, with the translator planning a full bilingual edition. The standard text is also in copyright. The only route left is collaborating with A. Grünert on the untranslated homilies (e.g. the four on Ps 76 or the nine on Ps 77), not a separate first translation.

item_021.title_short: Facundus of Hermiane, Pro defensione trium capitulorum (+ Contra Mocianum, Epistula fidei catholicae)
item_021.ru_found: I found no Russian translation of any of the three works, whole or in part. Searches run: Yahoo/Bing for «Факунд Гермианский перевод», «Факунд» «трех глав» перевод с латинского, «Факунд против Муциана», and «Факунд» with site:vostlit.info, ancientrome.ru, simposium.ru and karpov.ru (zero hits). I also ran 5 queries through the CyberLeninka API («Факунд», «Факунда Гермианского», «Facundus Hermiane», «Против Муциана Факунд», «Три главы Факунд перевод»), searched the azbyka.ru otechnik library (no author entry for Facundus), checked pravenc.ru via Bing (no ПЭ article indexed) and read ru.wikipedia. The only Russian work devoted to the text is a study, not a translation: А. П. Доброклонский, «Сочинение Факунда, епископа Гермианского: В защиту трех глав (pro defensione trium capitulorum). Ист.-крит. исслед. из эпохи V-го Вселенского собора», Москва: тип. М. Н. Лаврова, 1880, 312 pp. (his master's dissertation). Azbyka has it as a scan only, and the PDF needs a login: https://azbyka.ru/otechnik/Aleksandr_Dobroklonskij/sochinenie-fakunda-episkopa-germianskogo-v-zashhitu-treh-glav/. It probably contains Russian paraphrases and translated quotations, but I could not check this. Secondary literature only touches the text: М. В. Грацианский, «Св. Император Юстиниан и спор о Трёх Главах (540–553)», Вестник ПСТГУ, Сер. 1, 2007; прот. Н. Афанасьев, «Ива Эдесский и его время» (СФИ, 2018). Encyclopedia entries (ЭСБЕ, ru.wikipedia) mention no translation.
item_021.en_found: No published English translation turned up: nothing in TTH, FOTC, ACW or CCEL. en.wikipedia lists only PL and the SC French edition; its English 'tr.' is Hefele's History of the Councils, which paraphrases the work rather than translating it. I also found no English version of Contra Mocianum or the Epistula. The finding that refutes the colleague's 'none': an anonymous, unpublished English translation on Scribd, 'TRANSLATING Pro Defensione Trium Capitulorum_ (1)', uploaded by user 'yutacarlos2', 224 pages. Its embedded text opens with 'Book One, Chapter One: That Justinian, in his confession of faith, rightly professed that one of the Trinity was crucified…' and continues into Chapter Two: https://www.scribd.com/document/1029152634/TRANSLATING-Pro-Defensione-Trium-Capitulorum-1. There is no translator name, date or method note, and I could not see beyond Book I. At 224 pages it could be a draft of most or all of the 12 books, possibly made with machine help. It is not a scholarly publication, but check it before claiming an English 'first'. The aiforbible.com 'Defence of the Three Chapters' page is only a catalogue card, not a translation. Searches: Brave, plus Bing (x7) with queries on English translation / Three Chapters / Pro defensione excerpts / TTH, FOTC, ACW / Contra Mocianum / Against Mocianus / Liverpool, tertullian.org.
item_021.other_found: French, complete: Anne Fraïsse-Bétoulières (introduction, translation, notes), Latin text by J.-M. Clément and R. Vander Plaetse, Facundus d'Hermiane, Défense des Trois Chapitres (À Justinien), Sources Chrétiennes 471, 478, 479, 484, 499, Paris: Cerf 2002–2006. Confirmed by the Brill RPP entry and Wikipedia; SC 479 covers Livres VIII–X. Italian: Facondo di Ermiane, Difesa dei tre capitoli, 2 vols, introduction, translation and notes by Sara Petri, Città Nuova, Testi patristici, 2007 (vol. 2: 344 pp., ISBN 9788831181945). Whether it includes Contra Mocianum and the Epistula is unverified. German and Spanish: none found.
item_021.source_text: The public-domain text is Migne, PL 67 (1848; repr. 1865), cols 527–878: Pro defensione cols 527–852, Contra Mocianum c. 853–868, Epistula fidei catholicae c. 867–878. The 12 books are online at la.wikisource (https://la.wikisource.org/wiki/Pro_defensione_trium_capitulorum, encoded from PL 67 by Corpus Corporum, Zurich) and at Corpus Corporum (mlat.uzh.ch). The editio princeps by J. Sirmond (Paris 1629) is on archive.org (e.g. bub_gb_sEnGpghxQRgC). The standard critical edition is Clément & Vander Plaetse, CCSL 90A (Brepols 1974), in copyright. Its text is reprinted with the French translation in SC (Cerf 2002–06), also in copyright. Plan: translate from PL 67 and collate against CCSL 90A for readings.
item_021.research_yield: Articles possible: Facundus's African case against imperial power in dogma (Book XII); his Latin versions of Theodore of Mopsuestia fragments, Ibas's letter and the Chalcedonian acts; African resistance to Vigilius and the Fifth Council; and how Russian scholarship received him, from Dobroklonsky (1880) to Bolotov.
item_021.recommendation: Keep: no Russian translation exists, and none is published in English. The unpublished Scribd English draft should be checked before the project claims an English 'first'. Best first unit: Liber contra Mocianum (about 7–8k words, self-contained), then Book XII on imperial authority.

item_022.title_short: Zeno of Verona, Tractatus (Easter/neophyte dossier incl. zodiac sermon I.38)
item_022.ru_found:
Five complete tractates out of 93 are in Russian. None of them is in the proposed pilot dossier.
(1) Anonymous, Христианское чтение 1838, pp. 13-20: «О том, как должно понимать слова Апостола: егда предаст царство Богу и Отцу (1 Кор 15:24)».
(2-4) Anonymous, Христианское чтение 1843, ч. II, pp. 349-368, 369-377, 378-387: «О надежде, вере и любви» (PL I.2), «Об Иове», «О пророке Ионе».
All four are reprinted on azbyka.ru/otechnik/Zenon_Veronskij/, on predanie.ru/book/67541-tvoreniya/ and as the coollib/flibusta fb2 «Творения» (coollib b/841732, 3 pieces). Flibusta also lists a second «Творения» file (b/879119) that I could not open; it is probably a duplicate.
(5) NEW, missed by the sweep: протодиакон Владимир Василик, «Слово об алчности», pravoslavie.ru/143430.html, 15.12.2021. It is a full translation of one De avaritia sermon (PL I.10, the one that ends praising the congregation's almsgiving), made from Löfstedt CCSL 22 and presented as «впервые переведенная».
Pravenc «Зинон» (А.Р. Фокин, ПЭ т. 20, 2009) says there was no Russian study or translation of Zeno.
Searched with no further finds: CyberLeninka API (Зенон/Зинон Веронский and declensions; hits only mention Zeno, e.g. ХЧ 2024 Сидорова and the 2023 astrology article, which paraphrase without translating); Bing/DDG queries on зодиак, пасхальные проповеди/неофиты, Фокин, Василик, Христианское чтение 1838/1843, Зинона Веронийского; ru.wikipedia; pravoslavie.press.
No Russian translation of the zodiac sermon (Löfstedt I.38), the invitationes ad fontem, the ad neophytos addresses or the De Pascha cycle was found.
Caveat: Google, Yandex and elibrary could not be queried (captcha), so a journal excerpt could have been missed.
item_022.en_found:
The sweep's 'partial' is REFUTED.
(1) Updated Works, updatedworks.com/zeno-of-verona/tractatus/ (Patrologia Latina vol. 11 project, © 2026, all rights reserved). This is a complete English translation of all tractates in the PL/Ballerini order: Book 1 nos. 1-16 and Book 2 nos. 1-77, including the zodiac sermon (PL II.43 = Löfstedt I.38) and all the Invitations to the Font, To the Neophytes, Easter, Exodus and Daniel pieces. It runs to about 65k words and the page says 'You just read this work in full'. It is unsigned and has no named translator ('a fresh English translation ... reviewed for fidelity'), so it is evidently a mass, probably AI-assisted, translation of PL rather than a scholarly one.
(2) G.P. Jeanes, The Day Has Come! Easter and Baptism in Zeno of Verona (Alcuin Club Collections 73, Liturgical Press 1995, 282 pp.). It translates the Easter sermons, 'most for the first time'. The zodiac sermon is an Easter neophyte address and is very likely included, but I did not see the table of contents.
(3) A.S. Jacobs: Tract. II.8 De nativitate Domini, andrewjacobs.org, CC BY-NC 4.0.
(4) Excerpts in Hamman, Baptism: Ancient Liturgies and Patristic Texts (1967), and in Carroll, Preaching the Word (1984). I saw these only in archive.org metadata and did not verify the contents.
item_022.other_found:
German, full: A. Bigelmair, Des hl. Zeno von Verona Traktate, BKV² vol. 10 (Kösel, München 1934; archive.org traktateausdemla0010zeno, lending only). Bigelmair died in 1962, so this is in copyright until 2033. An earlier German translation (Kempten 1877) is mentioned by pravoslavie.press.
Italian, full: Le opere di S. Zenone volgarizzate (Verona 1784); I sermoni (Verona 1840); G. Banterle, I discorsi (Scrittori dell'area santambrosiana, Milano/Roma 1987; archive.org idiscorsi0000zeno); Banterle, revised by R. Ravazzolo, Trattati (Città Nuova, Roma 2008).
I found no French or Spanish translation.
item_022.source_text:
Public domain: Ballerini, Sancti Zenonis episcopi Veronensis Sermones (Verona 1739; archive.org bub_gb_KjBcXqzUGYkC; Augsburg reprint 1758 bub_gb_aUjYbc2xCaQC), reprinted as PL 11 (1845) and also on archive.org. Giuliari's edition (Verona 1883/1900) is also public domain, but I did not locate a scan.
The standard edition is B. Löfstedt, Zenonis Veronensis Tractatus, CCSL 22 (Brepols 1971), which is in copyright. It renumbers the pieces in manuscript order (I.1-62, II.1-30; zodiac = I.38 = PL II.43). The plan should be to translate from PL, collate textual cruxes against Löfstedt and the Löfstedt Concordance (1975), give Löfstedt numbers alongside PL numbers, and not reproduce the CCSL text.
item_022.research_yield: Russian-first articles: Zeno's Christianised zodiac for neophytes and late-antique astrology; Apuleian, Virgilian and African prose style; the Easter vigil at Verona; anti-pagan rites; Russian reception of Zeno (Христианское чтение 1838/1843, Василик 2021). Also a methods article comparing an AI English version (Updated Works) with Jeanes.
item_022.recommendation: Keep, but only for the Russian track: drop any first-English claim, since Updated Works already has a full AI-style English version and Jeanes covers the Easter sermons. Best first unit: the untranslated paschal-neophyte dossier (the Ad neophytos addresses incl. the zodiac sermon Löfstedt I.38 = PL II.43, plus the invitationes ad fontem), c. 4-6k words, checked against Jeanes and Banterle.

item_023.title_short: Didymus the Blind, Commentary on Ecclesiastes (Tura), Eccl 1:1–2:14
item_023.ru_found: I found no full or partial Russian translation. The papyrus was only discovered in 1941, so no 19th-century or older Russian translation can exist. Excerpts do exist. (1) The Russian edition of the ACCS series: Библейские комментарии отцов Церкви и других авторов I–VIII вв. ВЗ. Т. IX: Притчи, Екклесиаст, Песнь Песней, edited by J. R. Wright, Russian edition by Д. С. Бирюков (Тверь: Герменевтика, 2012, 480 pp., translated from English, Greek and other languages). It contains dozens of short passages headed "Дидим Слепец. Комментарии на Екклесиаста". The same passages are reposted on bible.optina.ru and ekzeget.ru. For the proposed unit Eccl 1:1–2:14 I counted excerpts at 1:1, 1:2, 1:3, 1:4, 1:5, 2:4, 2:8, 2:9, 2:10, 2:11 and 2:14. Together they come to about 1,250 words, roughly 10% of the unit. (2) Т. М. Суворкина and Е. В. Афонасин, "Продик Кеосский. Фрагменты и свидетельства", Respublica Literaria, 2020 (cyberleninka). It translates the Prodicus testimony on Eccl 1:8b (P.Tura 16.11, CPF Prodicus 3T), a few lines long. (3) Archimandrite Sergius (Akimov), "Проблемы толкования и перевода Еккл. 1:1", Труды Минской духовной академии, 2020. It quotes two passages, taken from the 2012 ACCS volume. Negative checks: azbyka.ru lists only the 1870 ТКДА "Книга о Святом Духе" and К. Илюточкин's dissertation "Корпус Дидима Слепца…", which discusses the commentary but contains no translation. The Православная энциклопедия article "Дидим Слепец" cites only the 1870 De Spiritu Sancto translation. A CyberLeninka API search ("Дидим Слепец", 55 hits) found nothing beyond these items.
item_023.en_found: The claim that no English translation exists is REFUTED. Didymus the Blind – Commentary on Ecclesiastes: An Independent English Translation of the Surviving Greek Commentary, translated by Bishoy Marcus (Marcus Family Publishing, published 12 Sept 2026; 274 pp.; ISBN 978-1764957830; https://www.amazon.com/dp/1764957830). According to the publisher's description, it covers "all six published parts" of the commentary, Eccl 1:1 through 12:6d, with an introduction, notes and a concordance to the papyrus page numbers. It is not an academic edition: the translator is described as an Australian physician who writes children's books on saints and parables. Its scholarly quality is unverified, and no reviews were found. English excerpts also exist: J. Robert Wright (ed.), ACCS OT IX: Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, Song of Solomon (IVP, 2005); R. A. Layton, Didymus the Blind and His Circle in Late-Antique Alexandria (2004), with passages in translation; and B. D. Ehrman, NTS 34 (1988), on EcclT 223.6b–13a (Pericope Adulterae). Roger Pearse noted in 2013 that no English translation existed.
item_023.other_found: German (full): the editio princeps volumes print a German translation facing the Greek. Kommentar zum Ecclesiastes (Tura-Papyrus), Papyrologische Texte und Abhandlungen (PTA), Bonn: Habelt. Teil I (Eccl 1:1–2:14), Binder & Liesenborghs, PTA 25–26 (1979–1983). Teil II (3–4:12), Gronewald, PTA 22 (1977). Teil III (5–6), J. Kramer, PTA 13 (1970). Teil IV (7–8:8), J. Kramer & B. Krebber, PTA 16 (1972). Teil V (9:8–10:20), Gronewald, PTA 24 (1979). Teil VI (11–12), Binder & Liesenborghs, PTA 9 (1969). There are also preliminary Köln 1965 editions. Italian: only studies that translate a few passages (e.g. M. Zambon on Didymus as a reader of Aristotle; Il calamo della memoria IX, 2021/22). French and Spanish: no translation found. Italian and Spanish versions of the ACCS series probably carry the same excerpts, but I did not verify this.
item_023.source_text: There is no public-domain or openly licensed critical text. The standard edition is PTA 9, 13, 16, 22, 24, 25 and 26 (Habelt, 1969–1983). It is in copyright, certainly for the German translation and notes. Under German UrhG §70, the 25-year protection for scholarly editions of the Greek text would have expired by 2008 at the latest (legal check advised). The Greek text is also in TLG under author 2102 (subscription only). Images: Cologne holds 82 pages (P.Köln Theol. Inv. 51), indexed at https://www.uni-koeln.de/phil-fak/ifa/NRWakademie/papyrologie/Turapap/ekklesiastes.html. The pilot unit needs PTA 25–26, edited by Binder & Liesenborghs.
item_023.research_yield: Classroom pedagogy at Alexandria from lectures with student questions; reception of Epicurus (an Epicurus letter fragment cited at Eccl 1:13), Prodicus and Porphyry (CPF testimonia); Origenist exegesis; Pericope Adulterae and Gospel of the Hebrews; a Russian article on Didymus as a teacher.
item_023.recommendation: Keep it, but lower the priority. The first full English version now exists (amateur, self-published, 2026), and Russian has only about 10% of the pilot unit in excerpts, mostly taken from the English ACCS volume. The best first unit is Eccl 1:1–2:14 (PTA 25–26). It contains the Epicurus and Prodicus passages, and the Greek text should be checked against the papyrus images.

item_024.title_short: Sophronius, Miracles of SS Cyrus and John (Encomium + Mir. 1-10)
item_024.ru_found: There is a partial Russian translation, and the colleague's evidence for it is wrong. "Чудеса святых мучеников Кира и Иоанна" appeared in Душеполезное чтение 1889, ч. 2, с. 18–41 (Moscow). The Православная энциклопедия article "Кир и Иоанн" (т. XXXIV, 2014, pravenc.ru/text/1840131.html) cites it in its Ист. section with no translator named. ru.wikipedia attributes it to архиеп. Сергий (Спасский); azbyka gives "еп. Сергий (Могилевский)", probably the same man. It is online at azbyka.ru/otechnik/Sofronij_Ierusalimskij/chudesa-svjatyh-muchenikov-kira-i-ioanna/. It covers 17 of the 70 miracles: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 19, 28, 31, 36, 37, 39, 48, 53, 60, 61, 62 and 70. It was translated from Mai's Greek and is explicitly abridged ("передаем описание их в сокращении"). It is a 24-page selection, not the "tiny 2.9k excerpt" the colleague claimed. Neither the Encomium (Панегирик) nor the Prooemium is in Russian. For the pilot unit, only Miracles 8–10 exist in Russian, and only in abridged form; Miracles 1–7 have no Russian at all. Other Russian material consists of retellings or short excerpts, not translations: the Жития святых of Dimitry of Rostov (Jan 31 / Jun 28); the Russian translation of Makarios of Simonopetra's Синаксарь (М. 2011, т. 3, с. 480–482; т. 5, с. 780–802); passages from Miracles 2, 37, 38, 46, 47 in Н. Б. Ларионова, ИЯКФ 29 (2025), DOI 10.30842/ielcp2306901529064; and М. А. Ведешкин, История 11.4 (2020). Searched: azbyka, ru.wikipedia, the Православная энциклопедия article and its bibliography, Crossref Russian-title queries, and the bibliographies of Ларионова and Ведешкин. No full Russian translation was found.
item_024.en_found: No full English translation was found. Two Dumbarton Oaks Medieval Library volumes were checked on the Harvard University Press pages. DOML 12, Miracle Tales from Byzantium (Talbot & Johnson 2012), contains Thekla, the Pege miracles and Gregory Palamas only. DOML 64, Sophronios: Homilies (Duffy 2020), contains only the seven sermons he gave as patriarch, not the Encomium. Neil (JAEMA 2, 2006) and Häfele (2020) list no English translation. English excerpts and summaries: (1) The Cult of Saints in Late Antiquity database (Oxford; portal.sds.ox.ac.uk / figshare, entries E05914–E07696) has English summaries of Miracles 1–51 by J. Doroszewska. Some entries also translate passages, e.g. Miracles 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 17, 28, 33, 36 and 51 (E06263 = Mir. 8, E07022 = Mir. 13). (2) The Mystagogy Resource Center blog (2025) has summaries of Miracles 1–4. (3) Scholarly studies quote passages: Duffy (JTS 1984), Booth (2009, 2013), Holman (2008), Montserrat (1998), Csepregi (2024). Miracles 52–70, the Prooemium and the Encomium have no English found.
item_024.other_found: FRENCH: (1) The full Miracles: J. Gascou, Sophrone de Jérusalem, Miracles des saints Cyr et Jean (BHG I 477–479), traduction commentée, Paris 2006 (De Boccard); confirmed in the Православная энциклопедия, Häfele and Open Library. (2) The Encomium: P. Bringel, Panégyrique des saints Cyr et Jean, Patrologia Orientalis 51.1 (no. 226), Brepols 2008, with Greek and French on facing pages. (3) Extracts: Festugière 1971 (Miracles 12, 31, 34, 35). (4) D. Peltier, Récit des miracles des saints Cyr et Jean, a doctoral thesis (Paris 1978) with a full translation, unpublished. GERMAN: (1) Miracles 1–7 online: an annotated rough translation by Politis, posted by the HU Berlin Lehrstuhl Antikes Christentum (antikes-christentum.de/de/forschung/heilung/heiligentexte/sophronios). (2) W. Häfele, Krankheit und ihre Behandlung, STAC 118, Mohr Siebeck 2020: Greek text with German translation of Miracles 1, 13, 30 and 37. LATIN (medieval): Boniface consiliarius translated the Encomium and Miracles 1–12; Anastasius Bibliothecarius translated the rest. This Latin is printed facing the Greek in Mai and PG. SPANISH: Fernández Marcos 1975 is an edition and study, not a translation. ITALIAN: none found.
item_024.source_text: Public domain: A. Mai, Spicilegium Romanum III (Rome 1840), Greek and Latin, "Ss. Mm. Cyri et Iohannis Laudes et miracula 70". Scans: archive.org/details/bub_gb_CubecxAg9_MC and archive.org/details/spicilegiumroman03maia. The same text is reprinted in PG 87.3 (Migne), cols. c. 3373–3676, also on archive.org. Mai transcribed Vat. gr. 1607 carelessly (Duffy 1984). The standard critical edition is N. Fernández Marcos, Los Thaumata de Sofronio (Madrid: Instituto Antonio de Nebrija/CSIC 1975). The book is in copyright (the editor is living). Spanish law (LPI art. 129.2) protects editions of public-domain works for only 25 years, so the edited text itself may now be free; verify before reproducing it. Further corrections: Lackner (BZ 1980), Duffy (JTS 1984; "New Old Readings"), Gascou 2006. Bringel's 2008 edition of the Encomium (Brepols) is in copyright. Practical approach: use the Mai/PG Greek, check readings against Fernández Marcos and Gascou, and record the emendations.
item_024.research_yield: Articles on: Christian incubation continuing the Isis cult at Menouthis; medical vocabulary and iatrosophists (Mir. 30, Gesios); anti-Miaphysite polemic before the Arab conquest; Alexandrian prosopography c. 610; Sophronius' prose style; reception (Latin versions, the 1889 Russian abridgment).
item_024.recommendation: Keep, but correct the status: Russian is an abridged 1889 selection of 17 miracles, and English is only summaries and excerpts. A better first unit is the Prooemium + Encomium + Miracles 1–7 (est. ~15k words), none of which exists in Russian or as a full English translation; use the Mai/PG text checked against Fernández Marcos, Gascou and Bringel.

item_025.ru_found: REFUTED. There is a complete Russian translation of all 20 Homilies: «Климентины. Гомилии. Краткое изложение проповедей апостола Петра в его странствиях», translated from the Greek by Е. Б. Смагина, with essays by Е. Б. Смагина and Д. В. Щедровицкий, commentary and a name index. The table of contents (preview PDF at e-univers.ru/upload/iblock/80f/xmq8477qz5bwa3lk4nko231vsl7xnmib.pdf) lists Homilies 1–20, with the pilot unit Hom. 4–6 on pp. 93–130, plus an appendix with the Epistula Petri ad Iacobum. Sources: terevinf.com/books/novinki/klimentiny-gomilii-kratkoe-izlozhenie-propovedey-apostola-petra-v-ego-stranstviyakh/; bookvoed.ru/product/...-8771414; chitai-gorod.ru/product/...-3138441; directmedia.ru/book-727922-klimentinyi-gomilii/. The colleague's evidence (azbyka.ru and the ru.wikipedia 'Климентины' page) predates this book. Searches run: DuckDuckGo in Russian (4 queries, including 'Псевдо-Климентины перевод Беседы', 'Климентины. Гомилии Смагина' and 'Климентины Узнавания Recognitiones перевод'); CyberLeninka API (Климентины, Псевдо-Климентины, Псевдоклиментины, Климентовы Беседы), which returned studies only; ru.wikipedia. item_025.en_found: Thomas Smith, Peter Peterson and James Donaldson, 'The Clementine Homilies', Ante-Nicene Christian Library vol. 17 (T&T Clark, 1870), reprinted in Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 8 (1886). It is complete, including the Epistles of Peter and Clement to James, and public domain. Online: en.wikisource.org/wiki/Ante-Nicene_Fathers/Volume_VIII/Pseudo-Clementine_Literature/The_Clementine_Homilies; archive.org (clementinehomili00clem); CCEL; earlychristianwritings.com. There is also an Accordance edition and an online version in progress at othergospels.com. Selections appear in J. K. Elliott, The Apocryphal New Testament (1993); NASSCAL e-Clavis also lists F. S. Jones's 2014 translation of the Syriac version (Brepols). Hom. 4–6 has recent scholarly analysis: Vigiliae Christianae 73.1 (2019), 'The Role of the Homilistic Disputes with Appion (Hom. 4–6)', plus a follow-up article on Hom. 6.
item_025.other_found: French: A. Siouville, Les Homélies clémentines, 'première traduction française' (Paris: Rieder, 1933; facsimile reprint 1991), complete. P. Geoltrain et al., Écrits apocryphes chrétiens II (Pléiade, 2005), Pseudo-Clementine novel (listed by NASSCAL as major translations). Abbé Maistre (1883–84), selections. Einführung und Übersetzung (Kommentare zur apokryphen Literatur 1/1; Göttingen: V&R, 2010; revised 2015), the first complete German translation; Irmscher & Strecker in Schneemelcher's NTApo (selections). item_025.source_text: Public-domain Greek: A. R. M. Dressel, Clementis Romani quae feruntur Homiliae viginti nunc primum integrae (Göttingen 1853), the first complete text, using the Ottobonianus manuscript; P. de Lagarde, Clementina (Leipzig 1865); Migne PG 2 (Cotelier/Dressel). Openly licensed digital text: First1KGreek / OpenGreekAndLatin urn:cts:greekLit:tlg1271.tlg006.1st1K-grc1 (CC BY-SA). It is based on Schwegler (Stuttgart 1847), which predates Dressel and so lacks the end of Hom. 19 and Hom. 20, though Hom. 4–6 is complete. The standard edition is B. Rehm, J. Irmscher and F.
