item_025.research_yield: Now low as a first translation: the Russian, English, French and German translations are all complete. The only remaining angles are a critical review of Smagina's translation, or a mythography/Alexander Romance comparison article based on Hom. 4–6. Neither needs a new Neoscholia translation.
item_025.recommendation: Drop: Smagina's complete Russian translation (Теревинф, 2025/26) covers all 20 Homilies, including the pilot unit Hom. 4–6, and complete English (ANF 8), French and German translations also exist. A possible pivot within the corpus is the Latin Recognitions (Rufinus), but it needs a fresh Russian check (my search found nothing) and Smagina may continue the series; another is the Greek Epitomes (Dressel 1859 / Risch GCS 2008), whose RU and EN status I did not verify.

item_026.ru_found:
Only a handful of the 238 sermons exist in Russian, and none of the proposed pilot sermons appears among them in full. What I found:
(1) Serm. 12, 39 and 40, translated with notes by N. Novikov from SC 175/243, in "Арелатские проповедники V–VI вв.: сб. исслед. и пер." (ed. А. Р. Фокин; М.: Центр библ.-патрол. исслед. / Империум Пресс, 2004), pp. 315 ff. Online at azbyka.ru/otechnik/Zhitija_svjatykh/arelatskie-propovedniki-5-6-vv/3. The Православная энциклопедия article "Кесарий" (pravenc.ru/text/1684255.html) confirms the Serm. 12 translation.
(2) Serm. 187 (Advent/Nativity, CCSL 104 pp. 763–766), translated by Александр Семанин for Богослов.RU and mirrored at azbyka.ru/otechnik/Kesarij-Arelatskij/propoved-o-rozhdestve-gospodnem/.
(3) Serm. 143, "О покаянии ниневитян", printed as an appendix translation (p. 318) in митр. Николай (Пачуашвили), "Миссионерское служение пророка Ионы и наследие святых отцов древней Церкви" (М.: ПСТГУ, 2022). Source: RSL catalogue with its full-text snippet.
(4) 19th century: свящ. П. Ф. Забелин, "Против пьянства: беседы св. Кесария епископа Арелатскаго" (Новгород, 1894–; at least 2 issues, the 2nd of 18 pp.; RSL FB U 16/1370). This is probably Serm. 46–47, but I could not verify the numbers.
(5) Excerpts only: Russian scholarship quotes passages in the authors' own translations. Examples are Д. М. Омельченко, "Борьба с язычеством…" (Cursor Mundi 2011), which quotes Serm. 13, 50–54 and 192–193 from the SC Latin text and cites no Russian translation, and her other articles. Also В. Певницкий's 19th-c. study, reprinted in Fokin 2004. Omelchenko's 2021 monograph (Петроглиф/ЦГИ) is a study, and I found no evidence that it has a sermon appendix. A snippet from the end of В. М. Тюленев's review of it (Средние века 82(3), 2021) appears to say that Caesarius' texts, "прежде всего проповеди", still need translating. That reading rests on the snippet alone.
Searched with no further finds: CyberLeninka (8 queries, both name forms), RSL catalogue (10 queries), azbyka, ru.wikipedia, ru.wikisource, vostlit and the srednieveka.ru archive. Commercial search engines, Google Books and OpenAlex were blocked or over quota. Not checkable: 19th-c. periodicals that may hold Caesarian sermons translated under Augustine's name, and possible excerpts in Soviet readers or the Russian Catholic Liturgy of the Hours.
item_026.en_found: Complete English translation: M. M. Mueller, Saint Caesarius of Arles, Sermons, Fathers of the Church vols. 31 (1956, Serm. 1–80), 47 (1964, 81–186) and 66 (1973, 187–238; reprinted 2004), CUA Press. archive.org holds lending copies (sermons0031caes, sermons0047caes, sermons0066caes, sermonsvolumeiii0003caes). There are also selections in English anthologies on paganism, and W. Klingshirn's TTH volume (Life, Testament, Letters), which has no sermons. I did run the English verification searches, but on archive.org only; web search was over its limit.
item_026.other_found: French: Sources Chrétiennes 175, 243 and 330 ("Sermons au peuple" 1–80, M.-J. Delage, 1971–86) and SC 447 ("Sermons sur l'Écriture", 2000), all confirmed on archive.org. The 1648 and 1760 French translations and the selections by Riché (1958), Blaise (1962) and Vogel (1964) are known from ru.wikipedia. Italian: a 10-sermon selection (1972) plus later translations in dissertations (per ru.wikipedia). German and Polish translations exist mostly for the monastic Rules. The pilot sermons 13, 33 and 50–54 are covered by SC 175/243 (French) and by FOTC (English).
item_026.source_text:
Public domain: Migne PL 39 (Appendix of pseudo-Augustinian sermons, Maurist text; many Caesarian sermons are there, e.g. Serm. 39 = Ps.-Aug. Sermo 274, PL 39, col. 2262) and PL 67 (Caesarius' homilies), both freely scanned.
Standard critical text: G. Morin, Sancti Caesarii Arelatensis Opera omnia I: Sermones (Maredsous, 1937), reprinted as CCSL 103–104 (Brepols, 1953). Brepols' edition is a copyrighted publication. Morin died in 1946, so his text is public domain in life+70 jurisdictions, and US law generally does not protect a critical text as such. archive.org has only Morin's vol. II (1942), as a restricted loan; I did not find vol. I online.
SC 175/243/330 (Delage, 1971–86, Latin with French) are in copyright.
Recommended: translate from Morin's text, checked against SC 175/243 for Serm. 1–80. For Serm. 192–193, use Morin/CCSL 104 and PL 39 where those sermons appear.
item_026.research_yield: An annotated Russian corpus of the anti-pagan sermons would support articles on: Kalends rites, augury, amulets and healing cults; Caesarius compared with Martin of Braga (Russian translation 2013) and with Old Russian anti-pagan homilies; and sermo humilis and late-Latin vocabulary.
item_026.recommendation: Keep, but lower to priority 3. Russian coverage is only about five modern sermons plus an 1894 temperance booklet, and none of the pilot sermons is fully translated, but a complete English translation (FOTC) exists. The best first unit is the anti-pagan dossier (Serm. 13, 33, 50–54, 192–193, about 12–15k words) from Morin's text, leaving out the sermons already in Russian (12, 39, 40, 143, 187).

item_027.ru_found: REFUTED for the proposed pilot unit. (1) The Oenomaus section, PE V.18–36 + VI.6–7, is already in Russian: I.M. Nakhov's translation in «Антология кинизма» (Moscow, 1984; 400 pp.). The excerpt is titled «Из сочинения "Обличение обманщиков" ("Против оракулов")». It has 14 numbered sections running in order from V.18–19 to V.34–36 and then VI.6–7, keeps Eusebius' framing text and runs to about 9,700 words. Online text: fil.wikireading.ru/hEkLqYwOKa. Catalogue records: fantlab.ru/work1387414 and the MGPPU OPAC. (2) Book XI is translated in full by A.O. Yastrebov, ed. Yu.A. Shichalin, in «Церковь и время» №20 (2002). It is on azbyka.ru, and an extract is reprinted at malgil.com/esl/Eusebius3.pdf. A 2018 notice from the Sretensky Seminary (sdamp.ru/news/n8112) says only Book XI has been translated. (3) PE I.9–10, Philo of Byblos, is translated by B.A. Turaev and reprinted in «Финикийская мифология» (St Petersburg: Летний сад, 1999); online at ancientrome.ru/antlitr/philon-bibl/phoinikika.htm. (4) The Atticus fragments are translated: PE XV.7 by S.V. Mesyats in «Космос и душа» (Moscow, 2005; annales.info/ant_lit/efir/attik.htm), and a fuller «Аттик. Фрагменты» is on academia.edu/44808012. (5) The Numenius fragments, many of them from PE, are translated by E.V. and A.S. Afonasin (academia.edu/6568209). (6) An unpublished 19th-century manuscript in the Optina collection at the Russian State Library holds a translation of selected chapters by the monk Vitaly: «Пятнадцать книг Евангельского приготовления: перевод отдельных глав», 23 leaves, 1870s–1890s, RGB OR Ф.213 к.46 ед.6. Searches turned up no Russian translation of the Porphyry «Философия из оракулов» fragments, Diogenianus, Aristocles, or Eusebius' own text in Books I–X and XII–XV beyond the items above.
item_027.en_found: E.H. Gifford, Eusebii Pamphili Evangelicae Praeparationis libri XV (Oxford, 1903), with Greek text and full English translation. It is public domain, on tertullian.org and archive.org, and tertullian.org notes it is still the only complete English version. Oenomaus is therefore covered in English. A free-standing reworking of Gifford's Oenomaus excerpts is on archive.org (OenomausDetectionOfDeceiversfromEusebius, 2015). Some Porphyry «Philosophy from Oracles» fragments are also translated in modern studies (O'Meara; A. Johnson, appendix).
item_027.other_found: French: complete translation by Séguier de Saint-Brisson (Paris: Gaume, 1846, 2 vols), plus the Sources Chrétiennes series. The pilot unit is SC 266, Livres V,18–36 – VI, ed. and trans. É. des Places (1980). Italian: full translation by Franzo Migliore, Preparazione evangelica 1–2 (Rome: Città Nuova, Testi patristici, 2012). German: J. Hammerstaedt, Die Orakelkritik des Kynikers Oenomaus (Frankfurt: Athenäum, 1988), a critical edition with German translation and commentary of exactly the pilot unit. Spanish: not checked.
item_027.source_text: Best open texts: Gifford, Oxford 1903 (Greek and English, public domain, archive.org) and Dindorf, Teubner 1867, available as TEI in First1KGreek (OpenGreekAndLatin/First1KGreek data/tlg2018/tlg001, CC BY-SA). Older public-domain texts are Gaisford (1843) and Heinichen (1842). The standard critical edition is K. Mras, GCS 43.1–2 (1954–56; 2nd ed. É. des Places, 1982–83, De Gruyter), which is in copyright. So are the SC volumes (1974–1991) and Hammerstaedt 1988 for Oenomaus. Translating from Gifford or Dindorf and checking against Mras is workable.
item_027.research_yield: A Porphyry oracle dossier (PE IV–V.17) could support articles on Porphyry's Philosophy from Oracles, Eusebius' demonology and the cessation of oracles. A fate dossier (VI.8–11) could support a study of Diogenianus against Chrysippus. Aristocles on Pyrrho (XIV.17–21) and Eusebius' anthologizing method are further topics. A new Oenomaus translation would only be a revision.
item_027.recommendation: Keep the work, but drop the Oenomaus pilot, which Nakhov translated in 1984, and drop any 'first translation' claim for Books XI and I.9–10. Use PE IV.1–V.17 instead (Porphyry's oracles and Eusebius on demons and the end of oracles); otherwise PE VI.8–11 (Diogenianus, Alexander, Bardesanes, Origen on fate). No Russian translation of either turned up.

item_028.title_short: Anon., Miracula SS. Cosmae et Damiani (Deubner coll. I–V, Mir. 1–38)
item_028.ru_found: No Russian translation of the Greek Kosmidion collection, whole or substantial, was found. What does exist: (1) Two miracles were read at Nicaea II (Mansi 13:64–68): the man with a fistula healed through the icon of Christ, Deubner pp. 173–74, and Constantine's wife at Laodicea, Deubner pp. 132–34. Both are in Russian in the Kazan Academy translation, Деяния Вселенских Соборов, т. 7, Деяние 4 («Из чудес святых Косьмы и Дамиана», pp. 140–41; first ed. 1873, reprinted many times). Text checked at azbyka.ru/otechnik/pravila/dejanija-vselenskikh-soborov-tom7/1_12_1. (2) С. В. Полякова, «Византийские легенды» (Литературные памятники, Л. 1972) translates only the Life BHG 372/375 (Deubner pp. 87–96). Its miracles happen during the saints' lifetime (Palladia, the camel, the snake, Malchus' wife); none of the Kosmidion incubation miracles are included. The Orthodox Encyclopedia (Православная энциклопедия) article «Косма и Дамиан» (pravenc.ru/text/2458823.html) and «Словарь книжников» list no Russian translation of the miracle collection. (3) A Church Slavonic cycle of the Life plus 12 miracles and the «Корсунское чудо» is printed in ВМЧ, Nov. 1–2 (СПб. 1897). That is Slavonic, not modern Russian. (4) There are 19th-c. devotional paraphrases, e.g. the «Иное житие» in a booklet at shchanov.org that briefly retells 6 of these 12, including Deubner 9 (the pagan who mistook the saints for Castor and Pollux). Also Dimitri of Rostov's Lives (2 miracles). These are retellings, not translations. Searches run: Bing/DDG in Russian («Чудеса святых Космы и Дамиана перевод с греческого Дойбнер», «Космидион … инкубация перевод», «Чудеса Козмы и Дамиана славянский перевод», «Византийские легенды 1972 Косма Дамиан», «собрание чудес … перевод комментарий», Деяния VII собора), plus azbyka, drevlit and pravenc. elibrary/cyberleninka could not be queried directly.
item_028.en_found: (1) This refutes the sweep's "none". I. Csepregi & D. Movrin, 'The Egyptian Miracles of Saints Cosmas and Damian in the London Codex (Rupprecht, Lond. Add. 37534 = BHG 373b)', Classica et Mediaevalia 74 (2025) 69–125, licensed CC BY 3.0 (https://tidsskrift.dk/classicaetmediaevalia/article/view/156873). It gives a complete English translation of the London/Egyptian collection (Life plus the surviving miracles). 21 of its stories run parallel to Deubner miracles (KDM 1, 3, 6, 9, 11, 13, 17, 19–23, 25–33), but in a shorter, miaphysite, non-identical recension. (2) The Oxford Cult of Saints database (CSLA, records such as E08437 and E08460 by J. Doroszewska, 2023) has English summaries, not translations, of the pre-700 Deubner miracles. Its bibliography lists Festugière as the only translation. (3) The two miracles read at Nicaea II should be in R. Price, The Acts of the Second Council of Nicaea (TTH 68, 2018), Act 4. That follows from it being a complete translation of the Acts, but I did not check the page. Excerpts are probably also quoted in Csepregi, Incubation in Early Byzantium (Brepols 2024) and in Kitzinger/Mango, also unchecked. No complete English translation of Deubner's Constantinopolitan collection was found. DOML 12, Miracle Tales from Byzantium (2012), covers Thekla, Pege and Gregory Palamas, not Cosmas and Damian.
item_028.other_found: French, complete: A.-J. Festugière, Collections grecques de miracles: Sainte Thècle, saints Côme et Damien, saints Cyr et Jean (extraits), saint Georges (Paris: Picard 1971). The Côme et Damien section (intro p. 85, text pp. 97–216) translates all 48 Deubner miracles; its introduction is checked via the archive.org OCR. German, Italian and Spanish: no translation found. Deubner's edition has no translation, and the Italian searches turned up only popular material. Modern Greek: only devotional church retellings, no scholarly translation. Church Slavonic: Life + 12 miracles in ВМЧ (1897 edition).
item_028.source_text: L. Deubner, Kosmas und Damian. Texte und Einleitung (Leipzig/Berlin: Teubner 1907; reprinted Aalen: Scientia 1980). The miracles are on pp. 97–208. It is public domain: archive.org/details/kosmasunddamian00deubgoog is marked NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT, and Deubner died in 1946, so the text is also PD in the EU. This remains the standard edition, and no newer critical edition of the Deubner collection exists. E. Rupprecht, Cosmae et Damiani sanctorum medicorum vita et miracula e codice Londinensi (Berlin 1935) edits the separate Egyptian recension. Its copyright status is unclear because the editor's death date is unknown, but the Deubner unit does not need it. The 2025 English translation of the London recension is CC BY 3.0 and can be cited and compared freely.
item_028.research_yield: Articles: Chalcedonian (Deubner) vs Egyptian miaphysite (London, English 2025) rewriting of the same miracles; Christian incubation vs the Epidaurian iamata; how doctors and saints divide medical work; images before Iconoclasm (the Nicaea II reuse); Greek vs Slavonic 12-miracle cycle and the «Корсунское чудо».
item_028.recommendation: Keep it. This would be the first Russian translation, and the first English one of the Constantinopolitan recension, but the sweep's "EN none" claim needs correcting: the Egyptian recension is now in English (2025). Restrict scope to Collections I–III (Mir. 1–26, before c. 600; about 18–20k words). Pilot with Collection I (Mir. 1–10 with prologue, Deubner pp. 97–121, about 7–8k words). Drop Mir. 39–47 (Maximos the Deacon, c. 1300).

item_029.title_short: Asterius the Sophist (Ps.-Asterius), Homilies on the Psalms (Richard hom. 1-31)
item_029.ru_found: I found Russian translations of about 8 of the 31 homilies, all 19th/early-20th c. and all under the wrong author's name. (1) Archimandrite Modest, «Св. Астерий Амасийский: Его жизнь и проповедническая деятельность» (Moscow: Печатня А.И. Снегиревой, 1911). This book contains full Russian versions of seven homilies from PG 40, 389-477: five on Ps 5 (Слово 1-5; Слово 5 is the Great Monday / Easter homily about Joseph), one on Ps 6 (hom. 12) and one on Ps 7 (hom. 13). They are about 14,800 Russian words in all and are reprinted on azbyka.ru/otechnik/Asterij_Amasijskij/ under Asterius of Amasea. PG 40, 389-477 reprints Cotelier's 1681 text of hom. 6-13, so seven of those eight are in Russian. (2) This one the colleague missed. Richard hom. 3 (Ps 3) is printed by Montfaucon as Ps.-Chrysostom, PG 55, 35-39. It is translated as «Беседа 1 на псалом 3» in «Творения св. Иоанна Златоуста в русском переводе», СПбДА, vol. 5 (1899). Online: azbyka.ru/otechnik/Ioann_Zlatoust/besedy_na_psalmy/1, about 2,300 words, opening with Absalom and the victory-statue antithesis. The identification rests on Richard's edition history as summarised by R. Pearse (PG 55, 35-39 = hom. 3) and on the Православная энциклопедия entry «Астерий Софист» (vol. 3, pp. 636-637), which lists PG 40 and PG 55 among the homilies' editions. I found no Russian translation of hom. 1-2, 4-5, 14-31, including 5 (PG 55, 539-544) and 25 (PG 55, 549-558). Where I checked: that encyclopedia entry (no translations in its «Соч.» list); its Asterius of Amasea entry (lists Russian translations in ХЧ 1827 and БВ 1892-94, none on Psalms); the azbyka author pages; CyberLeninka API with 4 Russian queries (Астерий Софист / Астерия Софиста / гомилии на псалмы Астерий / Астерий Амасийский), which returned nothing relevant. Limits: the WebSearch quota was used up and Yandex and DuckDuckGo showed bot-check pages, so elibrary, РГБ and НЛР were not searched. A modern journal translation therefore cannot be completely ruled out.
item_029.en_found: The colleague's "none" is refuted. (1) Nathan Porter, "Asterius of Cappadocia, Homily 16 on Baptism at the Easter Vigil" (Academia.edu, 2024), is a complete English translation of Richard hom. 16. URL: https://www.academia.edu/116769011/Asterius_of_Cappadocia_Homily_16_on_Baptism_at_the_Easter_Vigil. It is announced by R. Pearse at https://www.roger-pearse.com/weblog/2024/03/27/an-english-translation-of-asterius-of-cappadocia-homily-16-on-the-easter-vigil/ as the first English translation of that homily. (2) There are also excerpts. R. Pearse's blog (July 2015) has an English extract from a homily on Mt 27:25 (hom. 21 in Pearse's 2015 post, 11 in his 2024 post). J. Daniélou, Les symboles chrétiens primitifs (1961), quotes hom. I.5 and XX.14-17 in French; the book's English edition, Primitive Christian Symbols (1964), presumably carries them, but I did not check it. Cantalamessa's Easter anthology (English 1993) may contain Asterius excerpts; I could not verify this. (3) The 1904 English sermons of Asterius of Amasea (Anderson & Goodspeed; tertullian.org) are different works, not these homilies. So about 1 of 31 homilies is complete in English and the rest exist only as excerpts. Crossref and Open Library found no complete English translation.
item_029.other_found: German, complete: W. Kinzig, Asterius, Psalmenhomilien, 2 half-volumes, Bibliothek der griechischen Literatur 56-57 (Stuttgart: Hiersemann, 2002). The candidate file gives only vol. 56; the Hiersemann catalogue lists both 56 and 57. German studies that probably translate excerpts: H. auf der Maur, Die Osterhomilien des Asterios Sophistes (Trier 1967); G. Gelsi (1978); Kinzig, Erbin Kirche (1990). French: excerpts in Daniélou 1961; a blogger's (Albocicade) French translation of part of the 1st homily on Ps 8, mentioned by Pearse 2015. Latin: Hervet 1549 (hom. 1-3, 25-27, under Chrysostom's name) and Cotelier 1681 (hom. 6-13). Italian and Spanish: nothing found in Crossref.
item_029.source_text: The standard edition is M. Richard, Asterii Sophistae commentariorum in Psalmos quae supersunt (Symbolae Osloenses fasc. suppl. 16, Oslo: Brøgger, 1956), pp. 3-245. It is the only edition of hom. 1-2, 4, 14-24, 26-31, plus Richard, "Deux homélies inédites du sophiste Astérius", Symbolae Osloenses 1952. Richard died in 1976, so treat the edition as in copyright (EU life+70 runs to 2046); Kinzig's 2002 German translation is also in copyright. Public-domain texts cover 11 homilies: PG 40, 389-477 (Cotelier's text of hom. 6-13, printed under Asterius of Amasea) and PG 55, 35-39 (hom. 3), 539-544 (hom. 5), 549-558 (hom. 25) from Montfaucon. Scans are on archive.org (e.g., patrologiae_cursus_completus_gr_vol_055, whose OCR is unusable). Savile 1612 also prints hom. 3 and 5. A word index exists: Skard, Index Asterianus (1962).
item_029.research_yield: Easter-octave preaching and liturgy (neophytes, the eighth day, Ps 6 'for the octave'); the authorship dispute (Richard/Skard vs Kinzig, 330s vs c. 400) via stylometry; how the homilies were transmitted under Chrysostom's and Asterius of Amasea's names; Church as heiress (Ps 5:1); anti-Jewish themes; sophistic rhetoric in sermons.
item_029.recommendation: Keep, but drop Ps 3 and Ps 5-7 (hom. 3, 6-13) from the pilot: they already exist in Russian (СПбДА 1899; Modest 1911). Best first unit: hom. 4-5 on Ps 4. Both are confirmed as Asterius's by catena attribution and untranslated in Russian and English, and hom. 5 has a public-domain text in PG 55, 539-544. If copyright must be strictly avoided, start with hom. 5 + hom. 25 from PG 55.

item_030.title_short: Hilary of Poitiers, Tractatus super Psalmos (Instructio + Ps 2)
item_030.ru_found: Only one tractate exists in Russian: Psalm 130, «Беседа на псалом 130». Евгений Волохин translated it from the English NPNF version (Watson and Pullan, 1899), not from the Latin. It is online at azbyka.ru/otechnik/Ilarij_Piktavijskij/beseda-na-psalom-cxxx/ and originally hesychia.narod.ru (year not stated). Short excerpts probably also appear in the Russian ACCS volume, Библейские комментарии отцов Церкви, ВЗ т. VII: Книга Псалмов 1–50 (Тверь: Герменевтика, 2021, translated from English). The esxatos review mentions Hilary, but I did not see the excerpts themselves. И. В. Попов, «Св. Иларий» (БТ 4–7, 1968–71; Труды по патрологии, 2004), paraphrases and quotes the work but is a study, not a translation. Checked and found to contain no other part of this work: ПСЛЛ IV–VII (1998), whose Hilary section on pp. 19–35 is Tractatus mysteriorum, translated by О. Е. Нестерова; the azbyka 'О Троице (фрагменты)'; 'Единение верующих с Богом' (Истина и Жизнь 1992); and Метафраст 2019 (Ткачев, Contra Auxentium only). The Pravenc article lists no Russian translation. Searches of ru.wikipedia, kovcheg-very, svyatye.com, cyberleninka and Bing (ru) for Ps 118, Instructio and «трактаты на псалмы» found nothing more. ekzeget.ru was down (504), so its Hilary-on-Psalms entries are unchecked; they are probably secondary excerpts. Instructio and Ps 2: no Russian translation found.
item_030.en_found: This refutes the sweep's 'partial'. updatedworks.com/hilary-of-poitiers/tractatus-super-psalmos/ ('Updated Works') has a free English translation of the whole work, made from PL 9 ('reviewed for fidelity'). It is about 1.75M characters and 939 chapters: the Instructio/Prologue, Pss 1, 2, 13, 14, 51–69, 118 (Aleph–Tau) and 119–150. The fragments on Ps 9 and 91 seem to be missing. It is undated, has no named translator, is not scholarly, and is very likely machine- or AI-assisted. It does include the proposed pilot (Instructio + Ps 2). Scholarly English is limited to NPNF II.9 (Watson and Pullan, 1899): Pss 1, 53 (54) and 130 (131). ACCS Psalms volumes add short excerpts. Burns, A Model for the Christian Life (CUA 2012), is a study, not a translation.
item_030.other_found: German, complete: 'Abhandlungen über die Psalmen', in Sämmtliche Schriften des hl. Hilarius (Sämmtliche Werke der Kirchen-Väter 10–13), Kempten 1833. It is digitized at bkv.unifr.ch/works/cpl-428 and covers the Vorrede (= Instructio), Pss 1, 2, 9, 13, 14, 51–69, 91, 118 and beyond. French, nearly complete, in Sources Chrétiennes: SC 344/347 (Milhau 1988, Ps 118); SC 515 (Descourtieux 2008, Ps 1–14); SC 565 (2014, Ps 51–61); SC 603 (2019, Ps 62–66); SC 605 (2020, Ps 67–69, 91); SC 625 (2022, Ps 119–126); SC 643 (2024, Ps 127–133). Italian: Ilario di Poitiers, Commento ai Salmi, ed. A. Orazzo, Città Nuova, Testi patristici, vol. 1 (Ps 1–91, 2005, ISBN 9788831131858) and vol. 2 (Ps 118); I did not check whether vol. 3 exists. Spanish, complete: Tratado sobre los Salmos, A. López Kindler, Ciudad Nueva, Biblioteca de Patrística 112 and following, 2019, three volumes (Ps 1–100, Ps 118, Ps 119–150).
item_030.source_text: Best public-domain text: CSEL 22, ed. A. Zingerle (Vienna: Tempsky, 1891), free on archive.org (https://archive.org/details/shilariiepiscopi22hila). PL 9, col. 231–908, is also public domain. The standard critical edition is in copyright: CCSL 61 (Doignon 1997, Instructio + Ps 1–91), 61A (Doignon and Demeulenaere 2002, Ps 118) and 61B (2009, Ps 119–150), Brepols. The SC volumes also print their own copyrighted Latin. Zingerle is adequate for a pilot, but we should cross-check readings against CCSL 61.
item_030.research_yield: Russian-language articles on the Instructio as Latin reception of Origen's Psalter prologue; Hilary's views on the Septuagint, the number of psalms and their titles; his Vetus Latina Psalter readings; and anti-Homoian Christology in Ps 2. Russian scholarship on Hilary is thin (Попов, Орлов, Ткачев).
item_030.recommendation: Keep only as a lower-priority Russian-gap item. It is not a first in any modern language: German (1833), Spanish and nearly all of French and Italian are complete, and an online English version (likely AI) exists. Best first unit: Instructio Psalmorum alone (~6k words) from CSEL 22, checked against CCSL 61, with commentary on its Origenian sources.

item_031.title_short: Procopius of Gaza, Commentary on Genesis (Eclogae; pilot: Preface + Gen 1:1–2:3)
item_031.ru_found: REFUTES the 'none' claim for the pilot unit. Baranov V.A., «Элементы антиохийской экзегетической традиции в "Комментариях на Книгу Бытия" Прокопия Газского» // Византия, Европа, Россия: социальные практики и взаимосвязь духовных традиций (2021), pp. 343–359, DOI 10.19181/conf.978-5-89697-381-2.2021.34. The PDF is at isras.ru (…/Vizant_2021/Baranov_…sbornik_2021.pdf), and I read its pages. It gives Russian translations of the Preface (Metzler 1.1–12) and of passages from the hexaemeron section: the long Gen 1:6 passage on the two katastaseis (Metzler 31.26–32.57, printed with the Greek), plus passages at Metzler 69–79 on the creation of man. Note 5 says: "Здесь и далее перевод Д.И. Макарова с некоторыми небольшими изменениями." So D.I. Makarov holds a translation that may be larger and unpublished; I could not find it published separately. No full or partial published translation of the Genesis commentary exists. Other Russian items: Шаблевский Н., «Прокопий Газский. Катена на книгу Екклесиаст», Богословский вестник 2018 №3(30):227–256 (a different work). Болгова 2014 stated that Russia had no translations of Procopius. Шелест 2024 discusses a Slavonic version of his Song of Songs catena. Azbyka has no author page for him (I checked the index). On CyberLeninka, 65 hits for «Прокопий Газский»; Makarov 2022 (Христианское чтение) cites Gen 1:14 but does not translate it. Searched: CyberLeninka API (8 queries), CrossRef in Russian (6), ru.wikipedia, azbyka.
item_031.en_found: No full or partial English translation found. Checked: CrossRef (6 queries), Open Library (in 6 languages), archive.org, en.wikipedia. English quotations of passages appear in studies: Champion, Explaining the Cosmos (OUP 2014), ch. 'Procopius on Creation and Eternity', which probably quotes the creation passages (I could not open the full text); Ceulemans, VigChr 2017 ('Transmission, Sources and Reception of Procopius' Exegesis of Genesis'); Gleede 2024 (on Theodore of Mopsuestia fragments in the Eclogai in Genesim). Bolgova 2012 quotes the Preface in English. An archive.org item 'Procopius of Gaza – Letters English' covers the letters, not the exegesis. Caveat: the WebSearch quota was exhausted and Google, Bing and DDG blocked automated access, so a recent English book or thesis could have been missed.
item_031.other_found: German, full: K. Metzler, Prokop von Gaza, Der Genesiskommentar, GCS NF 23 (De Gruyter 2016), DOI 10.1515/9783110437454; Metzler also published 'Nachträge zum Genesiskommentar' (2020). Latin, full: Conrad Clauser (Zurich 1555), reprinted in PG 87.1. Italian and French studies with excerpts: 'Procopius the Christian Sophist' (Instrumenta Patristica et Mediaevalia, Brepols 2024), with Ottobrini on the Genesis commentary and Philoponus' De opificio mundi, Prinzivalli on Origen in the Epitome in Genesim, and Zaganas. No French, Italian or Spanish translation of the whole work found.
item_031.source_text: Public domain: A. Mai, Classici auctores e Vaticanis codicibus editi, vol. VI (Rome 1834), the first edition of the Greek, from Vatican manuscripts with gaps. It is reprinted with Latin facing in PG 87.1 (Paris 1865), Genesis at about cols. 13–510; the volume's list of contents reads 'Latine a Jacobo Gesnero, Graece ab Angelo Maio editus'. On archive.org: archive.org/details/pg-87-1 and archive.org/details/patrologiae_cursus_completus_gr_vol_087_1 (Public Domain Mark; the OCR is poor). This corrects the colleague's 'mainly Latin' note: for Genesis, PG has Mai's Greek. Standard edition: Metzler, GCS NF 22 (De Gruyter 2015), DOI 10.1515/9783110409833, in copyright and paywalled; German protection for scholarly editions likely runs to about 2040. Translate from Metzler's text and do not reproduce it; the PG Greek can be shown.
item_031.research_yield: Articles: Procopius' hexaemeron set against Philoponus' De opificio mundi, an active Russian topic (Shchukin, Nakaidze); identifying Theodore, Eusebius of Emesa, Didymus, Origen and Philo excerpts; the Preface as a theory of catena compilation; how Gaza rhetoric shapes the exegesis.
item_031.recommendation: Keep at priority 3: no full Russian or English translation exists, but Russian excerpts by Makarov, published in Baranov 2021, already cover the Preface and key passages of Gen 1. Either do the complete Preface + Gen 1:1–2:3, citing Baranov and asking Makarov about his translation, or start with the untouched Gen 2:4–3:24 (paradise and the fall; Origenist reception).

item_032.title_short: Eusebius, Chronicon Book I (Armenian Chronographia; pilot: Porphyry's Hellenistic king lists)
item_032.ru_found: The colleague's "partial" is wrong. A COMPLETE Russian translation of Book I exists online: simposium.ru, «Евсевий Кесарийский. Хронология», translated by the pseudonymous "Агностик", posted 08.06.2013 (http://simposium.ru/ru/node/10525, chapters node/10526–10540). It covers every section: Introduction, Chaldean, Assyrian, Median, Lydian, Persian, Hebrew (2 parts), Egyptian, Greek, Olympiads, "Цари коринфян, спартанцев, правители морей, цари македонян и фессалийцев" (node/10537), "Цари Азии [Малой] и Сирии" (node/10538), Romans (2 parts). It is an amateur translation made from Robert Bedrosian's English, which was itself made from the Armenian. That means the proposed pilot unit (Macedonian, Thessalian and Asian/Syrian kings) is already in Russian. Other Russian translations: (a) ancientrome.ru «Хроники. Список Птолемеев» (Porphyry, Schoene pp. 159–171), by А. С. Мартынов, ©2007, from Smith's English (attalus eusebius5.html); (b) Manetho «Египтика» by Д. В. Мещанский, simposium.ru node/10143 (2012), from Waddell's Loeb, which includes the Armenian Eusebius excerpts; (c) Abydenus fragments compiled by Б. Маслов, simposium.ru node/14594 (2020), with Armenian Eusebius passages via Karst; (d) Berossus «Вавилонская история» by Ю. П. Митин on ancientrome, cited by ru.wiki; (e) Kuzishchin (ed.), История Древнего Востока: тексты и документы (2002), Abydenus excerpts at pp. 297–308; (f) Jerome's Latin Canons (Book II, not Book I) in Творения бл. Иеронима ч. 5, Kiev 1910. I found no scholarly Russian translation made directly from the Armenian. Searched: ru.wiki «Хроника Евсевия», «Берос», «Манефон», «Абиден», «Александр Полигистор»; ancientrome; simposium. The CyberLeninka API returned nothing. The WebSearch quota was used up, so I worked by fetching pages directly.
item_032.en_found: There are two complete English versions of Book I. (1) Andrew Smith, attalus.org/translate/eusebius.html, made from Petermann's Latin in Schoene's edition and adjusted against the Greek fragments. It covers pp. 1–295, including Macedonians p. 227, Thessalians p. 241 and Asia/Syria p. 247. (2) Robert Bedrosian, "Eusebius' Chronicle, translated from Classical Armenian" (Long Branch NJ, 2008), made from Aucher 1818 and declared public domain (attalus.org/armenian/euseb.html; formerly rbedrosian.com). Parts also appear in Waddell's Loeb Manetho (1940), Verbrugghe & Wickersham's Berossos and Manetho (1996) and Burstein's Babyloniaca (1978).
item_032.other_found: French: Eusèbe de Césarée, Chronique I, translated from the Armenian by Agnès Ouzounian, introduced by A. Cohen-Skalli, with commentary by S. Brillante, S. H. Aufrère, S. Morlet and A. Ouzounian. Les Belles Lettres, coll. La roue à livres 90, Paris 2020, 576 pp., ISBN 978-2-251-45079-7. This is a full scholarly translation of Book I. German: J. Karst, Die Chronik aus dem Armenischen übersetzt (GCS 20, Eusebius Werke 5, Leipzig 1911), complete; Roger Pearse has put it online. Latin: Aucher 1818 and Petermann in Schoene 1875, both complete. I found no Italian or Spanish translation, but I could not search directly for them.
item_032.source_text: Armenian: J.-B. Aucher (Mkrtich Awgerean), Eusebii Pamphili Chronicon bipartitum, Venice 1818. It is public domain and is still the only printed edition of the Armenian text (archive.org/details/EusebiiPamphiliChroniconBipartumGraeco-armeno-latinum; Google Books id QUsOAAAAQAAJ). Schoene–Petermann, Eusebi Chronicorum libri duo I, Berlin 1875, is public domain and gives a Latin translation plus the Greek fragments. Karst 1911 is public domain in the US, but Karst died in 1962, so it stays in EU copyright until the end of 2032. The modern French edition (2020) is in copyright.
item_032.research_yield: Little that is new. The only gap is a first scholarly Russian translation made directly from the Armenian and checked against the Greek of Syncellus. Possible articles: Porphyry's Diadoch and Seleucid lists (FGrHist 260) set against the Greek fragments; how the Armenian translator handled Greek names; Alexander's succession.
item_032.recommendation: Drop it as a "first-ever" candidate. The whole of Book I, pilot unit included, is already in Russian (amateur, via English), and there are full English (2), French (2020) and German translations. If it is kept, frame it only as a scholarly Russian translation from the Armenian of Porphyry's king lists (Schoene pp. 159–263) with a Greek apparatus.

item_033.title_short: Themistius, Letter to Julian on Government (Arabic Risāla), whole text
item_033.ru_found: The "none" claim is refuted, with a caveat. A complete Russian text of the Letter is online, but it is amateur and second-hand. It sits inside an unauthorized Russian rendering of Simon Swain's whole 2013 CUP book, "Суэйн С. К. Р. Фемистий, Юлиан и греческая политическая теория при Риме: тексты, переводы и исследования четырех ключевых работ" (701k). It was posted on Самиздат on 30.05.2026 by the user "Шкловский Лев Переводчик" (directory inzhener_l): http://samlib.ru/i/inzhener_l/femistijjulianigrecheskajapoli.shtml (mirror: https://budclub.ru/i/inzhener_l/femistijjulianigrecheskajapoli.shtml). Part II contains the whole Letter, §§1–50, ending "Конец письма Фемистия царю Юлиану". The body is about 3,250 Russian words and keeps Swain's K/T sigla, textual notes and Nemesius parallels. It is translated from Swain's English, not from the Arabic, and looks machine-assisted (e.g. "Т опускается" for "T omits", "The Письмо", "Джулиану"). It has no Arabic text, and its copyright status is doubtful. No scholarly Russian translation from the Arabic, and no excerpts, turned up. ru.wikipedia «Фемистий» lists Russian versions only of the Greek orations (Егунов; Миллер 1985 «Ораторы Греции»). И. Ю. Шабага's Аристей series covers only the Greek Orations XIX (2022), XIV (2023) and XVIII (2024) (https://aristeas.ru/i_yu_shabaga). CyberLeninka API queries (Фемистий Юлиан / арабский перевод / послание) found no translation. Russian Yahoo queries (Фемистий Юлиан арабский; …письмо Юлиану о царской власти; …Рисала Ибн Зурда; …трактат об управлении государством; "Письмо Фемистия" Юлиану; Фемистий Шабага письмо Юлиану) found nothing beyond the samizdat text.
item_033.en_found: S. Swain, Themistius, Julian, and Greek Political Theory under Rome: Texts, Translations and Studies of Four Key Works (Cambridge UP 2013). It gives a new critical Arabic text and what Swain himself calls the "first English translation" (Part II, "Themistius, Letter to Julian", DOI 10.1017/CBO9781139208109.008). It is reviewed in BMCR 2014.12.23 (https://bmcr.brynmawr.edu/2014/2014.12.23). Swain says that before 2013 the Letter was available only through a French summary (Bouyges 1924) and Shahid's Latin. Related discussion, not a full translation: J. Watt, The Aristotelian Tradition in Syriac (Routledge 2019), chapters 10–11.
item_033.other_found: Italian, full (the sweep missed this): Maria Conterno, Temistio orientale: orazioni temistiane nella tradizione siriaca e araba (Brescia: Paideia, 2014). The book gives the first Italian translation of the Arabic Risāla ("Epistula de re publica gerenda"), together with the Syriac Peri philias and De virtute (https://biblio.ugent.be/publication/5870050). Latin, full: I. Shahîd, "Epistula de re publica gerenda, arabice servata", in Themistii orationes III (Teubner, Leipzig 1974), pp. 73–119; per Swain it was drafted in English and then turned into Latin. French: only M. Bouyges' 1924 summary. Spanish: none; Ritoré Ponce's Gredos Discursos políticos (2000) mentions the Risāla but translates only Orations I–XIX (checked against the full text). German and Turkish: none found.
item_033.source_text: Public domain but weak: L. Cheikho, "Risālat Dāmisṭiyūs fī l-siyāsa", al-Machriq 18 (1920) 881–889, issue 11. A scan is on archive.org (https://archive.org/details/al-machriq-, file AL_Machriq_18_Issue_11.pdf; the OCR confirms the text is there). It was reprinted in Cheikho, Anciens traités arabes (Beirut 1923) 1–11. Swain calls it an unreliable transcription of a single manuscript. Standard editions, all in copyright: Swain 2013 (CUP), based on MS Köprülü 1608 (K, al-Dimashqī's version) corrected from Cairo Taymur akhlāq 290 (T, Ibn Zurʿa's revision via Syriac); Shahîd 1974 (Teubner); M. S. Sālim 1970 (Cairo), reprinted by the Egyptian General Book Organization in 2018 and free to read on torath.gov.eg, though not openly licensed. A workable plan: Cheikho as the public-domain base, collated against the K readings Swain reports. True size: about 3.5–4k words, not 8–10k.
item_033.research_yield: Possible articles: the Letter's authenticity and addressee (Julian or Theodosius); its Bryson/Nemesius parallels and Themistian anthropology; how the Greek–Syriac–Arabic versions differ (al-Dimashqī vs Ibn Zurʿa); its reception in Arabic mirrors for princes; and a comparison with Ps.-Aristotle's Letter to Alexander. Much of this ground is already covered by Swain 2013.
item_033.recommendation: Downgrade. Full English (Swain), Italian (Conterno) and Latin (Shahîd) translations exist, plus a complete samizdat Russian rendering made from Swain's English. Keep it only as a short companion piece (the whole Letter, about 4k words), translated directly from the Arabic and framed as the first scholarly Russian translation from the Arabic.

item_034.title_short: Galen, De optimo medico cognoscendo (Arabic, Hunayn), chs. 1-4 + 9
item_034.ru_found:
I found no Russian translation, either full or of the proposed unit. Checks run:
(1) ru.wikipedia «Гален» raw list of translations. It covers Терновский/Кондратьев 1971; Балалыкин/Щеглов Сочинения т. I 2014; Пролыгина 2011/2014/2016/2017; Афонасин ΣΧΟΛΗ 2015, 2016; Щеглов 2024. The work is not there.
(2) Балалыкин's «Гален. Сочинения» vols. 2–5 (Барзах trans., LitRes 2023). Vol. 2 is pathology treatises, vols. 3–4 are De placitis, and vol. 5 is De nat. fac. plus the venesection works. The work is not there either.
(3) CyberLeninka API, 7 Russian queries. It turns up only mentions. Пролыгина, Историко-философский ежегодник 2016, names it «О распознавании наилучшего врача». Афонасин, «Гален. О моих воззрениях», ΣΧΟΛΗ 10.1 (2016) paraphrases 5.1–3 as «О том, как распознать лучшего врача», citing Nutton 1990. Пролыгина's ΣΧΟΛΗ 2017 note cites ch. 6 via Iskandar. Recent Hypothekai and ИЯКФ articles (2022–2025) do not use the work.
(4) Startpage and DDG: 9 Russian title variants («лучшего врача», «испытании», «распознавании наилучшего врача», «Хунайн», «перевод с арабского»…). These gave zero translation hits.
Caveat: I could not query elibrary.ru and the RSL catalogue. The colleague's side remark that no Russian Galen translation is of an Arabic-transmitted text is slightly off. Афонасин's De propriis placitis (2016) is one, though that work also survives partly in Greek. It does not affect this item.
item_034.en_found:
Full translation: A. Z. Iskandar, Galeni De optimo medico cognoscendo libelli versio Arabica, CMG Suppl. Or. IV (Berlin: Akademie-Verlag, 1988). It gives the Arabic text with a facing English translation and commentary. It is confirmed by the CMG Suppl. Or. list, the CMG «Galenus – Übersetzungen» list (updated to 2025 titles) and Fichtner's Corpus Galenicum no. 232 («De examinando medico», E,T,K Iskandar).
Partial or derivative English:
- Iskandar, "Galen and Rhazes on examining physicians", Bull. Hist. Med. 36 (1962) 362–365 (Fichtner tags it T = translation).
- V. Nutton, "The patient's choice: a new treatise by Galen", CQ 40 (1990) 236–257 (study with quoted passages).
- Quotations in Mattern, Prince of Medicine (2013), and Jouanna, Greek Medicine (2012).
item_034.other_found:
I found none in French, German, Italian or Spanish, from three sources:
- The CMG «Galenus – Übersetzungen» list gives only «Iskandar (CMG Suppl. Or. IV, 1988) (en)» for no. 232. By contrast, it lists FR, IT and ES versions for the sister Arabic or Latin texts, De experientia medica and De propriis placitis.
- Garofalo & Lami, Galeno, L'anima e il dolore (BUR 2012), intro n. 1, call it «Sull'esame del miglior medico» and mention only Iskandar's English.
- Startpage searches in IT, FR, DE and ES found only citations: Boudon-Millot cites «Comment reconnaître le meilleur médecin» in the CUF Galien I notes, and the Treccani entry also only cites it.
Fichtner also lists German studies by Strohmaier (1971; 1977, "Galen über die Vereinsamung des Menschen in der Großstadt"). Fichtner classes them as studies, not translations.
item_034.source_text:
Best open source: the Digital Corpus for Graeco-Arabic Studies (DCGAS), TEI XML "gal_deoptmedcogn-transl-ar1".
- Content: a transcription of Iskandar's Arabic text (pp. 40–136), proofread and corrected by U. Vagelpohl. It has no apparatus and is divided into 14 chapters, about 11,800 Arabic words.
- Licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (2025).
- URL: https://www.graeco-arabic-studies.org/fileadmin/user_upload/xml_files/gal_deoptmedcogn-transl-ar1.xml
Standard edition: Iskandar, CMG Suppl. Or. IV (Akademie-Verlag 1988, now De Gruyter). The English translation and commentary are in copyright. The CMG offers a free-to-read PDF at https://cmg.bbaw.de/epubl/online/suppl_or_04.php. The 25-year German protection (§70 UrhG) for the edited Arabic text has probably lapsed (1988 + 25), but the CC BY-SA file avoids the question.
The text is Hunayn's Arabic version, preserved in MSS Alexandria 3813 jīm and Bursa 1120.
Size: about 17–19k words in English, not the 25k in the item.
item_034.research_yield: Galen's 'consumer guide' to testing doctors. Possible topics: the Roman medical marketplace and charlatans; display culture of the Second Sophistic (ch. 9: the Pergamum ape test and public anatomies); Hunayn's Syriac-to-Arabic method; reception in al-Rāzī's Miḥnat al-ṭabīb and al-Ruhāwī. It may be the first Russian translation of a Galen treatise preserved only in Arabic.
item_034.recommendation: Keep. The 'no Russian, English only (Iskandar)' status held up. Best first unit: chs. 1–4 (decline of medicine, Rome physicians, the feverish youth case; about 3,100 Arabic words) plus ch. 9 (Galen's autobiographical demonstrations; about 1,900 words), roughly 7k English words. Translate from the CC BY-SA DCGAS text and cross-check against Iskandar's English, since the editor's own control is weaker in Arabic.

item_035.title_short: Galen, Peri ēthōn (Arabic epitome) and Compendium Timaei (Arabic)
item_035.ru_found: I found no Russian translation of either work, in full or in excerpts. What I checked: (1) Solopova's Russian bibliography «Античная философия и Восток. Ч. III» (ИФЕ 2018; iphras.ru PDF, full text extracted). Its section «9. Гален» lists for these works only Western items: Kraus–Walzer 1951, Mattock 1972, Stern 1956, Klein-Franke 1979 and Festugière–Tonneau 1952. Its only Russian Galen-related entry is al-Farabi's refutation of Galen (Алма-Ата 1987). (2) The «Переводы» list in ru.wikipedia «Гален» names 14 Russian translations, none of them «О нравах», «О характерах» or a Timaeus synopsis. (3) I ran 18 queries through the CyberLeninka API, including «Гален Тимей», «Гален нравы», «Гален о нравах», «Гален этика», «Гален Платон», «Гален арабский перевод», «Гален Хунайн», «синопсис диалогов Платона Гален», «Китаб ал-ахлак», «Compendium Timaei» and «De moribus Galen». They return only studies and the ΣΧΟΛΗ translations by И. В. Пролыгина of other works («О моих воззрениях» 2016, «О собственных книгах» 2017, «О порядке собственных книг» 2016). (4) I read three Russian articles on Galen's ethics (De indolentia 2018, «страсти» 2014, «paideia» 2024). None quotes Peri ēthōn or the Compendium. (5) ancientrome.ru has no Galen section. Google, Yandex and Rambler blocked automated searching, and my WebSearch quota was used up. So I could not check RSL/elibrary catalogues or the contents of Балалыкин's «Гален. Сочинения» volumes. A small risk of an unindexed Russian excerpt remains.
item_035.en_found: This refutes the colleague's "partial" status: both units now have complete English translations. (a) Peri ēthōn, Arabic epitome: J. N. Mattock, "A Translation of the Arabic Epitome of Galen's Book Περὶ ἠθῶν", in Stern, Hourani and Brown (eds.), Islamic Philosophy and the Classical Tradition (Oxford: Cassirer 1972), pp. 235–260. A second complete version is "Character Traits" in P. N. Singer (ed.), with contributions by Daniel Davies and Vivian Nutton, Galen: Psychological Writings (Cambridge Galen Translations, CUP 2013). Cambridge Core lists "Character Traits" in its contents. I believe Davies made the translation from the Arabic, but I could not confirm the exact credit. Arabic fragments are also published and studied in S. M. Stern, CQ n.s. 6 (1956) 91–101. (b) Compendium Timaei: A. R. Das, P. Koetschet and M. Schiefsky (eds. and trans.), Galen: Writings on Plato's Timaeus (Cambridge Galen Translations, CUP; online 16 July 2026, print 6 Aug 2026; DOI 10.1017/9781009552707; https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/galen-writings-on-platos-timaeus/DB8E8A33BCCDF3E5EAD12598D012C72A). Its "Compendium of the Timaeus" has an introduction (pp. 3–44), a full translation (pp. 45–94), a list of textual departures (p. 187) and an English–Arabic glossary. Das 2020 (Galen and the Arabic Reception of Plato's Timaeus, DOI 10.1017/9781108583107) is a study only.
item_035.other_found: Latin: Kraus and Walzer 1951 (Plato Arabus I), a full Latin translation of the Compendium facing the Arabic. French: A.-J. Festugière and R.-M. Tonneau, "Le Compendium Timaei de Galien", REG 65 (1952) 97–118 (DOI 10.3406/reg.1952.3262, Persée). I could read only its first page, so I could not confirm whether it gives a full French translation. Study: F. Klein-Franke, "The Arabic Version of Galen's Περὶ ἠθῶν", JSAI 1 (1979) 125–150. I found no German, Italian or Spanish translation of either work. My checks there were limited because most search engines were blocked or rate-limited.
item_035.source_text: Peri ēthōn: the Arabic epitome is edited by P. Kraus, «Kitāb al-akhlāq li-Jālīnūs», Bulletin of the Faculty of Arts, Egyptian University 5.1 (1937), with more Arabic fragments in Stern 1956 and Klein-Franke 1979. Kraus died in 1944, so the 1937 edition is probably public domain in Egypt and the EU, and in the US as a foreign 1937 publication. I did not find it online. Compendium Timaei: the standard edition is P. Kraus and R. Walzer, Galeni Compendium Timaei Platonis... fragmenta (Plato Arabus I, Warburg Institute 1951). It is still in copyright because Walzer died in 1975, so EU protection runs to 2045. The 2026 CUP translation still uses it as its base text, with a few listed departures. A scan is on archive.org (GaleniCompendiumTimaeiPlatonis, user upload 2008, rights unclear; its OCR is unusable). The medieval Arabic text itself is not protected. The CUP 2013 and 2026 translations are in copyright.
item_035.research_yield: Russian-language articles on Galen's moral psychology (character, habituation, shame, tripartite soul) and his medicalised Middle-Platonist reading of the Timaeus via Ḥunayn; Arabic reception (Miskawayh, al-Rāzī). International novelty is limited because both texts now have English translations.
item_035.recommendation: Remove from the core "first-ever" list: both units now have full English translations (Mattock 1972, Singer/Davies 2013, Das–Koetschet–Schiefsky 2026). The source is Arabic, which the editor checks less easily than Greek or Latin. Keep only as a Russian-gap reserve; if pursued, start with the Peri ēthōn epitome (Kraus 1937, probably public domain), checked against the two English versions.

item_036.title_short: Bryson, Oikonomikos / Tadbir al-manzil (whole Arabic text)
item_036.ru_found: I found no Russian translation, either full or partial. Searches run: (1) Russian Wikipedia API for Брисон, Брисон неопифагореец, Брюсон, Брусон, Ойкономикос, тадбир ал-манзил, тадбир аль-манзиль. There is no article on this Bryson; "Брисон" returns only Bryson of Heraclea and unrelated pages. (2) CyberLeninka API for Брисон, Бризон, Брусон, Брюсон, Бурусун, неопифагореец Брисон, тадбир ал-манзил, ойкономия неопифагорейцы, Калликратид, Финтида, псевдопифагорейские трактаты Стобей перевод, "Plessner Bryson" and "Bryson Swain". The only hit is Solopova's bibliography. The Russian translations of pseudo-Pythagorean texts that do exist cover other works: the letters of Melissa and Myia (ΣΧΟΛΗ 2018) and Timaeus Locrus (ΣΧΟΛΗ 2013). A 2025 ΣΧΟΛΗ article on Philo and Hellenistic Pythagorean texts does not mention Bryson. (3) Solopova M.A., «Античная философия и Восток. Избранная библиография. Ч. III» (Историко-философский ежегодник 2018; iphras.ru/uplfile/histph/2018/386-418-greece-east3.pdf). For Bryson it cites only Bouyges 1925 (Archives de philosophie) and Sezgin 2000, and lists no Russian-language item. (4) The vostlit.info "Б" author index and the ancientrome.ru author list: nothing. Not reachable: elibrary.ru, the RSL and NLR catalogues, and Google/Yandex (CAPTCHA or blocked), so a small journal or dissertation publication after 2018 cannot be fully ruled out.
item_036.en_found: Simon Swain, Economy, Family, and Society from Rome to Islam: A Critical Edition, English Translation, and Study of Bryson's Management of the Estate (Cambridge UP, 2013; DOI 10.1017/CBO9781139178075; https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/economy-family-and-society-from-rome-to-islam/90159B8512470BEAF82CE68E9FD106D4). Its contents: Part I, a complete English translation (pp. 5–24); Part V, an annotated Arabic text with English translation (pp. 425–497), the Latin epitome "Yconomica Galieni" (pp. 498–503), the Hebrew version (pp. 504–515) and an extract from the al-Azhar recension with translation (pp. 516–520). The publisher's blurb calls it "the first English translation". Reviewed by Davis-Secord, Classical Journal 2015 (DOI 10.1353/tcj.2015.0009). The colleague's "full" claim is confirmed.
item_036.other_found: German: Martin Plessner, Der OIKONOMIKOS des Neupythagoreers 'Bryson' und sein Einfluß auf die islamische Wissenschaft (Orient und Antike 5; Heidelberg: Winter, 1928). It contains an "Edition und Übersetzung der erhaltenen Versionen" (Arabic, Hebrew and Latin) with a full German translation, and is freely downloadable from archive.org. German Wikipedia's article "Bryson (Autor eines Oikonomikos)" lists only Swain and Plessner under text editions and translations. I found no French, Italian or Spanish translation (Dialnet returned 0 hits; Crossref showed none), but this is not exhaustive. Recent studies, not translations: Čelkytė, Phronesis 2023 (DOI 10.1163/15685284-bja10071); Başarslan, İslam Tetkikleri Dergisi 2023 (Turkish, DOI 10.26650/iuitd.2023.1193410). Correction to the file: the Greek is not entirely lost. Plessner and German Wikipedia confirm that two short Greek fragments survive in Stobaeus. Bouyges (1925) also discussed the text.
item_036.source_text: Public-domain base: Plessner 1928, with the Arabic text and the Hebrew and Latin versions (https://archive.org/details/der-oikonomikoc-des-neupythagoreers-bryson-und-sein-einflub-auf-die-islamische-wissenescha_1928; full PDF and OCR are publicly downloadable). As a 1928 publication it is public domain in the US. Plessner died in 1973, so his German translation and introduction remain in copyright in the EU until 2043, but the edited Arabic text itself is free to use. The editio princeps is L. Cheikho, al-Machriq 19 (1921); Cheikho died in 1927, so it is public domain. The Greek fragments are in Stobaeus (Wachsmuth–Hense, public domain). The standard modern critical edition, Swain 2013 (CUP), is in copyright: translate with reference to it, but do not reproduce its Arabic text or its apparatus.
item_036.research_yield: Enables the first Russian translation with commentary (suitable for ΣΧΟΛΗ, ВДИ or Восток). Possible articles: Roman estate economy and profit-making; management of slaves; the wife as co-owner; child-rearing; Neopythagorean pseudepigraphy and dating; the Greek → Arabic → Hebrew → Latin transmission; reception in Miskawayh, Ibn Sina, al-Dimashqi and Tusi.
item_036.recommendation: Keep, but only as a Russian-first candidate. The "untranslated" claim holds for Russian alone: full English (Swain 2013) and German (Plessner 1928) translations exist. The best first unit is the whole Arabic text, about 20 pages in Swain's translation, based on Plessner's public-domain Arabic and cross-checked against Swain. The short Latin "Yconomica Galieni" could be added as an appendix the editor can check directly.

item_037.ru_found: REFUTED: the "none" claim is wrong. (1) Published Russian partial translation: "Иоанн Никиусский. Хроника: [Отрывки. Гл. LXXXIV, LXXXVI, LXXXVIII, LXXXIX, XC, XCII, XCIV, XCV, XCVI]" in Евагрий Схоластик, Церковная история, 2-е изд., СПб.: Изд-во О. Абышко, 2010, pp. 539–576. That is nine whole chapters on 5th–6th c. church history. It appears among the appendices to I. V. Krivushin's Evagrius. I did not confirm who translated the excerpts. It may be Krivushin, translating from Zotenberg or Charles. ru.wiki "Евагрий Схоластик" dates the 2nd edition to 2006. The colleague's evidence is false: ru.wiki "Иоанн Никиусский" lists this Russian item itself, in its "Источники" section. (2) A full Russian translation from Ge'ez has been completed. It was made under RSF (РНФ) grant 22-18-00493, «"Хроника" Иоанна Никиуского», at SPbU (2022–2024), led by М. М. Холод, with С. А. Французов, Е. В. Гусарова, В. В. Василик, Д. И. Савельева, Е. А. Мехамадиев, С. О. Хижнякова and Е. С. Кальченко. The project's stated aim is a "комментированный перевод ... на русский язык". The 2024 report on rscf.ru/project/22-18-00493/ says the team "завершили работу над первым полным переводом «Хроники» Иоанна Никиуского на русский язык" with a full commentary, still in draft. The grant was extended as 22-18-00493-П, which 2025 articles cite. I could not confirm a printed book as of Oct 2026: Labirint showed nothing and Google Books was rate-limited. (3) Passage translations appear in articles. С. А. Французов translated the Cambyses passage from Ge'ez for Холод, ΣΧΟΛΗ 18.2 (2024) 607–629, and also the Cyrus passage for Холод, Proslogion 7(2) (2024) 78–97. Related work: Холод, «Александр Великий в Хронике», Мнемон 22 (2022); Холод, Argead kings, Karanos 6 (2023), in English; Ладынин on ch. XIX, Восток 2024–25; the Kubrat passage in Мингазов 2009 and Василик 2023. (4) vostlit.info has no entry (checked the "И" index and the Egypt/Africa indices). The site is not on ancientrome.ru either, and azbyka.ru has no text. Pilot unit chs. 111–121: I found no published Russian translation. Войтенко 2023 relies on Charles and on Большаков, История Халифата II (1993). Even so, these chapters are covered by the completed SPbU draft. Search methods: WebSearch quota was exhausted, so I used the CyberLeninka API (about 10 RU queries), ru.wiki raw pages, vostlit indices, azbyka, Labirint and the RSF card.
item_037.en_found: R. H. Charles, The Chronicle of John, Bishop of Nikiu, London/Oxford 1916, translated from Zotenberg's text. It is public domain and online at tertullian.org/fathers/nikiu2_chronicle.htm, and was reprinted by Evolution Publishing in 2007. There is also a new English translation with commentary of chs. 1–80, about half the text and including all the Cambyses, Argead, Alexander and Ptolemaic material: D. Elagina, The Textual Tradition of the Chronicle of John of Nikiu: Towards the Critical Edition of the Ethiopic Version, Diss. Hamburg 2018. It is free to read at ediss.sub.uni-hamburg.de/handle/ediss/6331. Elagina has announced a full new edition and translation (Aethiopica Supplement chapter, Harrassowitz 2025, DOI 10.13173/9783447124645.049). F.-S. S. Yirga, The Chronicle of John of Nikiu: Coping with Crisis in Post-Roman Egypt (UC Press, Dec 2025), is a monograph, not a translation.
item_037.other_found: French: H. Zotenberg, Chronique de Jean, évêque de Nikiou, Notices et extraits 24.1, Paris 1883, complete with Ge'ez text. An Amharic version from the late 19th century exists (per Elagina). I found no German, Italian or Spanish translation, but my searches there were limited because the web-search quota was exhausted.
item_037.source_text: Ge'ez text: Zotenberg 1883 (Notices et extraits 24.1, pp. 125–605), from two manuscripts. It is public domain and on Gallica (ark:/12148/btv1b52503512k). It remains the only complete edition. Modern critical edition of chs. 1–80: Elagina 2018 (Hamburg diss., about six manuscripts). It is free to read online, but the repository says no reuse rights beyond reading are granted, so it is in copyright. A full critical edition by Elagina is in progress. For chs. 111–121 the only edition is therefore the public-domain Zotenberg.
item_037.research_yield: Little left to claim. The SPbU RSF team has published about 30 articles (2022–25) on Cambyses, Cyrus, the Argeads, Alexander, toponyms, Kubrat and Chalcedon, and has a full commented Russian translation in the pipeline. Elagina's new edition and translation is also coming. The Arab-conquest chapters may already be covered.
item_037.recommendation: Drop. A full Russian translation from Ge'ez by Ethiopist specialists (SPbU, RSF 22-18-00493) was completed in draft in 2024 and the grant was extended. Nine chapters were already published in Russian in 2010. English has Charles (full) and Elagina (chs. 1–80). An LLM translation from Ge'ez would be redundant and weaker. No pilot unit is recommended. If anything, monitor for the SPbU edition.

item_038.title_short: Anon. (Edessa), Syriac Julian Romance (Part III: Aploris–Abdel letter, Julian's Persian campaign, Jovian)
item_038.ru_found: The colleague's "none" is wrong. There is one Russian excerpt. A. V. Muraviev translated the Eleuthera/Magnus episode (Julian's pact with the devil) from Hoffmann's edition. It appears in the appendix "Апостасия кесаря Юлиана в восточной агиографии", section "[Повесть о Юлиане]", of: Мар Афрем Нисибинский. Юлиановский цикл / пер. с сир., предисл., комм. А. В. Муравьёва; науч. ред. Д. А. Поспелов. М.: Фонд «Наследие Православного Востока»; Инфорес, 2006, 240 pp. It is online at https://azbyka.ru/otechnik/Efrem_Sirin/yulianovskij-tsikl/ . The excerpt runs to about 2,400 Russian words. Its opening is filled in from the Arabic Chronicle of Seert. Muraviev cites "Hoffmann 1880, S. 232 ff."; Gollancz places this story at Hoffmann pp. 242–250. It is the "Second Julian Romance" (BL Rich 7192), which Gollancz printed as an appendix, not the main BL Add. 14641 romance. No Russian translation of Part I, Part II or the proposed Part III was found. Muraviev's other Russian work on the topic is analytical, for example «Образ Шапура II в сирийской литературе», ВДИ 2005 No. 3, pp. 115–125, which may quote short passages; not checked. His Romance studies were published in English in Христианский Восток 1/7 (1999) and 2/8 (2000, with S. Brock: the palimpsest fragments, in English). Searched: CyberLeninka API (about 12 Russian queries: сирийский роман Юлиан, Иовиан Эдесса, роман о Юлиане Отступнике, Аплорис, Евсевий Римский Юлиан и др.); ru.wikipedia (Сирийская литература, Иовиан, Юлиан II, Персидский поход Юлиана, which give no translation); ru.wikisource; vostlit alphabetical indexes (no entry); azbyka (hit). Not checked, because the WebSearch budget was exhausted: eLibrary, the RSL/NLR catalogues, and the full text of Pigulevskaya's «Культура сирийцев в средние века» (1979) and «Сирийская средневековая историография» (2000). Those could contain quoted fragments, but a full Russian version of any part is very unlikely.
item_038.en_found: Two complete English translations. (1) Sir Hermann Gollancz, Julian the Apostate, now translated for the first time from the Syriac original. Oxford UP / Humphrey Milford, 1928, 264 pp. It covers the whole Hoffmann text, with the Second Romance as an appendix. It is free on archive.org (julian-the-apostate-gollancz-1928; bwb_T4-AFY-191) and is in the public domain (author died 1930; US publication 1928). (2) Michael Sokoloff, The Julian Romance: A New English Translation. Gorgias Press, Texts from Christian Late Antiquity 49. First issue 23 Nov 2016 (ISBN 978-1-4632-0533-1); revised edition with facing Syriac and the palimpsest material, 12 Jul 2017, 501 pp. (ISBN 978-1-4632-0708-3), confirmed on gorgiaspress.com. Also: S. Brock and A. Muraviev, "The Fragments of the Syriac Julian Romance from the Manuscript Paris Syr. 378", Христианский Восток 2/8 (2000) 14–34, with Syriac text and English translation; and R. Gottheil, A Selection from the Syriac Julian Romance (Brill 1906; Gorgias reprint 2014), a Syriac text-and-glossary reader without translation. Recent studies: J. W. Drijvers, JLA 2011 and The Forgotten Reign of the Emperor Jovian (OUP 2022, a chapter on the Romance); D. Schwartz, JECS 2011; Muraviev, Hugoye 18 (2015); G. J. Reinink 2023; P. Wood 2010.
item_038.other_found: German: Th. Nöldeke, ZDMG 28 (1874), a study and translation of the Second Romance, plus his "Über den syrischen Roman von Kaiser Julian" with summaries. French: Jean Richer 1978, an abridged translation and reworking, reported by en.wiki and it.wiki citing Butts 2011; I did not verify it independently. Arabic: an old abridged Arabic version (Sinai ar. 516; a Mingana fragment), announced by U. Ben-Horin 1961; a Muraviev–van Esbroeck CSCO edition and German translation ("Die sinaitische Übersetzung der syrischen Juliansage") was announced "in press" in 2006, and I could not confirm that it was published. Italian and Spanish: none found (it.wiki "Romanzo di Giuliano" lists none). It.wiki also reports a dating dispute: Mazzola and Van Nuffelen argue for a date after 640.
item_038.source_text: The best open source is J. G. E. Hoffmann, Iulianos der Abtrünnige: Syrische Erzählungen (Leiden: Brill, 1880). It is in the public domain, with a free PDF on archive.org (id iulianosderabtru0000juli, Beth Mardutho/Princeton copy, 284 images). It has 250 pp. of Syriac: the main romance from BL Add. 14641 (6th c.) to p. 242, and the Second Romance from BL Rich 7192 at pp. 242–250. Gollancz 1928 (also public domain) can be used as a public-domain English control. The standard modern text is Sokoloff 2017 (Gorgias), which has a facing Syriac text that adds the Paris syr. 378 palimpsest; it is in copyright, as is Brock–Muraviev 2000. The lost opening of Part I can only be partly restored from those copyrighted publications, but Part III is complete in Hoffmann.
item_038.research_yield: First Russian translation of Part III. Enables articles on Edessene civic theology (Julian vs. Edessa, Maanu), Jovian as an ideal Christian emperor (vs. Ammianus), the reception in Ṭabarī, and links to the Syriac Alexander Legend and Pseudo-Methodius, which fit the editor's Alexander Romance profile.
item_038.recommendation: Keep as a mid-priority, Russian-first candidate, but correct the record. Russian status is excerpts only (Muraviev 2006 translated the Second Romance devil-pact episode), and English is fully covered twice, once in a public-domain version. Part III is about 75k English words, not 20k, so the first unit should be an episode of about 15–20k words: the Aploris–Abdel letters plus the Edessa confrontation (Gollancz pp. ~105–175 / Hoffmann Part III opening), translated from Hoffmann 1880 and checked against Gollancz.

This is the most important overlap: some pilot acts may already have a French translation, so the pilot should be chosen from acts CID V leaves untranslated. German studies with quoted extracts, not translations, unverified: H. Rädle, Untersuchungen zum griechischen Freilassungswesen (1969); K.-D. Albrecht, Rechtsprobleme in den Freilassungen... (1978). Italian: A. Calderini, La manomissione e la condizione dei liberti in Grecia (1908), a study. Italian/Spanish translation status unknown.
item_039.source_text: Public domain: SGDI II (Collitz–Baunack, Delphic fascicles by J. Baunack, 1892–99; archive.org sammlungdergriec0201colluoft and 0202). Its 1890s readings and numbering are partly outdated. Les Fouilles de Delphes III (EFA, 1909–1980s fascicles) is better, but most fascicles are likely still in copyright; this needs checking per fascicle and editor. PHI Greek Inscriptions gives free online texts of FD/SGDI but no open licence. Standard modern edition: Mulliez, CID V (EFA 2020–), in copyright. It cannot be reproduced, only cited and collated. Workable approach: publish the SGDI text, mark divergences from CID V/FD III in the apparatus or commentary, and translate from the corrected reading.
item_039.research_yield: Russian-first dataset for articles: paramonē as a legal institution; slave prices and origins over time (Thracian/Black Sea ethnics, relevant to Russian readers); women and families; comparison with Roman manumission; onomastics; a critique of the Hopkins–Roscoe statistics.
item_039.recommendation: Keep provisionally at priority 4, but do not claim "first Russian translation" until Soviet sourcebooks and Blavatskaya et al. 1969 have been checked; re-run this verification when the search budget is restored. Best first unit: c. 100 earliest acts (c. 201–170 BC) without a French translation in CID V, using the SGDI text collated against CID V readings.

item_040.ru_found: No Russian translation of P.Cair.Zen. II, or of any P.Cair.Zen. volume, was found. Scattered Soviet translations of single Zenon-archive documents do exist, though. A.B. Ranovich, «Эллинизм и его историческая роль» (1950), ch. «Эллинистический Египет», footnote: «PSI 502, русский перевод: АСПИ, стр. 436/7». АСПИ is «Античный способ производства в источниках» (Л., 1933), a Soviet source reader with Russian translations of papyri. The same chapter only paraphrases PCZ 59012, 59013, 59015, 59021, 59025, 59042, 59142, 59155, 59263, 59295, 59341a and 59484/59499, without full translations (checked: http://www.sno.pro1.ru/lib/ranovich_ellinizm_i_ego_istoricheskaya_rol/6.htm). The Soviet readers (Хрестоматия по истории древнего мира, 1951–53; Хрестоматия по истории Древней Греции, ред. Д.П. Каллистов, 1964; the later Эллинизм. Рим reader) and M.K. Trofimova, ВДИ 1961 № 2 may contain single Zenon letters, but I could not check their contents. The Russian edition of Tcherikover, «Эллинистическая цивилизация и евреи», probably quotes the Tobias/Palestine papyri, but I did not confirm this. Searches run: «архив Зенона папирусы перевод»; ancientrome.ru Зенон/Аполлоний; «Хрестоматия…эллинизм…Аполлоний диойкет»; Каллистов 1964 хрестоматия; Зельин/Павловская/Трофимова «архива Зенона»; «Зенон Кавнский архив…русский перевод»; annales.info «Источниковедение Древней Греции (эпоха эллинизма)». CyberLeninka shows only studies. HGV lists no Russian translation for any of the 150 vol. II records.
item_040.en_found: For the proposed unit I parsed HGV metadata (idp.data on GitHub, TM 700–1000) for all 150 P.Cair.Zen. II records (59140–59297). 25 of 150 have some English translation, several only of a few lines. Sources: Edgar's own preliminary publications in ASAE 24 (1924), about 13 texts (59154, 59156, 59157, 59159, 59166, 59179, 59184, 59192, 59220, 59223, 59225, 59241, 59254, 59256); Hunt & Edgar, Select Papyri (Loeb) I 90, 92, 93 and II 265 (59154, 59192, 59251, 59236); CPJ I 9a–b (59241; 59292, line 611 only); Bagnall & Derow 2004 nos. 24, 92, 135; White, Ancient Letters 1986; Westermann, JEA 12 (1926); Rostovtzeff, Large Estate 1922 (59155 lines 1–7; 59199 lines 2–11); Lewis 1986; Rowlandson 1998; Kloppenborg 2006 (vineyard texts); Meijer & van Nijf 1992; Thompson 1988. That leaves about 125 of the 150 texts with no English. My WebSearch budget ran out after one English query, so the English status rests on HGV bibliography and known sourcebooks. The colleague's '14 hosted on papyri.info' understates English coverage, because the Edgar ASAE and Loeb translations are not hosted there.
item_040.other_found: Per HGV, 49 of the 150 vol. II texts have a translation in some language, counting re-editions with translation. French: C. Orrieux, Les papyrus de Zénon (1983), about 25 texts in vol. II; Clarysse & Vandorpe, Zénon (1995); Burnet, L'Égypte ancienne (2003); X. Durand, C.Zen.Palestine 32 (1997). German: Schubart, Ein Jahrtausend am Nil (1923); Hengstl, Griechische Papyri (Tusculum 1978) nos. 117–118; R. Scholl, C.Ptol.Sklav. (1990), about 10 texts incl. 59142, 59145, 59148, 59191, 59195, 59213, 59240, 59249, 59267, 59273, 59292; TUAT N.F. 1 (2004); Mees 2002. Italian and Spanish: none found. No full translation of the volume exists in any language. About 100 texts of 150 (≈67%) have no translation at all, which is less than the claimed 80%. The untranslated texts are mostly accounts, fragments and short notes.
item_040.source_text: The standard and only full edition is C.C. Edgar, Zenon Papyri II (Catalogue général des antiquités égyptiennes du Musée du Caire, nos. 59140–59297, Cairo: IFAO, 1926). It is public domain: Edgar died in 1938, so the work is PD in the EU and Egypt, and 1926 publication makes it PD in the US. Scans: https://archive.org/details/EdgarZenonII1926 (the archive.org item EdgarZenonIV1931 is labelled 't.V (1931)' and needs checking). The machine-readable Greek text in the DDbDP on papyri.info / github.com/papyri/idp.data includes later corrections and is CC BY 3.0; HGV metadata is also CC. papyri.info is now behind bot protection, so bulk access should go through the GitHub repo. Edgar's Greek text carries no copyright. Copyrighted reference works: Pestman, A Guide to the Zenon Archive (P.L.Bat. 21, 1981) and the Berichtigungsliste, both needed only for corrections and dates.
item_040.research_yield: First Russian corpus of the Zenon archive. Articles possible on: Apollonios' management of the Philadelphia gift estate (orders, sowing schedules, vineyards), the textile workshops and female labour (59142, 59263, 59295), Greek–Egyptian labour relations and petitions, the royal oath, and comparing Edgar's summaries with full translations.
item_040.recommendation: Keep, but lower the priority slightly: only the volume as a whole is a Russian first, single texts already have Soviet/Russian excerpts, and a third of the volume is translated into English, French or German. Best first unit: the run of Apollonios-to-Zenon letters on the Philadelphia estate, about 59140–59210 (257–255 BC), in RU+EN, marking the roughly 25 texts that already have English and putting the untranslated letters first.

item_041.title_short: Kaibel, Epigrammata Graeca ex lapidibus (Attic sepulcralia 1–178)
item_041.ru_found: There is no Russian translation of Kaibel, or of CEG, GVI or any Attic verse-epitaph corpus. Only scattered single items exist. (1) Елисеева Л. Г., Андреева Е. Н., «Здесь теперь я отдыхаю под землёй…», Проблемы истории, филологии, культуры, 2021 (cyberleninka.ru). It translates 7 inscribed dog epitaphs, among them Kaibel EG 329, 332 and 626. None is Attic. (2) Петровский–Шульц, «Греческая эпиграмма» (ГИХЛ 1960), and ЛП «Греческая эпиграмма» (ред. Н. А. Чистякова, Наука 1993). The 1993 volume translates Page's OCT (1975). Both are literary (Anthologia Palatina / Page) and overlap with stones only incidentally. (3) Black Sea verse epitaphs appear in Латышев/КБН/Яйленко/Шелов-Коведяев publications, outside the Attic unit. Зусева-Озкан (2025) studies first-person epitaphs and quotes only AP translations from the 1960 anthology, which shows the gap. For the pilot unit, no Russian translation of any item was found. I searched for Фрасиклея (Kaibel 6), Тетих (Kaibel 1) and the Potidaea epitaph (Kaibel 21 = CEG 10). Searches: CyberLeninka API (8+ queries), ru.wikisource, ancientrome.ru (Воронков bibliography), facetia/simposium (1960 and 1993 anthologies), litpamyatniki.ru. A few famous items may be translated in Soviet textbooks such as Казаманова or the Хрестоматия; this is unverified.
item_041.en_found: No English translation of Kaibel as a corpus exists. Much of the pilot's archaic and classical part (Kaibel 1–96) is translated piecemeal, more than the sweep implied. (1) Friedländer (with Hoffleit), Epigrammata: Greek Inscriptions in Verse from the Beginnings to the Persian Wars (UC Press 1948; repr. Ares 1987; archive.org epigrammatagreek0000paul, lending only). It covers archaic items such as Kaibel 1 (Tettichos) and 6 (Phrasikleia). I believe it has English translations but did not confirm this. (2) Tsagalis, Inscribing Sorrow: Fourth-Century Attic Funerary Epigrams (De Gruyter 2008). The BMCR 2008.09.18 review says he "translates the quoted inscribed epitaphs in all cases". (3) Attic Inscriptions Online (atticinscriptions.com) has 215 funerary inscriptions with English translations. These include IG I³ 1179 = CEG 10 = Kaibel 21 (Potidaea, tr. R. Pitt), war-dead monuments and some Roman-era stones. (4) Lattimore, Themes in Greek and Latin Epitaphs (1942), translates many in passing (from memory, not itemised). The Roman and late-antique Attic items (Kaibel 97–178, about 82 poems) are least covered.
item_041.other_found: Spanish: María Luisa del Barrio Vega, Epigramas funerarios griegos (Gredos, 1992, 432 pp., ISBN 84-249-1479-1; verified on Dialnet and OpenLibrary). It is a large anthology of verse funerary inscriptions and almost certainly includes many Attic items. German: W. Peek, Griechische Grabgedichte (1960), Greek–German selection. Merkelbach–Stauber SGO (1998–2004) gives German translations, but only for the East, not Attica. Spanish: Guichard, Quinientos epigramas griegos (Cátedra 2021). Whether it includes inscribed epigrams was not checked.
item_041.source_text: Kaibel, Epigrammata Graeca ex lapidibus conlecta (Berlin: Reimer 1878). Public domain; archive.org epigrammatagraec00kaibuoft is flagged NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT and has OCR text. I checked the OCR: the Attica section runs nos. 1–19 (6th c.), 20–96 (5th c. onward) and 97–178 (aetatis Romanae, including late-antique Christian nos. 172–178). No. 179 starts "Insularum et Asiae", so the pilot boundary is confirmed. Kaibel's text is obsolete and every item must be checked against current editions. IG II² pars 3 (Kirchner, 1935–40) is probably public domain in the EU since Kirchner died in 1940. Copyrighted collation editions: IG I³ (1981–98), CEG 1–2 (Hansen, De Gruyter 1983/89), Peek GVI (1955). Recommended practice: translate from Kaibel's numbering, and in the commentary record the current CEG/IG/GVI readings.
item_041.research_yield: Possible articles: 1,100 years of Attic funerary self-representation (archaic to Christian) in one series; how Kaibel's 1878 restorations compare with CEG/IG; popular prosody and formulae; parthenos/gender motifs; the pagan-to-Christian epitaph transition in Athens; dialogue with AP Book 7.
item_041.recommendation: Keep: no Russian corpus translation exists, only isolated items. English coverage of the classical Attic material is real (Friedländer, Tsagalis, AIO), so the unit is 'first' only for Russian and for Roman-era items. Best first unit: all of Kaibel 1–178 for Russian. To also be new for English, start with Roman and late-antique Attic nos. 97–178, collated against IG II² and GVI.

item_042.title_short: Dodona oracular lead tablets (questions to Zeus Naios and Dione), selection
item_042.ru_found: I found no Russian collection, anthology or systematic translation, but the evidence is thinner than "none". Searches run: WebSearch (RU); about 12 CyberLeninka API queries (Додона оракул; Додонский оракул таблички; свинцовые пластинки Додоны; вопросы оракулу Зевса Додонского; оракульные таблички; додонские таблички; Зевс Наий; Eidinow Dodona; Dakaris Vokotopoulou Christidis, and others); ru.wikipedia full-text search; one Google query. The only Russian work on the tablets is a series of articles by S. S. Kazarov (ЮФУ), 2015–2026. Examples: «Боги в Додоне» (Гуманит. и юрид. исследования, 2024) cites DVC numbers without translating them. Kazarov & Mikhailov, «Предсказание будущего в Древней Греции» (2026), paraphrases single questions in Russian, such as a group asking Zeus and Dione whether to settle «в стране Хемариоев». Zolotnikova (Вестник БГУ, 2019) is a survey of literary sources. That is isolated paraphrase only, with no translated unit. Not checked because Yandex, DDG, Bing and Google Books were blocked or rate-limited: a possible Kazarov monograph, Soviet readers (e.g. Хрестоматия по истории Древней Греции, 1964), and Russian translations of Burkert or Nilsson that may quote one or two tablets.
item_042.en_found: English coverage is larger than the sweep stated. (1) Eidinow, Oracles, Curses, and Risk among the Ancient Greeks (OUP 2007): Greek text and English translation of "upwards of 150" questions (BMCR 2008.01.14). This covers essentially the whole pre-2013 published corpus, i.e. Lhôte's set plus about 20 Christidis texts. (2) I.Dodone Online (Univ. Valladolid, E. Martín González & S. Konstantopoulou, 2024–26; dodonaonline.com/i-dodone-online): EpiDoc re-edition of 300 DVC texts with English AND Spanish translations. 14 entries were online as of July 2026 (WP API), e.g. DVC 4. (3) DOL "Lamellae" pages: 24 DVC texts with French and English translations. (4) K.
