item_070.source_text:
Best open source text: R. Hercher, Claudii Aeliani De natura animalium libri XVII…, vol. 1, Leipzig: Teubner 1864. It is public domain and available as a Perseus/OGL TEI digital edition, URNs urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0545.tlg001.perseus-grc1 and opp-grc1 (catalog.perseus.org/catalog/urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0545.tlg001; Perseus doc 2008.01.0590). Perseus texts are normally CC BY-SA.

Other public-domain backups:
- Hercher, Paris: Didot 1858, with Latin.
- Jacobs, Jena 1832, Greek and Latin.

Standard modern critical edition: M. García Valdés, L. A. Llera Fueyo, L. Rodríguez-Noriega Guillén, Aelianus. De natura animalium, Bibliotheca Teubneriana (Berlin/New York: De Gruyter 2009). It is in copyright. Use it only to check readings against Hercher, not as the base text.
item_070.research_yield: Russian-language articles on Aelian's moral zoology and Second Sophistic animal ethics (Book 1). Possible topics: his sources (Aristotle, Alexander of Myndus, Juba); Alexander and India anecdotes set against the Alexander Romance; reception in Philes (item_091) and the Physiologus. None of this would be a first-ever translation internationally.
item_070.recommendation: Keep only as a Russian gap-filler, not a flagship "first-ever" item: English (Loeb) and several other modern full translations exist. Lower the priority from 4 to 3. Start with Book 1 after checking that Gasparov 1964 and Polyakova 1961 contain no Book 1 chapters, and avoid Book 16, which overlaps Taronyan 2007 and the Russian fragment translations of Megasthenes and Ctesias.

item_071.title_short: Harpocration, Lexicon of the Ten Orators (letter Α)
item_071.ru_found:
I found no complete or partial Russian translation, but "none" overstates it: Russian excerpts exist.
(1) V. V. Latyshev, «Известия древних писателей греческих и латинских о Скифии и Кавказе», reprinted in ВДИ 1947–49. It includes «Гарпократион. Речения десяти ораторов» (ВДИ 1948 № 1, p. 279). These are only the Pontic and Scythian entries, e.g. Νύμφαιον citing Craterus, and Σκυθικά. Most of them fall outside Α–Δ.
(2) Single entries are translated inside other works: «Антифонт. Фрагменты и свидетельства» (2021, CyberLeninka), which quotes Harp. Α 121; the notes to the Ath. Pol. translation on ancientrome.ru; Thesaurus Deorum; and the notes to the simposium.ru translations of Demosthenes and Isocrates.
In this run I re-checked only ru.wikipedia «Валерий Гарпократион»: it lists no edition or translation and cites only Lübker's Реальный словарь (1885).
The rest comes from the cached wave-2 verification: about 11 Russian queries, plus ancientrome.ru, simposium.ru, vostlit and 46 CyberLeninka hits, none of which translates the work.
Limitation: the WebSearch budget for this turn was used up, so I could not run the 4 fresh Russian searches. I did not use proxy search engines as a workaround.
item_071.en_found:
Harpokration On Line (HOL), Duke DC3: J. D. Sosin, J.-P. Smith-MacDonald, M. Zalin, M. Farmer, C. de Lisle, S. Trzaskoma, J. B. Kiesling and others.
- Re-checked in this run (dcthree.github.io/harpokration): every visible entry has a translation, some have two, and each carries a CC BY 4.0 badge. Entries link to the Perseus URN tlg1389.tlg001 and to Suda On Line Adler numbers.
- Re-checked: github.com/dcthree/harpokration-data states the translations are licensed CC BY 4.0 International.
- From the cache: the complete draft was announced by Duke on 4 Feb 2016, the site shows 1247/1247 entries translated, and the repo dump has about 1,433 versions and about 57.8k English words. ToposText mirrors it.
- Not confirmed this run: the Duke news page returned 503.
- There is no printed English translation.
item_071.other_found:
The file's "None found" is refuted:
- **French (partial; it covers the proposed unit).** Re-verified this run via the theses.fr API: Nicolas Andrulli, «Édition critique, traduction et commentaire du Lexique des dix orateurs d'Harpocration (lemmes Α–Λ)», doctoral thesis, Sorbonne Université, supervised by M.-P. Noël, defended 29 Nov 2024. It gives a new critical edition of Α–Λ plus selected Μ–Ψ. It is not available online; DOI 10.70675/83a481d5z4571z4687zaad2zf57b880f4b1e.
- **Italian (partial).** From the cache, not re-fetched: V. Casella, «I lemmi giuridici di Arpocrazione. Introduzione, testo, traduzione e commento» (Alessandria: Edizioni dell'Orso, 2018), with a preliminary study in RDE 6 (2016). It covers the legal lemmata of all letters, so it duplicates the proposed "legal entries Α–Δ" unit.
- **Spanish.** From the cache: a Seville undergraduate thesis (TFG, 2023/24) on historians cited in Harpocration, probably excerpts only; unverified.
- **German.** None found.
item_071.source_text:
Best open text: W. Dindorf, Harpocrationis Lexicon in decem oratores Atticos (Oxford, 1853), which is public domain.
- It is digitized as Perseus canonical-greekLit data/tlg1389/tlg001/tlg1389.tlg001.perseus-grc2.xml. I re-verified this run that the __cts__.xml names Dindorf, Oxford 1853. The Perseus XML is CC BY-SA 4.0.
- HOL displays the same text. Bekker (Berlin, 1833) is also public domain.
- The standard modern edition, J. J. Keaney, Harpocration: Lexeis of the Ten Orators (Amsterdam: Hakkert, 1991), is in copyright. Its variant readings can be cited and flagged.
- Andrulli's 2024 edition of Α–Λ, once published, will supersede parts of both.
- Size correction from the cache: Dindorf has about 41.7k Greek words, not 30–35k. Α–Δ is 422 entries and about 12.4k words, not 300 entries and 8k. Letter Α alone is 284 entries and about 8k words.
item_071.research_yield: Harpocration as a source for Athenian legal and institutional terms, compared with Pollux and the Suda; the Atthidographer and Ath. Pol. fragments he preserves; Theopompus and Anaximenes on Philip; his Pontic entries (Craterus' decrees, Nymphaion) re-read against Latyshev.
item_071.recommendation: Keep, but only as a Russian-gap item. English is complete under CC BY, the legal lemmata exist in Italian (Casella 2018), and Α–Λ exists in French (Andrulli 2024). Drop the legal Α–Δ subset; the best first unit is the whole of letter Α (284 entries, about 8k words) from Dindorf/Perseus, with Keaney readings flagged and checked against HOL.

item_072.title_short: Ps.-Ammonius, De adfinium vocabulorum differentia (Α / Α–Δ)
item_072.ru_found:
No Russian translation found, in full or in part. Web search was not possible: the shared WebSearch budget for this run was already used up, so both search attempts (one EN, one RU) were blocked and the required 4+4 searches could not be run. Checks done instead:
- ru.wikipedia: there is no article on Аммоний Грамматик (Wikidata Q695923 has no ruwiki link). The article «Филон Библский» names only a «Словарь синонимов», with no translation.
- ancientrome.ru/antlitr: no Ammonius entry. The Philo of Byblos page carries only Turaev's «Финикийская история».
- Project cache (ru_series_crosscheck.json): ΣΧΟΛΗ, Платоновские исследования and the Belgorod/КВТ venues have no Ammonius translation (the Ammonius named there is the Neoplatonist, not this lexicon).
Not checked: elibrary/cyberleninka, RSL/NLR catalogues, and possible excerpts in «Античные теории языка и стиля» (1936/1996). The verdict should be treated as provisional.
item_072.en_found: No English translation found. Wikipedia (Ammonius Grammaticus, Philo of Byblos) lists none, and Open Library lists only Greek/Latin editions (1739, 1787, 1822, 1966). The closest English item is A. Pillon, Handbook of Greek Synonymes, ed. T.K. Arnold (London: Rivington 1850; IA handbookofgreeks00pillrich). It is a translation of Pillon's own 1847 synonymy, not of Ammonius: it paraphrases Ammonius' distinctions about 22 times ("According to Ammonius..."). That counts as scattered paraphrase at most. Web search was blocked by the budget, so recent articles or theses with translated entries could not be ruled out.
item_072.other_found:
This refutes the sweep's "none found". There is a French translation, verified in the BnF catalogue: «Traité des synonymes et homonymes grecs, traduit du grec d'Ammonius, augmenté d'un grand nombre d'articles tirés de divers autres grammairiens grecs», par Al. Pillon (Paris: N. Maze, 1824, in-8°; BnF ark:/12148/cb30016949v). BnF gives it the uniform title "De adfinium vocabulorum differentia. français". It is a pre-critical, augmented, school-oriented version made from the Valckenaer text. Whether it covers every entry is unverified, and no Gallica copy was found.
Not a translation: Pillon's own «Synonymes grecs» (Paris 1847). fr.wikipedia's line "traduit par A. Pillon, 1824 et 1847" is right only for 1824.
No German, Italian or Spanish translation was found, but those were not searchable. Renaissance Greek–Latin lexica (Curio 1541, Toussain 1552) include Ammonius material; whether with Latin versions is unverified.
item_072.source_text:
Best open text:
- First1KGreek TEI of Nickau's text (tlg0708.tlg001.1st1K-grc1.xml), CC BY-SA 4.0, Harvard/Leipzig 2016: https://github.com/OpenGreekAndLatin/First1KGreek/blob/master/data/tlg0708/tlg001/tlg0708.tlg001.1st1K-grc1.xml. It has 525 entries in 24 letters, about 17.5k Greek words. It contains OCR errors (e.g. "ΑΜΜΑΙΟΥ", "ἔνδσθεν"), so it must be checked against Nickau.

Public-domain backup: Valckenaer, ed. G.H. Schaefer (Leipzig: Weigel 1822), with Eranius Philo and Valckenaer's Animadversiones: https://archive.org/details/dedifferentiaadf00ammouoft (NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT, 528 pp.). The Leiden 1739 and 1787 (Ammon) editions are also public domain.

Standard edition: K. Nickau, Ammonii qui dicitur liber De adfinium vocabulorum differentia (Teubner 1966, lxxvii+181 pp.; now De Gruyter). The book is in copyright, and IA copies are lending-only. Under German §70 UrhG, protection of the constituted text of a scholarly edition has expired, which is the basis for First1K's licence. The apparatus and introduction remain protected.
item_072.recommendation: Keep. Russian and English are still empty, so the 1824 French adaptation hardly reduces novelty, and the open CC BY-SA Greek text makes the project easy to set up. The sweep's pilot is miscounted: Α–Ε is about 7.1k words (208 entries), not 4k. Start with letter Α (91 entries, about 2.9k words) or Α–Δ (153 entries, about 4.9k words).

item_073.ru_found: No Russian translation found, whole or partial. The search was limited: this turn's WebSearch budget was already used up, so no search-engine queries in Russian or English could be run. Russian checks were direct page fetches instead. (1) ru.wikipedia «Фриних» is a disambiguation page listing only the tragedian, the comic poet and the strategos. Wikipedia's language links show that no Russian article on Phrynichus Arabius exists. (2) ru.wikipedia «Аттицизм»/«Аттикизм» mentions Phrynichus once (wrongly as «Фриних из Александрии»). It cites no translation, only reference entries: Гаспаров in БРЭ 2005, ЭСБЕ 1890, ЛЭТП 2001. (3) The ancientrome.ru author index has no Фриних and no Мерид. (4) The project's own cross-check cache against ~900 Russian translations (Латышев, ВДИ, ΣΧΟΛΗ, Аристей and others) has no match and no overlap flag for Phrynichus. Not checked, and still possible: single glosses quoted in Russian secondary literature, for example the 1936 anthology «Античная теория языка и стиля» (Фрейденберг), «История греческой литературы» vol. 3 (1960), or Hyperboreus and Philologia Classica articles on Atticism. These would be excerpts at most. The project's research cache had no earlier verification of item_073.
item_073.en_found: No complete or continuous English translation exists (no Loeb or other series volume found). (1) The PURA Digital Encyclopedia of Atticism (atticism.eu, ERC grant 865817, Ca' Foscari, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) has about 75 thematic lexicographic entries. Many quote Ecloga glosses in Greek with an English translation. Example: the entry on ἀκμήν (G. Gerbi, 2024, updated 2026) translates Ecl. 93. These are scattered excerpts, not a sequence. (2) Rutherford, The New Phrynichus (London: Macmillan 1881) has the Greek text and a long English commentary. I checked the archive.org full text: the commentary explains each rule but does not translate the glosses. (3) PURA's own DEA entry on Phrynichus (Cavarzeran, Favi, Gerbi, Pellettieri, Tribulato, 2024, updated 20/05/2026) lists no translation of the Ecloga in its bibliography. This is strong evidence that none exists. The colleague's 'partial' should be refined to 'excerpts only'; the gap claim still stands.
item_073.other_found: None found. The de, fr, it, es and el Wikipedia articles list only editions: Núñez (Augsburg 1601), Lobeck 1820, Rutherford 1881, Fischer 1974. They name no translation into German, French, Italian, Spanish or Modern Greek. The en.wikisource author page lists no translation either. Lobeck's commentary is in Latin and annotates the text without translating it. Not checked through search engines because of the budget limit: possible Spanish or Italian theses and Modern Greek series (e.g. Kaktos).
item_073.source_text: The standard edition is E. Fischer, Die Ekloge des Phrynichos (SGLG 1, de Gruyter, Berlin/New York 1974; Tübingen dissertation 1970). It is in copyright. Under German §70 UrhG the right in the edited text itself may have run out after 25 years, but the introduction and apparatus are still protected, so treat the edition as in copyright. Fischer's numbering is the citation standard used by atticism.eu (DEA cites up to Ecl. 402). Two public-domain texts exist: (a) C. A. Lobeck, Phrynichi Eclogae nominum et verborum Atticorum (Leipzig 1820), at BSB https://www.digitale-sammlungen.de/de/view/bsb10237155; (b) W. G. Rutherford, The New Phrynichus (1881), at https://archive.org/details/newphrynichusbei00phryuoft, marked NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT. Rutherford revised and renumbered the text. The text was not found at the expected tlg1608 path in First1KGreek. Recommended practice: translate from Lobeck or Rutherford, check the readings against Fischer, cite by Fischer's numbers, and cross-reference the DEA (CC BY-NC-ND, so link to it but do not reuse its translations).
item_073.research_yield: Possible articles: Phrynichus' banned 'Koine' forms as a measure of Hellenistic and Roman popular Greek (including NT and Alexander Romance α). His literary canon and rejection of Menander. Atticism as Second Sophistic identity. The first Russian introduction to Atticist lexicography.
item_073.recommendation: Keep, possibly raised to priority 2. The Russian gap is complete, and no full translation in any modern language was found. Best first unit: the dedication to Cornelianus plus Ecl. 1–100 (Fischer's numbering), about 3k Greek words. Translate it as a bilingual annotated text, cross-referenced to the DEA and Rutherford.

item_074.title_short: Hephaestion, Enchiridion de metris (with Peri poiematos)
item_074.ru_found: I found no Russian translation, but this is not fully verified. WebSearch was refused before my first query because the shared 200-search budget for this turn was already used up, so none of the required 4 Russian and 4 English searches ran. What I did check: (1) ru.wikipedia "Гефестион (грамматик)" (fetched). Its editions list has Westphal 1866, Consbruch 1906 and van Ophuijsen 1987 (English). Its literature list has van Ophuijsen and Кузнецов, "Латинская метрика" (2006). No Russian translation is listed. (2) The ancientrome.ru/antlitr author list (fetched) has no Hephaestion entry. (3) The project cache: the wave-1 sweep and 02_candidates.md row 149 ("Гефестион, «Энхиридий»") have no RU translation. I could not search elibrary or cyberleninka (Philologia Classica, Аристей, Hyperboreus, ΣΧΟΛΗ, ВДИ), search.rsl.ru or nlr.ru. I also could not check whether excerpts appear in anthologies such as «Античные теории языка и стиля» (1936/1996) or «Античная музыкальная эстетика» (1960), or in Gasparov's work on metrics. A recent journal translation of single chapters cannot be ruled out.
item_074.en_found: There are two complete English translations, not one as the colleague claimed. (1) T. F. Barham, "The Enkheiridion of Hehfaistiown concerning Metres and Poems", Cambridge: Deighton, 1843. It has Greek text and an English translation with notes, x+229 pp. It is in the public domain and scanned at https://archive.org/details/hephaistinosenc01hephgoog (listed on en.wikipedia). The title says it covers both metres and poems, but I did not open the scan to confirm it translates everything. (2) J. M. van Ophuijsen, "Hephaestion on Metre: A Translation and Commentary", Leiden: Brill, 1987 (Mnemosyne Suppl. 100, ISBN 9789004084520). This is the full modern translation with commentary and is in copyright.
item_074.other_found: The colleague's "none found" is refuted. Spanish has a full translation: Biblioteca Clásica Gredos no. 383, "Métrica (Hefestión); Harmónica. Rítmica (Aristóxeno); Harmónica (Ptolomeo)", 616 pp. The year 2010 comes from the es.wikipedia Hephaestion article; the volume entry comes from the es.wikipedia annex "Bibliografía de la Biblioteca Clásica Gredos". I could not verify the translator. German: none found. de.wikipedia lists only Consbruch, van Ophuijsen and Tzetzes' Byzantine verse paraphrase. Italian: none found (it.wikipedia lists the Giunta editio princeps of 1526, Gaisford 1855, Consbruch 1906 and van Ophuijsen). French: the fr.wikipedia page was not found and nothing else was checked. A Budé or CUF edition was not checked.
item_074.source_text: The best public-domain text is M. Consbruch, Hephaestionis Enchiridion cum commentariis veteribus, Leipzig: Teubner 1906. It is the standard critical edition, reprinted Stuttgart 1971 (ISBN 978-3-519-01399-0), and the 1906 original is public domain. The Enchiridion and Περὶ ποιήματος fill pp. 1–73, followed by the scholia and Choeroboscus. Older public-domain texts: Westphal, Scriptores metrici Graeci I (Teubner 1866; Google Books id=Duz0ZuIpNL4C); Gaisford, 3rd ed., Oxford 1855; and Barham 1843 with an English translation (archive.org). No newer critical edition is known to replace Consbruch. Only van Ophuijsen's 1987 translation and commentary (Brill) is in copyright. I did not confirm an open TEI/First1KGreek digital text.
item_074.research_yield: Hephaestion's metrical terms compared with Russian (Gasparov) usage. His citations as a source for fragments of Sappho, Alcaeus, Anacreon and comic poets. Asynarteta and Περὶ ποιήματος on stanza structure. His reception through Choeroboscus and Tzetzes. A Russian teaching companion on Greek metre.
item_074.recommendation: Keep it as a mid-priority filler that fills a Russian gap, not a flagship: there are two full English translations and a full Spanish one, and it lies outside the editor's Alexander Romance specialism. The best first unit is the short Περὶ ποιήματος plus Enchiridion chapters 1–6 (prosody, feet, catalexis). These need less scansion, which suits an LLM. Run Russian database checks (elibrary, Philologia Classica, rsl.ru) before committing.

item_075.title_short: Apollonius Dyscolus, Περὶ συνδέσμων / On Conjunctions (complete)
item_075.ru_found: I found no Russian translation of De coniunctionibus, whole or partial. The search was limited: the shared WebSearch budget ran out, and both searches I tried (one RU, one EN) returned "budget used up". I could not run the required 4 RU and 4 EN searches. What I did instead was direct fetches plus the project cache. (1) ru.wikipedia "Аполлоний Дискол" lists no translation, only studies: Добиаш, Синтаксис Аполлония Дискола (Киев 1882), and Поликарпов, Philologia Classica 7 (2007) 96–109. (2) Schmidhauser's bibliography of all translations of Apollonius (schmidhauser.us/apollonius/bibliography/translations/) lists no Russian translation of any work. (3) The ancientrome.ru author index has no Apollonius Dyscolus. (4) philology.ru linguistics index: no entry. One open caveat, also flagged in ru_series_crosscheck.json: the thematic anthology «Античные теории языка и стиля» (ed. О. М. Фрейденберг, М.–Л. 1936; repr. СПб.: Алетейя 1996) prints short excerpts from the grammarians (Varro, transl. Я. М. Боровский, 1936 pp. 80–83, 94–104, 120; Dionysius Thrax, 1996 pp. 111–144). It probably includes Apollonius excerpts, mainly from the Syntax. A few lines on the conjunction cannot be ruled out. I could not check the table of contents online. Check it before claiming «первый перевод на русский».
item_075.en_found: No English translation of On Conjunctions was found. Schmidhauser's list of translations of all of Apollonius's works has only one English entry, Householder 1981, which covers the Syntax. en.wikipedia also names no translation of Conjunctions or Adverbs. English versions of the other works: Syntax by F. W. Householder (Amsterdam: Benjamins 1981); De pronomine pars generalis with English translation by A. U. Schmidhauser (PhD diss., Geneva 2007). Scattered English renderings of single passages probably exist in secondary literature on Stoic logic (e.g. on συναπτικοί and παρασυναπτικοί), but I did not verify any. I could not run the English searches (budget exhausted), so a recent thesis or article cannot be ruled out.
item_075.other_found: FRENCH, full: C. Dalimier, «Apollonius Dyscole: Traité des conjonctions», Paris: Vrin 2001 (from a Sorbonne diss., 1995), with introduction, revised text, translation and commentary. Confirmed in Schmidhauser's translations and editions lists. No German, Italian or Spanish translation of Conjunctions is listed there. Other works for context: Syntax in German (Buttmann 1877), Spanish (Bécares Botas, Gredos 1987), French (Lallot 1997), Polish (Bednarski 2000) and Latin (Portus/Sylburg 1590); De pronomine in German (Brandenburg 2005). Brocquet made a French translation of the Adverbs (mémoire 1982); I did not check whether it was published. Possibly: German translations of Stoic-related passages of Conj. in Hülser, Die Fragmente zur Dialektik der Stoiker (1987–88). This is from memory and not verified.
item_075.source_text: Public domain. R. Schneider, Apollonii Dyscoli quae supersunt I.1: Scripta minora (Grammatici Graeci II.1.1, Leipzig: Teubner 1878), Conj. at pp. 213–258. Schneider's commentary in GG II.1.2 (1902) is also PD and useful. Bekker, Anecdota Graeca II (Berlin 1816) is the editio princeps of Conj. Free scans of Bekker, and a free Unicode transcription of Schneider's text, are at https://schmidhauser.us/apollonius/works/ (conn.txt / connectives.pdf). The transcription is about 12,600 whitespace tokens, so about 11–12k Greek words. The text depends on a single manuscript (Paris. gr. 2548) and has lacunae and corruptions. The modern standard text, Dalimier 2001 (Vrin), is in copyright. Use Schneider as the base and Dalimier only as a reference.
item_075.research_yield: How Stoic logical connectives (συμπλεκτικοί, διαζευκτικοί, συναπτικοί, παρασυναπτικοί) were absorbed into grammar. Apollonius compared with Dionysius Thrax §20 and Priscian XVI. Ancient theory of expletive particles (γε, δή, ἄρα) set against Denniston. A Russian grammatical glossary. Lines of influence into Byzantine and Slavonic grammar.
item_075.recommendation: Keep at priority 2. First unit: Conj. Schneider 213.1 to about 232 (preface, definition, copulative, disjunctive, conditional and causal conjunctions; about 5–6k words). The expletive-particle section follows as unit 2. Before claiming a Russian "first", check the table of contents of «Античные теории языка и стиля» (1936/1996) for Apollonius excerpts. Re-run the RU and EN searches once the search budget allows.

item_076.title_short: Erotian, Collection of Hippocratic Words (preface with list of works + Α–Γ)
item_076.ru_found: No Russian translation found, but the check was limited. The WebSearch budget for this run (200 calls, shared across agents) was used up on my first query, so none of the planned Russian searches ran. Direct checks: ru.wikipedia has no article (both "Эротиан" and the list title the colleague cited returned 404). ancientrome.ru/antlitr has no Erotian in its author index (fetched and decoded from cp1251). The project's earlier sweeps (02_candidates.md, wave1 JSON) give "нет" with no evidence. Not checked: cyberleninka, eLibrary, RSL/NLR catalogues, Kovner's "Очерки истории медицины" and the Rudnev/Karpov Hippocrates introductions (1936–44), which might paraphrase or quote the list of works. Re-run the RU searches when the budget allows.
item_076.en_found: No full or partial English translation found. The English searches could not run (same budget limit). Direct checks: the en.wikipedia "Erotianus" article lists none. de.wikipedia "Erotianos (Grammatiker)" has a detailed list of editions and records only Latin translations; fr, es, ca, el, la and hu Wikipedias list none; Wikidata Q990996 has no work items. English excerpts probably exist but were NOT verified this session. Candidates (from memory): H. von Staden, Herophilus (CUP 1989), whose Bacchius fragments come largely from Erotian; von Staden, "Lexicography in the third century B.C.: Bacchius of Tanagra, Erotian and Hippocrates" (in López Férez ed., Tratados hipocráticos, 1992); and handbooks on the Hippocratic Corpus that quote Erotian's list (Smith 1979, Craik 2015, Longrigg's sourcebook 1998). Treat these as leads to check, not evidence.
item_076.other_found: No modern-language translation found (FR/DE/IT/ES not searched for the budget reason; the Wikipedia evidence above was checked). There are Latin translations, verified via archive.org metadata. B. Eustachi (Venice: Giunta, 1566) has a Latin translation and notes: archive.org/details/erotianigraecis00hippgoog. J.G.F. Franz (Leipzig 1780) prints the Greek with a Latin translation, together with the Galen and Herodotus glossaries: archive.org/details/b28775132. H. Estienne's Dictionarium medicum (Paris 1564) gives the text with Latin explanations; e-rara and Gallica scans are linked from fr.wikipedia. Not checked: a Spanish thesis or translation (Spain has a strong Hippocratic school), and the Anastassiou–Irmer Testimonien zum Corpus Hippocraticum (I believe it has no translation).
item_076.source_text: Standard edition: E. Nachmanson, Erotiani vocum Hippocraticarum collectio cum fragmentis (Uppsala: Appelberg, 1918; Collectio scriptorum veterum Upsaliensis). Nachmanson died in 1943, so the edition is public domain worldwide; archive.org marks it NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT. Scan: https://archive.org/details/erotianivocumhip00erotuoft. The companion study, Nachmanson, Erotianstudien (1917), is also PD: https://archive.org/details/erotianstudien00nachuoft. The older edition by J. Klein (Leipzig 1865) is PD as well: https://archive.org/details/erotianivocumhip00erot. As far as I know Nachmanson is still the standard edition and no newer copyrighted edition has replaced it, but this was not search-verified. Erotian is not in First1KGreek, so the Greek text would need OCR from the Nachmanson scan or keying from the TLG.
item_076.research_yield: Articles possible: Erotian's list and classification of Hippocratic works and the early shape of the Corpus; Hellenistic medical glossography (Bacchius, Glaucias, Heraclides of Tarentum); literary quotations used as evidence in the glosses; Greek–Russian medical terminology notes.
item_076.recommendation: Keep at priority 2 (specialist audience). No translation was found in any modern language; only Latin versions from 1566 and 1780 exist. Best first unit: the preface with the list and classification of works, then letters Α–Γ, from Nachmanson 1918 (PD). Before launch, re-run the four Russian and four English searches the budget blocked, checking von Staden 1989/1992 for English excerpts.

item_077.title_short: Timaeus the Sophist, Lexicon Platonicum (whole lexicon, 468 entries)
item_077.ru_found: No Russian translation found, but the check is limited. WebSearch was unavailable because the run-wide budget of 200 searches was already used up, so none of the required Russian queries ran. Direct checks instead: (1) ru.wikipedia, «Тимей (греческий грамматик)», names only the Ruhnken 1754 and Koch 1828 editions and ЭСБЕ, and no translation. (2) I downloaded the contents pages of every ΣΧΟΛΗ issue from 1.1 (2007) to 20.2 (2026), 40 issues, plus the book-series page (classics.nsu.ru/schole/pageN.html) and scanned them for Тиме-/Timae-/lexicon/словар-. There is nothing on Timaeus the Sophist or a Platonic lexicon. The only Timaeus hits are Plato's dialogue and the Proclus/Calcidius commentaries. Not checked: Платоновские исследования (URL unreachable), Hyperboreus (DNS failure), Philologia Classica, ВДИ, cyberleninka/elibrary, and the RSL/NLR catalogues. The genre (a Greek-to-Greek glossary) and its obscurity make a Russian translation very unlikely, but the catalogue sweep still needs to be done.
item_077.en_found: No English translation found. en.wikipedia (Timaeus the Sophist) names no English translation. Its bibliography gives only the Bonelli/Barnes edition (Leiden 2007, French) and Dörrie–Baltes (German excerpts), plus Dickey 2007 and Carhart 2007, which are studies. fr.wikipedia names only Bonelli. Single glosses that passed into the Suda may appear in English in the Suda On Line, but that is indirect and was not checked. English searches (Loeb, BMCR, Google Books) could not be run because the search budget was exhausted.
item_077.other_found: French, complete: Maddalena Bonelli, Timée le Sophiste, Lexique platonicien. Texte, traduction et commentaire, with an introduction by Jonathan Barnes, Leiden: Brill 2007 (Philosophia Antiqua; confirmed via fr/en.wikipedia). German, excerpts: H. Dörrie and M. Baltes, Der Platonismus in der Antike, vol. 3 (Stuttgart-Bad Cannstatt 1993), pp. 54 and 58, Greek text with German translation of the relevant passages (cited in en.wikipedia). Italian: from memory and not verified this run, S. Valente, I lessici a Platone di Timeo Sofista e Pseudo-Didimo (De Gruyter, Sozomena, 2012), a critical edition with introduction. I believe it contains no translation. No Spanish found; not searched.
item_077.source_text: Public domain: D. Ruhnken, Timaei Sophistae Lexicon vocum Platonicarum (Leiden: Luchtmans 1754; 2nd ed. with commentary 1789), and G. A. Koch's revision (Leipzig 1828). Both are long out of copyright and normally scanned on Google Books/archive.org; I did not confirm scan URLs because search was unavailable. C. F. Hermann's Teubner Plato vol. VI (1853) probably reprints the lexicon (from memory). The text survives in essentially one manuscript, Coislinianus 345, part of which is now at Lavra on Athos (ZPE 131, 2000, 58–64). Use Koch 1828 as the base text and check it against the modern apparatus. Both modern standard editions are in copyright: Bonelli 2007 (Brill) and Valente 2012 (De Gruyter, if confirmed).
item_077.research_yield: Articles on Imperial-age Platonic lexicography (Timaeus vs. Harpocration, Moeris, Phrynichus, Ps.-Didymus), Atticism and the school reading of Plato, the dating and the 'ἄμουσος παιδιά' prooemium, and the paths by which glosses reached Photius and the Suda. Specialist interest only; Bonelli's commentary already covers much.
item_077.recommendation: Keep, demoted to the reserve list. RU and EN are both still gaps, but a complete French translation with commentary exists (Bonelli 2007), and a Greek-to-Greek glossary gives readers less than a narrative text. Start with the prooemium plus letter Α (about 60–80 entries) from Koch 1828, checking each gloss against Bonelli and Valente and identifying the Platonic passage it explains.

item_078.title_short: Ptolemy Chennus, Novel History (Photius Bibl. cod. 190, whole)
item_078.ru_found: REFUTED. A.V. Garadja (А.В. Гараджа), "Новая история Птолемея Хенна (Phot. Bibl. 190)", ΣΧΟΛΗ 16.2 (2022), pp. 862–888, DOI 10.25205/1995-4328-2022-16-2-862-888, PDF https://classics.nsu.ru/schole/assets/files/16-2-garaja.pdf. I downloaded and read the PDF. Its abstract calls it "the first full Russian translation of the work", and the commentary has more than 50 notes, with heavy use of Eustathius. The translation is made from Henry's 1962 text, with Bekker page markers 146a–153b, and covers the preface and books I–VII in full. So the proposed unit is exactly this text. ru.wikipedia (Птолемей Хенн) does not mention this translation and lists only Latyshev's excerpts (ВДИ 1947 №4, pp. 277–278), which is why the sweep wrongly said "partial". The project cache already flagged this (research/raw/ru_series_crosscheck.json, research/odyssey.md, research/02_candidates.md), and I confirmed it from the primary PDF. I did not check Vasilik's Russian Photius because the question is already settled. Caveat: the per-turn WebSearch budget was used up, so the required 4 RU and 4 EN searches could not be run. My verification used the cache plus direct fetches of the PDF and of the Wikipedia and tertullian.org pages.
item_078.en_found: tertullian.org, "Photius: Bibliotheca. Codices 186–222 (selected)" (http://www.tertullian.org/fathers/photius_copyright/photius_05bibliotheca.htm), has an English version of the whole of cod. 190. It runs from the preface to "Such are the chapters of the seventh book…" and ends with the note "[Translated from Henry]". It is therefore indirect, made from Henry's French. The translator of cod. 190 is not named (a Brady Kiesling note follows cod. 186), and the page header reads "Portions © Les Belles Lettres". en.wikipedia cites it. I found no direct English translation from the Greek in print. B. Hartley's doctoral thesis, Novel Research: Fiction and Authority in Ptolemy Chennus (Exeter, 2014; cited by Garadja), may include one, but I could not check because the Exeter repository returned 403.
item_078.other_found: French: R. Henry, Photius, Bibliothèque III (Budé/CUF 1962), pp. 51–72, full Greek text with facing translation; this is the base text for Garadja and the tertullian.org English. Italian: a complete translation of the Bibliotheca (Edizioni della Normale, Pisa, 2016, ed. Bianchi and Schiano) should include cod. 190, but this is from memory and was not checked this session. German: Chatzis 1914 (Paderborn) gives an introduction and text; I did not check whether it has a translation. Decloquement 2021 (de Gruyter) is a study, not a translation. Spanish: not checked, because the search budget was used up.
item_078.source_text: Public domain: I. Bekker, Photii Bibliotheca vol. 1 (Berlin 1824), pp. 146–153; Roulez 1834 (separate edition with commentary); A. Westermann, Mythographoi (Brunswick 1843), pp. 182–199. Garadja gives these pages; the candidate file's 182–192 seems to be wrong. All are on Google Books / archive.org. Chatzis 1914 is public domain in the US. The standard modern edition, R. Henry, Budé 1962 (Les Belles Lettres), is in copyright.
item_078.research_yield: Low for Neoscholia, because Garadja's annotated Russian translation (2022) already covers the whole text. What is left: a direct English version from the Greek, and articles on Chennus's invented sources or his Homeric "corrections", which can be written without a new translation.
item_078.recommendation: Drop: Garadja (ΣΧΟΛΗ 2022) has published a full Russian translation with commentary of cod. 190, and an indirect full English rendering exists. At most, keep it as a low-priority option for a direct English translation from Bekker/Westermann, crediting Garadja.

item_079.title_short: John Tzetzes, Chiliades (Historiai), Chiliad I or Alexander histories
item_079.ru_found: METHOD CAVEAT: the shared web-search budget ran out before I started, so I could not run the required 4 Russian and 4 English searches. This verdict rests on (a) the project's cached sweeps (wave1_landscape_and_sweeps.json, ru_series_crosscheck.json, alexander.json) and (b) pages I fetched directly. (1) Памятники византийской литературы IX–XIV вв. (М.: Наука, 1969): Tzetzes excerpts on pp. 252–259, by Т. В. Попова, with her introduction on pp. 251–252 (ru.wikipedia 'Иоанн Цец', fn. 23 and the bibliography). At about 8 pages this cannot be more than a few hundred lines, and I could not confirm which histories it covers. (2) Латышев, Известия древних писателей о Скифии и Кавказе, т. I, and the ВДИ 1952 №2 Дополнения: a cached reading of the vol. I index found Tzetzes only as commentator on Lycophron (pp. 400–406), with no separate Chiliades entry. Scythian passages, such as the Arimaspea lines in Chil. VII, may still appear under other authors; not verified. (3) О. В. Смыка (smyka.persona.msu.ru, checked): he translated only the Carmina Iliaca (Аристей 2021; Черновики переводов 2022; МГУ 2023), nothing from the Chiliades. I found no complete or substantial Russian Chiliades and no Russian version of Chiliad I or the Alexander histories, but Russian searching remains incomplete.
item_079.en_found: One full English translation exists. It is a volunteer team project sponsored by mitologia.pt (Otilio Silva): A. Untila (I), G. Berkowitz (II–IV), K. Ramiotis (V–VI), V. Dogani (VII–VIII), J. Alexander (IX–X), M. S. Fadhlurrahman (XI) and N. Giallousis (XII–XIII), made from Kiessling 1826. It was uploaded to archive.org on 2015-03-21 (https://archive.org/details/TzetzesCHILIADES) as 'the first English translation', under licence CC BY-NC-ND 3.0, and is also on theoi.com (https://www.theoi.com/Text/TzetzesChiliades1.html, all 13 books). ToposText 617 (https://topostext.org/work/617) indexes it and reports that permission to use a corrected version was refused. It has minimal notes and was not peer-reviewed. The DOML Tzetzes volumes (Goldwyn & Kokkini 2015, 2019) are the Allegories, not the Chiliades. I found no other English translation, scholarly or partial, but search was limited.
item_079.other_found: Latin: a full word-for-word version by Paulus Lacisius of Verona accompanied Gerbel's editio princeps (Basel, 1546), as Kiessling's 1826 preface confirms. Kiessling's own edition prints the Greek only, with notes. French, German, Italian, Spanish and modern Greek: the bibliographies of fr/de/it/es/el.wikipedia list editions only (Gerbel 1546, Kiessling 1826, Leone 1968) and no translations. Pietro Leone's Italian volume of 2015 is the Carmina Iliaca, not the Chiliades. I could not run catalogue searches, so modern partial translations into these languages remain unverified.
item_079.source_text: Public domain: Th. Kiessling, Ioannis Tzetzae Historiarum variarum Chiliades graece (Lipsiae: Vogel, 1826), at https://archive.org/details/historiarumvari00kiesgoog and Google Books dG0GAAAAQAAJ. It is based on two Munich manuscripts. The standard critical edition is P. L. M. Leone, Ioannis Tzetzae Historiae (Napoli: Libreria Scientifica, 1968; 2nd ed. Galatina: Congedo, 2007), which is in copyright, is used by the TLG, and numbers its lines slightly differently. Translate from Kiessling, check Leone's readings in the commentary, and cite both line numberings.
item_079.research_yield: Tzetzes' source-work (Ctesias, Diodorus, Lycophron scholia); Byzantine Alexander lore (Bucephalus I.28; Books VI–VIII) versus the Romance tradition; fragments preserved only here (Hipponax, Aristeas); 12th-c. scholarly self-presentation; Russian reference translation for classicists.
item_079.recommendation: Keep as a Russian-gap project, merged with its duplicate item_118. Lower the priority from 5 to 3: a full English translation exists, though an amateur and unannotated one, and the work is 12th-c. Byzantine rather than ancient. Best first unit: Chiliad I (histories 1–32, about 1,000 lines, Croesus through Xerxes, including Arion, Stesichorus, Simonides and Bucephalus), after first checking which passages Попова translated on pp. 252–259 of the 1969 anthology.

item_080.title_short: George of Pisidia, Heraclian poems + Hexaemeron (Bellum Avaricum)
item_080.ru_found:
I found no complete Russian translation of any of the poems, so the right verdict is "excerpts only", not "partial". Searches I could not run: the WebSearch budget was used up (200/200), so none of the 4 RU + 4 EN queries went through. Everything below comes from cached project data and direct page fetches.
(1) С.А. Иванов, excerpts of Bellum Avaricum, Heraclias and In restitutionem S. Crucis, mainly the passages about Slavs and Avars. Published in Свод древнейших письменных известий о славянах, т. II (М., 1995), pp. 65–75. Source: footnote 9 of Т.А. Нестеренко, «Император Ираклий в поэзии Георгия Писиды», Классическая и византийская традиция 2017, pp. 365–368 (full text cached in my scratchpad as kvt2017.txt). Vostlit has Иванов's Synkellos excerpt from the same Свод volume but no Pisides page; I checked the Г and П indexes.
(2) А.Д. Сиротенко, «Менандр и Писида: к вопросу об изображении императора Ираклия», ВВ 73 (2014), 62–72. Contains excerpts of Heraclias and In restitutionem S. Crucis.
(3) Нестеренко 2017 itself translates about 7 lines of Heraclias (on Dvin), using the PG 92 text. It states plainly that there is no full Russian translation of Pisides («отсутствие полнотекстового перевода»).
(4) Диакон Владимир Василик, «Тема войны в византийской гимнографии», pravoslavie.ru/35738.html (21.06.2010). Verse translations of 3 short passages of Bellum Avaricum (Scylla/Charybdis, the naval battle, the Virgin as strategos). The ru.wikipedia article on the siege of 626 quotes this translation.
(5) Probable but not checked: М.В. Бибиков, Byzantinorossica II (2009), from p. 81, likely has excerpts. The ru.wiki list of 7 works «в русских переводах (отрывки)» seems to follow it.
(6) Hexaemeron: there is no modern Russian translation. There is the medieval Slavonic translation by Dimitry Zograf (1385), «Похвала к Богу о сотворении всеа твари», ed. И.А. Шляпкин (СПб., 1882), per the Православная энциклопедия article (М.В. Бибиков).
The pilot unit, Bellum Avaricum (541 lines), is only partly touched: Иванов covers the Slav/monoxyla passages and Василик a few lines.
item_080.en_found: I found no complete English translation of any poem. Checked: en.wikipedia, which lists only the Tartaglia Italian; the Dumbarton Oaks Medieval Library volume list (Wikipedia, up to no. 89, and domedieval.org/volumes): no Pisides; the DOI of the colleague's source, which resolves to H. Leppin, "George Pisides' Expeditio Persica and Discourses on Warfare", in Hadjittofi & Lefteratou (eds.), The Genres of Late Antique Christian Poetry (De Gruyter 2020), a study. Translated passages do exist in studies: Mary Whitby 1994, 1998, 2002 and 2003; Howard-Johnston, Witnesses to a World Crisis (2010); M. Hurbanič, The Avar Siege of Constantinople in 626 (Palgrave 2019), cited on en.wikipedia for Pisides' troop figure. Greatrex & Lieu 2002 probably also has excerpts (from memory, not checked). Mango & Scott's Theophanes (1997) translates Theophanes' prose paraphrases of Pisides. Not checked because searches were blocked: whether a TTH or other volume by Mary Whitby has appeared or is announced. Confirm this before committing to an English edition.
item_080.other_found: Italian, complete: A. Pertusi, Giorgio di Pisidia, Poemi I. Panegirici epici (Studia Patristica et Byzantina 7, Ettal 1959): text, translation and commentary of Exp. Pers., Bell. Avar., Heraclias and the shorter panegyrics. L. Tartaglia, Carmi di Giorgio di Pisidia (UTET, Torino 1998): all the poems, with facing Italian. F. Gonnelli, Giorgio di Pisidia, Esamerone (Pisa, ETS 1998): text, Italian translation and commentary. Italian partial: M. Broggini, annotated anthology of the Expeditio Persica, Porphyra 12 (2008). Latin: Querci 1777 = PG 92. German, French, Spanish: no full translation found (de, fr, es and it Wikipedia list none). German studies with translated passages: Speck 1980, van Dieten 1985, C. Ludwig 1991. Old Church Slavonic: Hexaemeron (1385, Dimitry Zograf).
item_080.source_text: Standard critical texts: Pertusi 1959 for the three epic panegyrics; Tartaglia 1998 for all the poems; Gonnelli 1998 for the Hexaemeron. The translations and commentaries are in copyright (Pertusi died 1979, so his work is protected to about 2049). The Italian 20-year right in critical editions (L. 633/1941 art. 85-quater) has expired for Pertusi but not yet for the 1998 editions. Public-domain Greek: Migne, PG 92 (= Querci 1777), with checked PDFs at Documenta Catholica Omnia (http://www.documentacatholicaomnia.eu/30_20_0600-0650-_Georges_Pisides.html): Exp. Pers. cols. 1197–1260, Bell. Avar. 1259–1294, Heraclias 1297–1334. Also I. Bekker, CSHB (Bonn 1836), and L. Sternbach, Carmina inedita, WSt 13–14 (1891–92). I did not check scan URLs for these two, and the Bibliotheca Augustana Pisides pages could not be reached. Recommended method: translate from Pertusi's text and line numbers; publish the PD PG/Bekker Greek with the variants noted.
item_080.research_yield: Heraclius as a new Alexander (Heraclias), read against the Syriac Alexander Legend. The Theotokos as strategos: Bellum Avaricum, the Akathist and Theodore Synkellos. Slavs and monoxyla in 626. Pisides as a source for Theophanes. Greek Hexaemeron compared with the 1385 Slavonic version.
item_080.recommendation: Keep at top priority: there is no full Russian or English translation, only excerpts. Best first unit: Bellum Avaricum complete (541 lines, Pertusi numbering), with commentary set against Иванов's Свод excerpts, Synkellos and the Chronicon Paschale. Then Heraclias, for the Alexander theme. Re-check English (Whitby/TTH) and post-2017 Russian work (Сиротенко) once search access returns.

item_081.title_short: Anonymous, Byzantine Alexander Poem (Marc. gr. 408), Book I opening
item_081.ru_found:
I found no Russian translation, full or partial, and the RU "none" claim stands. The WebSearch budget for this run was already used up (shared limit of 200 per turn), so I could not run fresh general searches. This verdict rests on a cached full verification (research/raw/alexander.json) plus direct fetches I made in this run.

From the cache:
- CyberLeninka, 8 Russian queries, including «поэма об Александре», «византийская поэма Александр», «Александрия византийская», «Псевдо-Каллисфен» and «поэма об Александре 1388». No hit on Marc. gr. 408. The only Byzantine Alexander item is Degg 2023, a review of Kaldellis, not a translation.
- facetia.ru, vostlit.info indices А/В and ru.wikipedia «Роман об Александре»: nothing.

Fetched in this run:
- facetia.ru/alexander-romances notes only that one of the 13th–14th c. Byzantine reworkings was «стихотворная». It gives no translation, no 1388 date and no Marcianus 408.
- Near-miss checked at facetia.ru/node/4804: Т. В. Попова, «Повесть о подвигах Александра», in «Памятники византийской литературы IX–XV вв.» (М.: Наука, 1968/69). It is PROSE (Troy, the letter to Jerusalem, the prophet Jeremiah), translated from Веселовский, «Из истории романа и повести» I (1886). It is not the 1388 verse poem.

Not checked: elibrary.ru dissertations, РГБ/РНБ catalogues, and Yandex (blocked by CAPTCHA).
item_081.en_found:
I found no English translation, and the EN "none" claim stands.

- Aerts, The Byzantine Alexander Poem (De Gruyter 2014, 2 vols, doi 10.1515/9781614513070). Crossref metadata, re-fetched this run, has no translation field. The cached Crossref chapter list shows:
  - vol. 1: Introduction (pp. 1–32), Greek text Books I–III, indices;
  - vol. 2: a 14-page English Synopsis (pp. 253–266) and Commentary (pp. 267–612).
  So there is a summary and commentary in English, but no translation.
- The commentary may render single lines in English. I could not check this: the De Gruyter page returned HTTP 405 and the PDFs are bot-blocked.
- Aerts, Quaerendo 41 (2011), and Matzukis, BZ 80 (1987) and BZ 99 (2006), are studies only.
- Not in DOML. No BMCR review.
- Stoneman's Legends of Alexander the Great and his Penguin Greek Alexander Romance (recension L) do not include the poem.
- Possible scattered quotations: Jouanno 2012 (in The Alexander Romance in Persia and the East) and Moennig in Cupane–Krönung 2016. Not verified; at most these would be excerpts.

I could not run 4 fresh English web searches because the budget was exhausted.
item_081.other_found:
I found no translation into any other language.

- German: Reichmann 1963 (Beiträge zur klass. Philologie 13) is Greek text, apparatus and German introduction only. The cache checked the full OCR: no Übersetzung.
- Earlier partial editions, also untranslated: Kapp 1872 (vv. 1–199, 5569–5813, 6093–6118) and Legrand, Bibliothèque grecque vulgaire II (1881), vv. 1–772.
- Italian: Gonzato, BZ 56 (1963), is a dating study only.
- French near-miss: Jouanno, Histoire merveilleuse du roi Alexandre (Anacharsis 2009) translates recension γ, not this poem (BMCR 2010.01.52). Jouanno's Naissance et métamorphoses du Roman d'Alexandre (2002) probably quotes the poem in French, but at most as excerpts (not verified).
- Modern Greek: nothing found (didaktorika.gr checked in the cache). Treat this as unknown rather than proven absent.
item_081.source_text:
Best public-domain text:
- W. Wagner (ed., posthumously by D. Bikelas), Trois poèmes grecs du moyen-âge inédits (Berlin: S. Calvary 1881), pp. 56–241.
- Available at archive.org/details/troispomesgrecs00wagngoog (NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT) and phaidrabg.bg.ac.rs/o:588 (CC BY 2.0 AT, 28 MB PDF), both confirmed this run.
- Weaknesses noted by Reichmann: no apparatus, unmarked conjectures, normalised vernacular forms, omitted verses.

For the pilot vv. 1–772 there is a second public-domain witness: Legrand, Bibliothèque grecque vulgaire II (1881). Kapp 1872 also covers vv. 1–199.

In-copyright editions to collate against:
- Reichmann 1963 (Hain, Meisenheim; Leiden thesis scan at archive.org/details/IA41536505_0041, with no rights field). The 25-year German protection for scholarly editions (§70 UrhG) has probably lapsed for the constituted text. The introduction and apparatus remain protected.
- Aerts 2014 (De Gruyter): the current critical text, fully in copyright, not open access.

Translate from Wagner and record Reichmann's and Aerts's readings in the notes. Correction to the sweep: "No open digital text found" is wrong, and Aerts counts 6,130 verses.
item_081.recommendation: Keep: the poem is untranslated in Russian, English and, as far as found, every other language, and it sits squarely in the editor's Alexander Romance specialism. The best first unit is Book I vv. 1–772 (proem, Nectanebo, birth), translated from Wagner 1881 and checked against Legrand 1881, Reichmann and Aerts. That way the pilot rests on two public-domain witnesses.

item_082.title_short: Pseudo-Scymnus, Periodos to Nicomedes (prologue + non-Pontic sections)
item_082.ru_found: The claim that the proposed unit is untranslated is REFUTED for its Pontic half. (1) V. V. Latyshev, Scythica et Caucasica / Известия древних писателей греческих и латинских о Скифии и Кавказе, т. I (Греческие писатели), СПб. 1890–1893(–1900). I checked the archive.org scan directly (https://archive.org/details/IzvestiiaDrevnikhPisateleiGrecheskikhILatinskikhOSkifiUKavkaz, OCR file Latyshev1_djvu.txt). It has a section headed «ΑΝΩΝΥΜΟΥ [ΣΚΥΜΝΟΥ ΤΟΥ ΧΙΟΥ, ὡς φέρεται] ΠΕΡΙΗΓΗΣΙΣ» (Аноним [Скимн Хиосский, как полагают], Землеописание). It gives the Greek with a facing Russian translation and notes, beginning at v. 767 (Istros) and running through the north and east Pontic coast, the Maeotis/Bosporus and Colchis to about v. 1016–1026, i.e. the end of the verse text. Strabo follows directly. The pages are about I, 87–96; the project cache says 87–91, and I did not confirm the exact range. This is roughly 25% of the poem. (2) The same translation was reprinted with commentary in ВДИ 1947–1948 («Известия древних писателей о Скифии и Кавказе», a serial reprint), which is confirmed indirectly. A vostlit note to the Anonymous Periplus Ponti Euxini (ВДИ 1948 № 4, translated by Штерн/Латышев/Прозоров, https://www.vostlit.info/Texts/Dokumenty/Byzanz/VI/Pseudo_Arrian/frametext1.htm) refers to «снабженных в данном издании подробным комментарием периплов Псевдо-Скилака и Псевдо-Скимна». (3) That Anonymous Periplus, which preserves the prose paraphrase and verse fragments of the lost end of Ps.-Scymnus, is itself in Russian in the same series. (4) ru.wikipedia «Псевдо-Скимн» lists no Russian translation, and its bibliography is all EN/DE/FR. No Russian translation of the prologue (vv. 1–138) or of the western and Greek sections (vv. 139–766) was found: not in the project cache (ru_series_crosscheck.json, which comes from a vostlit crawl and series lists) and not in the Latyshev scan, which starts at v. 767, so the West Pontic Thracian cities (vv. ~720–766) are not covered. LIMITATION: the session's WebSearch budget was used up before my first query, so the required 4 Russian and 4 English searches could not be run (cyberleninka/elibrary/Аристей/ΣΧΟΛΗ/Hyperboreus/РГБ not searched). A recent modern Russian full or partial translation, for example in a journal, cannot be ruled out.
item_082.en_found: Full English exists three times over. (1) D. G. J. Shipley, "The Nikomedean Periodos ['Pseudo-Skymnos']", ch. 17 of Geographers of the Ancient Greek World: Selected Texts in Translation (CUP 2024), pp. 466–500. This is a new annotated translation; I verified it on the cambridge.org chapter page (doi 10.1017/9781009194211.022). It is not open access. (2) D. W. Roller, Three Ancient Geographical Treatises in Translation: Hanno, the King Nikomedes Periodos, and Avienus (Routledge 2021), chapter doi 10.4324/9781003030379-3. The DOI resolves to a Taylor & Francis chapter, but the page returned 403, so I verified the contents only from the DOI and the sweep. (3) B. Kiesling, "Pseudo Scymnus or Pausanias of Damascus, Circuit of the Earth", an unedited English translation on ToposText, cited by en.wikipedia "Pseudo-Scymnus".
item_082.other_found: French: D. Marcotte, Les Géographes grecs I: Pseudo-Scymnos, Circuit de la terre (CUF, Les Belles Lettres 2000), text plus full French translation. en.wikipedia confirms it as "standard text, with a French translation". German: M. Korenjak, Die Welt-Rundreise eines anonymen griechischen Autors ("Pseudo-Skymnos") (Olms 2003), Greek–German, from memory and not verified this session. Related studies, not translations: Boshnakov 2004 (Palingenesia 82) and Bravo 2009 (Studia Hellenistica 46). Latin: a facing Latin version in Müller, GGM I (1855), public domain. Bulgarian translations of the Thracian and West Pontic passages in the «Извори за старата история и география на Тракия и Македония» series probably exist, but this is unverified. No Italian or Spanish version was found; not searched.
item_082.source_text: Public-domain texts: (1) C. Müller, Geographi Graeci Minores I (Paris: Didot 1855), "Anonymi [vulgo Scymni Chii] Orbis descriptio", with a Latin version (archive.org scans exist; the exact pages, about 196–237, are from memory). (2) A. Meineke, Scymni Chii et Dionysii descriptio Graeciae (Berlin 1846). (3) For vv. 767–end: Latyshev, Scythica et Caucasica I (1893), with the Greek text revised (https://archive.org/details/IzvestiiaDrevnikhPisateleiGrecheskikhILatinskikhOSkifiUKavkaz). The standard modern editions are in copyright: Marcotte 2000 (CUF), Korenjak 2003 and Diller 1952 (The Tradition of the Minor Greek Geographers; copyright status uncertain). Base the translation on Müller and Meineke and check readings against Marcotte by citation only.
item_082.research_yield: Several article topics: the prologue's poetics (iambic didactic verse after Apollodorus, the source list, royal patronage under Nicomedes); colonization foundation dates compared with Eusebius and Ephorus; the western Greek colonies; the date and authorship debate (Pausanias of Damascus vs Semos); and the reception of Ephorus and Demetrius of Callatis.
item_082.recommendation: Keep only as a Russian-first candidate at priority 3. English (three versions), French and German are complete, and the Pontic half of the proposed pilot is already in Russian (Latyshev 1893, reprinted in ВДИ 1947–48). Best first unit: the prologue (vv. 1–138) plus the western Mediterranean and Greek sections up to the West Pontic cities (vv. 139–766), which have no Russian translation. Translating the whole poem would replace Latyshev's 1893 Pontic rendering.

item_083.ru_found: Only excerpts exist in Russian, so the sweep's 'partial' should be 'excerpts_only'. (1) Latyshev, Scythica et Caucasica: Scythia/Caucasus snippets from the poems and from the scholia in Nicandrum, reprinted in ВДИ 1947 №3, pp. 302–303 (listed on ru.wikipedia 'Никандр Колофонский'; also cached in ru_series_crosscheck.json, overlap 'partial', noted as 'unit essentially free'). (2) Two epigrams by Nicander in «Греческая эпиграмма» (Литературные памятники, СПб.: Наука, 1993), p. 296; these are not part of the unit. No full or continuous Russian translation of either poem or of the scholia was found. ancientrome.ru/antlitr has no Nicander page. Bolgov's Belgorod guide (simposium.ru node 14067) covers historians only, and ru.wikisource has no author page. LIMITATION: WebSearch returned 'budget exhausted (200/turn)' on every query, so none of the 4 Russian (and 4 English) searches were run. Direct fetches and the project caches were used instead. NOT checked: cyberleninka/elibrary journals (Аристей, ΣΧΟΛΗ, Hyperboreus, Philologia Classica), RSL/NLR catalogues, history-of-medicine readers, and the contents of «Александрийская поэзия» (1972) and «Эллинские поэты» (Ладомир 1999).
item_083.en_found: Full, and free online. (1) A.S.F. Gow & A.F. Scholfield, Nicander: The Poems and Poetical Fragments (CUP 1953): both poems with a prose translation. It is reproduced on attalus.org, which states 'This translation is by A.S.F.Gow & A.F.Scholfield (1953)': Theriaca at https://www.attalus.org/poetry/theriaca.html and Alexipharmaca, all 630 lines, at https://www.attalus.org/poetry/nicander.html. (2) F. Overduin, Nicander of Colophon's Theriaca: A Literary Commentary (Brill 2014/15, doi 10.1163/9789004283602, confirmed via Crossref): Theriaca only. No English translation of the scholia (Keil/Crugnola on the Theriaca, Bussemaker/Geymonat on the Alexipharmaca) was found, but because of the search outage this is unverified.
item_083.other_found: French: J.-M. Jacques, CUF (Les Belles Lettres), t. II Les Thériaques (2002) and t. III Les Alexipharmaques (2007), with text, translation and notes (fr.wikipedia). Italian: G. Spatafora, Nicandro, Theriaká e Alexiphármaka (Carocci, Roma 2007); V. Gigante Lanzara, Theriaka. Alexipharmaka (Olschki, Firenze 2022) (it.wikipedia). Latin: Gorraeus, Paris (fr.wiki gives a 1622 copy); Didot 1862, Poetae bucolici et didactici (Ameis/Lehrs), Greek–Latin, archive.org poetaebucoliciet00amei. German and Spanish: not verified, because the search budget was exhausted. es.wikipedia lists no Spanish translation. Related editions: Eutecnius' prose paraphrases (Gualandri 1968; Geymonat 1976) and the scholia (Crugnola 1971; Geymonat 1974; Wentzel 1892 for the Göttingen scholia).
item_083.source_text: Best public-domain text: O. Schneider, Nicandrea. Theriaca et Alexipharmaca (Teubner, Leipzig 1856). It includes the scholia (Keil on the Theriaca, Bussemaker on the Alexipharmaca) and is marked NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT on archive.org, with PDF and full text (https://archive.org/details/theriacaetalexi00schngoog; also Google Books Lq1fAAAAMAAJ). Two more public-domain sources: Dübner/Bussemaker, Scholia et paraphrases in Nicandrum et Oppianum (Didot 1849), with the scholia and Eutecnius, and Didot 1862 (Greek–Latin). The standard modern editions are all in copyright: Gow–Scholfield 1953 (CUP), Jacques CUF 2002/2007, Crugnola 1971 and Geymonat 1974 for the scholia, and Gigante Lanzara 2022. So: translate from Schneider, and check the readings against Gow–Scholfield and Jacques.
item_083.research_yield: Possible articles: Nicander's toxicology against the Apollodorus–Galen–Aelius Promotus tradition; Hellenistic glossographic poetics and hapax legomena; a Russian nomenclature for ancient materia medica (plants and snakes); the Nicander scholia as evidence for ancient pharmacology; multi-model disagreement over obscure glosses.
item_083.recommendation: Keep only as a Russian-first candidate, at priority 3 rather than 4: English is complete and free online, and French plus two Italian translations exist, so 'first-ever' applies only in Russian. Best first unit: the whole Alexipharmaca (630 lines, from Schneider 1856), with the Bussemaker scholia on lines 1–185. Those scholia may be the genuinely first-in-any-modern-language part, which still needs a search check.

item_084.ru_found: Confirmed: (1) Ellinskie poety VIII–III vv. do n. e., ed. V. N. Yarkho (Moscow: Ladomir, 1999). It has 'Yamby', tr. O. V. Smyka and V. N. Yarkho, pp. 300–303, and 'Gekala', tr. Smyka, pp. 210–211. Source: ru.wikipedia 'Каллимах из Кирены'. (2) Smyka reprinted his pieces in O. V. Smyka, Perevody. Chernoviki perevodov (Moscow: Novyi khronograf, 2023), section 'Эллинские поэты', about pp. 119–131. Full text: smyka.persona.msu.ru/tr3.pdf, which I read via pdftotext. It contains only two pieces from the candidate: Hecale fr. 260 Pf. (= Hollis fr. 69–74, Theseus and the bull plus the crow's speech, about 69 lines), and Iambus 1 'Кубок Бафикла' (fr. 191, about lines 1–78 with gaps). It also has Branchus (fr. 229) and several Aetia pieces. Yarkho's share of pp. 300–303 could not be checked; it may be one more iambus or a few lines. (3) Golubets, Drevnegrecheskaya elegiya (1996), and Averintsev (Hymns, 1972) cover the Aetia and the Hymns only, not the Iambi or Hecale. ru.wikipedia 'Гекала' lists no translation. ancientrome.ru has no Callimachus entry. Fantlab lists only the 1999 pieces for Smyka. Nothing found for Iambi 2–13, Hecale beyond fr. 260, or the Diegeseis. Caveat: the WebSearch budget for this turn was already used up, so my two Russian keyword searches ('Каллимах Ямбы перевод', 'Каллимах Гекала перевод фрагменты') did not run. Journal articles (ВДИ, ΣΧΟΛΗ, Philologia Classica), dissertations and amateur online versions were therefore not checked.
item_084.en_found: Confirmed via ru.wikipedia and en.wikipedia. (1) Loeb LCL 421, 'Aetia, Iambi, Hecale and Other Fragments', tr. C. A. Trypanis (1958). Includes the Diegeseis. The 1975 revision is from memory. (2) F. Nisetich, The Poems of Callimachus (OUP 2001), a complete translation. (3) Kerkhecker, Callimachus' Book of Iambi (OUP 1999). (4) B. Acosta-Hughes, Polyeideia: The Iambi of Callimachus (UC Press 2002). (5) A. S. Hollis, Hecale (OUP 1990; 2nd ed. 2009), commentary. Whether it has a full facing translation is unverified. (6) Mair, LCL 129 (1921), with the Hecale fragments known then (Rainer tablet). Public domain. (7) Online: attalus.org/poetry/callimachus3.html, Hecale fr. 230–358 (46 fragments) adapted by Daniel Curley from Trypanis (2021). Also from memory, not re-checked: Lombardo & Rayor, Callimachus (Johns Hopkins 1988), selections.
item_084.other_found: Confirmed via ru.wikipedia. French: Y. Durbec, Callimaque, Fragments poétiques (Les Belles Lettres 2006), with the Iambi and Hecale; E. Cahen, Budé (1922), selected fragments. Italian: G. B. D'Alessio, Callimaco (BUR, 2 vols., 4th ed. 2007), the complete works including the Giambi, Ecale and Diegeseis. German: M. Asper, Kallimachos Werke, Greek–German (Darmstadt 2004). Italian, from the candidate file: E. Lelli 2005 on Iambi 14–17 (not the unit). From memory, unverified: German, Howald & Staiger (Artemis 1955); Spanish, L. A. de Cuenca & M. Brioso, Gredos BCG (1980). The unit is fully available in English, French, Italian and German.
item_084.source_text: Standard editions, all in copyright: R. Pfeiffer, Callimachus I: Fragmenta (Oxford 1949; Pfeiffer died 1979); Hollis, Hecale (2009); the Kerkhecker and Acosta-Hughes texts of the Iambi. No open digital text of the Iambi or Hecale found. Perseus/Scaife tlg0533 (CC BY-SA) has only the Hymns and Epigrams (Wilamowitz 1897; Mair 1921). poesialatina.it/_ns/greek/testi/Callimachus/Hecala.html has the Hecale Greek; the site was unreachable, so its base edition is unknown. Public-domain building blocks: Hunt, P.Oxy. VII (1910; P.Oxy. 1011, Iambi), on archive.org (not opened); Gomperz 1893 (Rainer tablet); Mair, Loeb 1921; Schneider, Callimachea II (1873). From memory: Norsa–Vitelli, Diegeseis (1934), probably PD in the EU since Norsa's death (1952); Pfeiffer, Callimachi fragmenta nuper reperta (1921/23), US-PD. Practical route: translate from Pfeiffer and Kerkhecker, publishing the Greek only as short lemmata or as a newly built papyrus text.
item_084.research_yield: First Russian Iambi with Diegeseis: Iamb 13 and polyeideia; the Hipponactean persona; Iamb 6 and Pheidias' Zeus; Iamb 4 as fable-agon; the Diegeseis as ancient hypotheses; Hecale's theoxeny and Ovid's Baucis; why Russian scholarship of the Hellenistic period has neglected Callimachus' fragmentary works.
item_084.recommendation: Keep at reduced priority. Russian has essentially nothing beyond Iambus 1 and Hecale fr. 260, but English, French, Italian and German are all complete and the critical text is in copyright. Best first unit: Iambi 2–13 with Diegeseis VI–X (all untranslated in Russian), plus a fresh Iambus 1 for completeness, translated from Pfeiffer and Kerkhecker with brackets checked strictly.

item_085.ru_found: Only one Russian translation was confirmed: excerpts by M. E. Grabar-Passek in Памятники поздней античной поэзии и прозы II–V века (М.: Наука, 1964), pp. 34–39. The source is ru.wikipedia 'Оппиан', which does not say which poem the excerpts come from. Six pages is at most about 150–200 lines, against about 3,500 hexameters in the Halieutica. No full or book-length Russian translation was found. Other checks: ru.wikipedia 'Галиевтика' is about Ovid's Halieutica (Gasparov 1978), not Oppian. O. V. Smyka's translation volumes (smyka.persona.msu.ru, 2022–2023) include Manasses' verse Life of Oppian (2016/2023), Triphiodorus, Colluthus and Philes, but no Oppian text is listed. The project cache (ru_series_crosscheck) flags possible Pontic excerpts in Latyshev's Известия древних писателей о Скифии и Кавказе (ВДИ 1947–48). I could not confirm this, because the Wikisource and Wikipedia URLs returned 404. IMPORTANT: the shared WebSearch budget was already used up when this agent started, so none of the required Russian or English searches ran. Checks were limited to direct WebFetch of known pages and the local cache. Online amateur translations, journal articles in ВДИ/Аристей/Hyperboreus and dissertations remain unchecked.
item_085.en_found: A. W. Mair, Oppian, Colluthus, Tryphiodorus, Loeb Classical Library 219 (London: Heinemann, 1928). It gives a full prose translation facing the Greek, and archive.org has it: https://archive.org/details/oppiancolluthust00oppiuoft. en.wikipedia 'Oppian' also lists an 18th-century English verse translation by Diaper and Jones (Oxford, 1722). No modern English translation after Mair was found, but searches could not be run. Kneebone's CUP 2020 monograph is a study, not a translation.
item_085.other_found: German: Fritz Fajen, 'Oppianus Halieutica – Oppian der Fischfang' (Stuttgart/Leipzig: Teubner, 1999). It has an introduction, Greek text and a German translation (confirmed by de.wikipedia 'Oppian'). Spanish: Carmen Calvo Delcán, Opiano, De la caza / De la pesca (Madrid: Gredos 134, 1990), 415 pp. (confirmed by ru.wikipedia). Latin: Lorenzo Lippi's verse version (1478; Aldine 1517), plus Rittershusius 1597 and Schneider 1776. Italian (Salvini, 18th c.) and French (Limes, 1817) versions are known from memory only and were not confirmed here.
item_085.source_text: The best usable public-domain Greek text is Mair's Loeb (1928) on archive.org (oppiancolluthust00oppiuoft; doi 10.5962/bhl.title.30404). Published in 1928 and Mair died in 1928, so it is US public domain and also out of copyright under life+70. Older public-domain editions: Lehrs (Didot, Paris 1846), Schneider (1776) and Rittershusius (1597), whose 1597 edition prints the Tzetzes scholia. Scholia: Bussemaker (Didot, 1849). The standard modern critical edition is Fajen 1999 (Teubner, now De Gruyter) and is in copyright. Use it only for checking readings, not as the base text. An openly licensed TEI text from First1KGreek/Perseus (tlg0023.tlg001) probably exists, but I could not confirm it (GitHub 404, Scaife blocked).
item_085.research_yield: Possible articles: Oppian as a source on Black Sea and Pontic fisheries (with Bosporan salting-site archaeology); fish-name identification against Thompson; the 'sympathy' and dolphin narratives; Oppian versus Ovid's Halieutica (Gasparov); imperial court didactic poetry for the Antonines; Byzantine reception (scholia, Manasses' Life, Philes).
item_085.recommendation: Keep as a Russian-only first translation. The Russian gap is real at the level of whole books, but English, German and Spanish translations exist, so the 'first-ever' claim holds only for Russian. Start with Book 1 (about 800 lines, with the proem to the emperor). First check the Grabar-Passek 1964 pp. 34–39 excerpts and Latyshev for overlap, and rerun the web searches that could not be done here.

item_086.ru_found: No Russian translation found. This check is limited: the shared web-search budget ran out on my first query, so neither of my searches returned results (1 Russian: «Максим "О начинаниях" астрологическая поэма перевод»; 1 English). I could not run the required 4+4 searches. Checked directly instead: (1) ru.wikipedia «Максим Эфесский» does not mention the poem and says his astrological works are lost, with no Russian translations cited; (2) the ancientrome.ru/antlitr author index has no Maximus the astrologer; (3) the project's cache (wave1, wave2, ru_series_crosscheck) has no Russian evidence for this poem. My background knowledge agrees: no Russian translation of any Greek catarchic poem is known in Литпамятники, ВДИ, ΣΧΟΛΗ or Аристей. Still to search: cyberleninka and elibrary for «Максим Περὶ καταρχῶν», «катархическая астрология», «Максим Эфесский астролог».
item_086.en_found: No English translation found, but this was not confirmed by search because the search budget was exhausted. Direct checks: en.wikipedia 'Maximus of Ephesus' cites only Zito's French (2016) and Radici Colace's Italian paraphrase volume (1988), with no English. en.wikipedia 'Electional astrology' names only Dorotheus. From background knowledge, I know of no version in Loeb, Project Hindsight (Schmidt) or Cazimi Press (Dykes and Gramaglia translated Hephaestion III 'On Inceptions' and Dorotheus, not Maximus). Short excerpts quoted in secondary literature are possible but unverified.
item_086.other_found: French, complete: N. Zito, Maxime, Des initiatives (Perì katarchôn), CUF, Les Belles Lettres, Paris 2016, 336 pp., text and translation (cited on en.wikipedia and fr.wikipedia). The colleague's CUF series number 521 is not re-verified. Italian: P. Radici Colace, Le parafrasi bizantine del Perì katarchôn di Massimo: critical text, translation and commentary, EDAS, Messina 1988, ISBN 8878200271. That volume translates the Byzantine prose and verse paraphrases, not necessarily the poem itself. No German, Spanish or older Latin translation identified; Ludwich 1877 appears to be text-only with a Latin apparatus.
item_086.source_text: Ludwich, Maximi et Ammonis carminum De actionum auspiciis reliquiae. Accedunt Anecdota astrologica (Teubner, Leipzig 1877), public domain. Scan: https://archive.org/details/maximietammonis00ludwgoog (metadata NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT; Google Books id qHYCAAAAYAAJ). It contains the poem (610 vv. in Ludwich's numbering) under twelve headings: I On birth, II Purchase of slaves, III Sailing and trade, IV Travel, V Marriage, VI Diseases, VII Surgery, VIII Runaway slaves, IX Children's schooling, X Agriculture, XI Prisoners, XII Theft. Sections I–III appear in the verse text as headings only; their content survives only in the Byzantine prose metaphrasis, which Ludwich also prints, along with the fragments of Ammon. The archive.org OCR of the Greek is unusable, so the text needs re-keying or TLG. The standard modern edition, Zito CUF 2016, is in copyright, as is Radici Colace 1988; use them only for collation and checking.
item_086.research_yield: Possible articles: electional astrology and slavery (buying slaves, runaways, prisoners, theft); surgery and schooling timed by the Moon; the poem's relation to Dorotheus V and Hephaestion III; the Orphic 'Works and Days'; the attribution to Maximus of Ephesus; Nectanebo's timing of Alexander's birth (Alexander Romance 1.12).
item_086.recommendation: Keep at priority 4: very likely a first translation into both Russian and English, from a public-domain Greek text of manageable size. Best first unit: the whole verse text (vv. 1–610, Ludwich) plus the prose paraphrase of the lost sections I–III, checked against Zito. If it must be split, start with V (marriage) and VIII (runaway slaves). Before committing, rerun the 4 Russian and 4 English searches (cyberleninka, elibrary, Google Books, BMCR).

item_087.ru_found: REFUTED: the claim of no Russian translation is wrong. O. V. Smyka has translated all three poems into Russian. (1) Antehomerica as «Иоанн Цец. До Гомера»: Аристей XXIV, pp. 189–203 (the project cache gives the year as 2020 in one record and 2021 in another), reprinted in Смыка О. В., Исследования и переводы, М.: Изд-во МГУ, 2023, pp. 126–137 (https://smyka.persona.msu.ru/tr2.pdf). (2) Homerica + Posthomerica as «Иоанн Цец. По Гомеру и После Гомера»: Смыка О. В., Черновики переводов, М.: Новый хронограф, 2022, pp. 283–324, marked as a draft (https://smyka.persona.msu.ru/tr1.pdf). I checked these directly today against the publication list on Smyka's own site (smyka.persona.msu.ru); the tables of contents of both books list them. ru.wikipedia 'Иоанн Цец' (fetched today) cites both. It also cites the 1969 excerpts (Памятники византийской литературы IX–XIV вв., pp. 252–259), which are not of this work. Two things I could not open because the PDF is over 10 MB: whether every one of the 407 Antehomerica lines is rendered, and whether Tzetzes' scholia are included. The page count suggests the poem text is complete and the scholia are not. Limitation: the shared WebSearch budget was used up, so I ran no new Russian searches. The evidence comes from the project's earlier verified cross-checks (wave1_critic.json, ru_series_crosscheck.json, 02_candidates.md), confirmed by direct fetches of the sources.
item_087.en_found: Volunteer translation of all three poems by Ana Untila for mitologia.pt, on the Internet Archive since 2014. It was translated from F. Jacobs' 1793 Greek edition and is licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. It has no scholia and no introduction or commentary. I read the front matter of the Antehomerica full text: line markers run to 405, but the numbering is irregular. Links: https://archive.org/details/TzetzesANTEHOMERICA, https://archive.org/details/TzetzesHOMERICA, https://archive.org/details/TzetzesPOSTHOMERICA. All three are linked from en.wikipedia 'John Tzetzes'. I found no peer-reviewed English translation; the DOML volumes by Goldwyn and Kokkini cover the Allegories, not this work. New English searches could not run because the search budget was used up.
item_087.other_found: de.wikipedia lists only Leone's 1995 critical edition and no translations. I could not verify any Italian, French, German or Spanish translation; no search was possible. I believe Leone 1995 has no facing Italian translation, but this is unverified. A Greek–Latin version may exist in the Didot volume (Lehrs, c. 1840) alongside Quintus Smyrnaeus; this comes from memory and is unverified.
item_087.source_text: Public domain: F. Jacobs (ed.), Ioannis Tzetzae Antehomerica, Homerica et Posthomerica, Leipzig 1793, on Google Books (https://books.google.com/books?id=oTQOAAAAYAAJ, linked from en.wikipedia); I. Bekker (ed.), Berlin 1816 (public domain; URL not checked). Standard critical edition: P. A. M. Leone, Ioannis Tzetzae Carmina Iliaca, Catania: CULC 1995. It is in copyright and is the main source for Tzetzes' own scholia on the poems.
item_087.research_yield: Low for a translation. Smyka covers all three poems in Russian (Antehomerica in a journal) and Untila covers them in English. The only possible gap left is Tzetzes' own scholia on the Carmina Iliaca, as a study of Byzantine classroom method. That depends on Leone's copyrighted 1995 text.
item_087.recommendation: Drop it as a candidate. Russian is effectively complete through Smyka (Antehomerica in Аристей, reprinted by МГУ in 2023; Homerica and Posthomerica as a 2022 draft), and English is complete in a volunteer version. If anything is kept, it would be only Tzetzes' scholia on the Antehomerica, after first checking that Smyka did not translate them and that the copyrighted Leone 1995 text may be used.

item_088.ru_found: No Russian translation found, but the check was incomplete. The session's WebSearch budget was used up, so none of the required search-engine queries ran (0 of 4 RU, 0 of 4 EN). I used direct page fetches and the project cache instead. (1) ru.wikipedia «Манефон» names «Апотелесматика (Ἀποτελεσματικά) — астрологическое сочинение в 6 книгах» but gives no translation. Псевдо-Манефон» (node 10148) is the Letter to Ptolemy Philadelphus, not the poem. (3) The ancientrome.ru antlitr author index has no Manetho. item_088.source_text: Best public-domain text: A. Koechly, Manethonis Apotelesmaticorum qui feruntur libri VI (Leipzig: Teubner, 1858), digitised in the usual repositories (Google Books, archive.org, MDZ); I did not fetch a URL this session. Koechly's Didot edition (1851, with Latin) and Axt & Rigler (1832) are also public domain. The standard modern edition is Lightfoot (OUP 2020/2023), which is in copyright. It revises the text and groups the books by date (2-3-6, then 4-1-5). Book and line numbering must be matched against Koechly. Translating from Koechly is legally safe, but it is philologically dated, and following Lightfoot's text or English too closely risks a derivative work.
item_088.research_yield: Articles on astrological catalogues as evidence for Roman Egyptian society (professions, slaves, marriage, sexual deviance, violent death); on the author's own horoscope (Book 6) and the dating of the layers; on didactic hexameter technique beside Dorotheus and Maximus; and on Egyptian/Hermetic sources.
item_088.recommendation: Keep at mid priority: it would be the first Russian translation, but Lightfoot's complete English edition with commentary already exists, so the English-side gain is nil. Good first unit: Book 4 (c. 600 lines, translated from Koechly 1858 and checked against Lightfoot), or the Book 6 proem plus the author's horoscope as a shorter pilot. Rerun the Russian journal and catalogue searches once the search budget allows.
