item_091.title_short: Manuel Philes, De animalium proprietate (opening c. 500 vv.)
item_091.ru_found:
The claim of no Russian translation is REFUTED. I checked O. V. Smyka's own list of publications for 1971–2023, printed in her "Переводы. Черновики переводов" (М.: Новый хронограф, 2023), pp. 553–557 (https://smyka.persona.msu.ru/tr3.pdf, text extracted and read). Relevant entries:
(1) No. 42, 2016: "Византийский поэт Мануил Фил. Из стихов о животных, адресованных императору Михаилу IX Палеологу", translated from Greek: the Введение (proem) and chs. 1 (eagles), 2 (vulture), 3 (kite) and 39 (martichoras). Труды каф. древних языков = Труды ист. ф-та МГУ, сер. III, т. 83 (М.: Индрик), pp. 270–276. Her introduction is on pp. 265–267 (no. 43). No. 44, pp. 268–270, is her translation from Latin of Arsenios of Monemvasia's paratext "...стихи ямбические... об особенностях животных".
(2) No. 37, 2015: "Из поэмы «О свойствах животных» (I, 80 ст.) «Об орлах»", in Ars docendi (М.: ПСТГУ), pp. 218–224.
(3) No. 24, 2009: "Мануил Фил. Стихи на разные темы", which includes «О свойствах животных» (chapters not specified), in Труды каф. древних языков, вып. II (М.: Индрик), pp. 251–263.
(4) Per earlier project research, the 2016 piece was reprinted in Смыка, "Исследования и переводы" (МГУ 2023), from p. 257 (tr2.pdf). I could not re-open that PDF (over 10 MB).
In total this is roughly 10% of the poem (my estimate), but it covers the proem and chs. 1–3, so the proposed opening unit overlaps directly. ru.wikipedia 'Мануил Фил' lists no translations, which is why the sweep missed this.
Caveat: the web-search budget was used up for this run, so none of the required 4 RU and 4 EN searches could be run. The evidence comes from cached project research (ru_series_crosscheck.json, wave1_critic.json) and direct fetches.

item_091.research_yield: Philes as an indirect witness to Aelian's and Oppian's text; how Palaiologan court poets reworked ancient natural history; chapters on Ctesian and Indian marvels (martichoras) and the Alexander-lore animals; the Vergikios illustrated manuscripts; comparing Philes' choices with Smyka's and Caramico's translations.
item_091.recommendation: Keep, but demote: the work is 14th-century, and Russian (Smyka: proem, chs. 1–3, 39) and Italian (Caramico 2006, part II) coverage both exist. Drop the opening-500-verses unit. Start after ch. 3 (e.g. chs. 4–38, skipping 39), once the contents of Smyka's 2009 selection and Caramico's part II chapter range have been checked.

item_092.title_short: Constantine Manasses, Synopsis Chronike (antiquity sections: Troy, Assyria–Persia–Alexander)
item_092.ru_found:
REFUTED IN PART. The sweep claimed there is "no modern Russian from the Greek". That is false: several Russian translations of fragments made from the Greek exist.
(1) О. В. Смыка, «Из „Хроники“ Константина Манассии», Труды кафедры древних языков III (Труды ист. ф-та МГУ), М.: Индрик, 2012, pp. 228–246. It covers vv. 1–143 (prologue and Creation), 2546–2554 and 6722–6733 (per ru.wikipedia, fetched). It was reprinted in Смыка, «Исследования и переводы» (М.: Изд-во МГУ, 2023), pp. 138–165; the contents were confirmed on smyka.persona.msu.ru. The same volume also has Manasses' Life of Oppian (p. 166) and his Hodoiporikon (p. 173; first published in Аристей XV, 2017).
(2) О. В. Бычков, «Культура Византии» (М., 1989), p. 438: about 20 lines (per ru.wikipedia).
(3) Д. Е. Афиногенов, ВДИ 1999 №1, pp. 137–145: vv. 4805–4830.
(4) Д. Полывяный in «Родник златоструйный» (М., 1990; vostlit rus6/Manassia): Russian of extracts from the Middle Bulgarian version. The project cache had checked this; its "Alexander" is Tsar Ivan Alexander.
(5) A cached crosscheck reports a Smyka passage in «Homo omnium horarum» (2020) marked "Synopsis 4908 ff.". It is unverified and the attribution looks doubtful.
(6) An 18th-c. Kantemir manuscript translation (Словесность и история 2020/1, pp. 176–180) is unpublished; I could not open the PDF because of a certificate error.
None of the verified fragments covers the Troy digression or the Assyria/Persia/Alexander section. However, I could not open the 2023 reprint (tr2.pdf is over 10 MB), and Smyka works heavily on Troy (Dares, Dictys, Triphiodorus), so this needs a check. The Slavonic «Троянская притча» in the Russian Chronograph (Творогов) is an Old Russian text, not a modern translation.
Search note: the shared WebSearch budget was exhausted before my first query. Findings come from direct fetches (ru.wikipedia, smyka.persona.msu.ru, vostlit) and the project cache (ru_series_crosscheck.json, alexander.json). The required 4+4 searches were not run.

The archive.org scan breviariumhisto00bekkgoog was verified, with full text and OCR; the OCR quality for the Greek is uneven. The same text is reprinted in Migne PG 127 (1864), also public domain.

item_092.research_yield: Manasses' Troy (Homeric versus Dictys–Malalas tradition) and its Slavonic afterlife in the «Троянская притча» and the Russian Chronograph. Best first unit: the Troy digression (c. 370 vv., roughly vv. 1100–1470 in Lampsidis, to be confirmed), after checking Smyka's 2023 reprint (pp. 138–165) for overlap.

item_093.title_short: Choricius of Gaza, Orations I–VIII (unit: Laudatio Marciani I)
item_093.ru_found:
REFUTED: the "none" claim is wrong. All eight orations exist in Russian by Н.Н. Болгов (with А.М. Болгова) in «Классическая и византийская традиция» (КВТ, Белгород, НИУ БелГУ):
- Or. I and II (Энкомий Маркиану I–II), Or. V (Эпиталамий Захарии) and Or. VI (Эпиталамий Прокопию, Иоанну и Элии): КВТ 2019, pp. 214–272. I checked the PDF directly (https://if.bsuedu.ru/upload/iblock/8e9/%5B%D0%9A%D0%92%D0%A2%2019%20%D0%B8%D1%82%D0%BE%D0%B3%5D.pdf). Or. I is complete (§§1–94, pp. 214–234) and includes the St Sergius ekphrasis (§§17–76). Or. II's outline includes the St Stephen ekphrasis (§§25–51).
- Or. III (Арат и Стефан), IV (Сумм) and VII (Мария): КВТ 2018, pp. 366–411.
- Or. VIII (Прокопий; Болгова и Болгов): КВТ 2017, pp. 421–436.
- Collected in «Мир поздней античности» вып. 16 (2020, 424 pp.) and in «Хорикий. Риторические сочинения» (Белгород: Эпицентр, 2022, 343/344 pp., ISBN 978-5-6049183-4-0; RSL record 01011623284), which the Византийский клуб almanac 2023 calls a complete translation of all works.
Also in Russian: the Brumalia speech (Болгов 2016), Dialexeis 2 and 5 (Сорокина и Болгов 2013), and extracts from the Apologia mimorum (Фрейберг 1968).
The Russian ru.wiki article, which the sweep relied on, is out of date.
Caveat: Bolgov's Or. I appears to be made via F.K. Litsas' English dissertation, not directly from the Greek. Its notes are translated Litsas commentary ("Cf. Chap. I, p. 13, esp. n. 5 (Litsas)", "Laud. Arat. et Steph., Comm. n. 1"), and the phrasing is calqued ("Ведите тогда свой путь, о речи").
Method: the web-search budget for this run was used up, so none of the required RU/EN searches could run. Evidence comes from the project cache (ru_series_crosscheck.json, wave1_critic.json) plus my direct fetch of the КВТ 2019 PDF.

item_093.recommendation: Drop: the work fails Neoscholia's first criterion. Or. I–VIII, including the pilot Or. I with the St Sergius ekphrasis, are fully published in Russian (Болгов, КВТ 2017–2019; book editions 2020 and 2022). If Gaza rhetoric is still wanted, consider a corrective from-Greek retranslation of Or. I §§17–76 only, as a secondary project.

This refutes the colleague's 'none'. About 12 of the 166/174 letters exist in Russian, all by the Belgorod group (Bolgov), all in Garzya–Loenertz/Amato numbering:
(1) Е.Е. Богомаз, Н.Н. Болгов, «Письма Прокопия Газского», Научные ведомости БелГУ. История. Политология 2017 №8(257), вып. 42, pp. 46–48: Ep. 1, 20, 74. The article claims to be the first Russian translation of any letter. https://cyberleninka.ru/article/n/pisma-prokopiya-gazskogo
(2) М.М. Синица, М.Ю. Лопатина, «Прокопий Газский. Письма (Ep. 2, 3)», Классическая и византийская традиция (КВТ) 2017, pp. 420–421. I verified this in the volume's text. The translation is very literal and awkward.
(3) Синица, Ep. 4–6, КВТ 2018, pp. 364–367. Confirmed via Синица's bibliography in КВТ 2019.
(4) Синица, Ep. 7–10, Эргастирий IV (Белгород 2020), pp. 88–91. From the project cache, which read the PDF.
(5) Синица, «Ранневизантийский эпистолограф Прокопий Газский. Письма 1–6», Кондаковские чтения VII (Белгород: Эпицентр 2022), pp. 255–282. I read this in the PDF. It translates the letters with Amato's commentary from Rose di Gaza, rendered from the Italian, and keeps machine-translation artefacts (e.g. «совершенный с приведенной стоимостью»). Синица states that no complete scholarly translation exists and hopes «все 174 письма» will follow. That makes the Belgorod group a possible competitor or partner.
Russian excerpts of other letters (e.g. Ep. 18, 77, 16) are quoted in Лопатина & Манохин, «Ранневизантийская Газа в Палестине» (Белгород 2022), and in А.М. Болгова's works (2014, 2015, 2018).
Not verified: «Прокопий Газский. Риторическо-софистические сочинения», Мир поздней античности. Документы и материалы вып. 15 (Белгород 2020, 106 pp.). The title suggests the opuscula, not the letters. The faculty publications page (if.bsuedu.ru/science/publication.php) lists no КВТ, Кондаковские or Альманах volumes after 2023. The 2021–2023 Альманах volumes and КВТ 2020–2021 contain no further letters.
Method: WebSearch was refused because the session's search budget (200 calls) was used up, so none of the required 4+4 Russian/English searches could be run. The evidence above comes from the project's ru_series_crosscheck cache (built from Belgorod PDFs), direct fetches of the PDFs, CyberLeninka, and ru.wikipedia.
item_094.en_found:
There is no scholarly English translation, but two complete machine translations are online. This upgrades the colleague's 'partial'. I class them 'full' with a caveat, as the cache did for the AI versions of Zonaras and Hilary:
(1) romanletters.org (Craig Vander Galien, 2026). It has all 166 letters (/authors/procopius-of-gaza/, e.g. /letters/procopius_gaza/1/ 'To Caesarius and Eubulus') in English made by Claude from OCR'd Greek of PG 87 (matia.gr PDF). Each page says it is AI-assisted and not peer-reviewed. The site gives the licence for data and translations as CC BY 4.0.
(2) Roger Pearse, 'Procopius of Gaza, Letters – machine translation now online with notes' (30 Apr 2026). This is Google Translate of Ciccolella's Italian translation (Amato, Rose di Gaza 2010, pp. 290–437), with selected notes run through DeepSeek. Pearse says it has 'no scholarly value'. It is on archive.org/details/procopius-of-gaza-letters-english-output and is linked from en.wikipedia. It is derivative of a copyrighted Italian translation.
English excerpts probably appear in studies (Westberg 2010; Downey; Christian Gaza in Late Antiquity 2004), but I could not check them because the search budget was used up.
item_094.other_found: Italian, full: F. Ciccolella (with Amato for Ep. 166 and 169–174) in E. Amato (ed.), Rose di Gaza: gli scritti retorico-sofistici e le Epistole di Procopio di Gaza (Hellenica 35, Edizioni dell'Orso 2010). It covers 174 letters, confirmed by BMCR 2011.10.10. Latin, full for its corpus: R. Hercher prints a facing Latin version with the 162 letters in Epistolographi Graeci (Paris 1873); PG 87.2, cols. 2717–2800, also has Greek–Latin (about 104 letters per ru.wiki). French: none found for the letters. item_094.source_text:
Public domain:
- R. Hercher, Epistolographi Graeci (Paris: Didot 1873), Greek with facing Latin. archive.org/details/epistolographoih00hercuoft, flagged NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT. I checked its OCR: it has 162 letters, and Hercher's Ep. 1 is to Nephalius.
- PG 87.2 (Greek and Latin, fewer letters).
NUMBERING TRAP: Hercher's order differs from Garzya–Loenertz (G-L). G-L Ep. 1 is to Caesarius and Eubulus. All modern scholarship, all the Russian translations and romanletters use G-L numbering, so the colleague's pilot ('Letters 1–40, Hercher numbering') does not match the existing literature. Use G-L numbering and a concordance.
Standard editions:
- A. Garzya and R.J. Loenertz, Procopii Gazaei Epistolae et declamationes (Studia Patristica et Byzantina 9, Ettal 1963), 166 letters. The book is in copyright. The 25-year German right for scholarly editions (§70 UrhG) has probably lapsed for the Greek text itself; this needs a legal check.
- Amato 2010 (174 letters, including the Megethius exchange, Ep. 167–174, first published in BZ 2005) is in copyright. So is its Italian translation.
item_094.research_yield: Prosopography of the Gaza network (Zacharias, Hieronymus, the iatrosophist Gessius, Megethius) against PLRE; the letters as school models and Atticist paideia; Procopius set beside Aeneas and Choricius; an article on method comparing reviewed AI translation with romanletters and Pearse.
item_094.recommendation: Keep, at priority 4 rather than 5: about 93% of the letters have no Russian translation and there is no scholarly English. But the RU 'none' is wrong, and two complete machine translations into English exist. Re-scope the pilot to G-L Ep. 11–40 without Ep. 20 (about 29 letters), using Hercher only as the public-domain witness through a concordance, and cite Синица and Богомаз–Болгов, or contact the Belgorod group first.

item_095.title_short: Libanius, Letters (Foerster 494–600 as pilot; 494–839 and 1113–1544 overall)
item_095.ru_found:

item_096.en_found: The colleague's "none" is wrong. All 85 letters are in English, translated from the Latin rather than the Greek. Edward Rosen (with Erna Hilfstein) translated Copernicus's 1509 Latin version into English in Nicholas Copernicus, Complete Works vol. III: Minor Works (Warsaw: Polish Scientific Publishers / London: Macmillan, 1985). It was reprinted as Minor Works (Baltimore: Johns Hopkins University Press, 1992), pp. 27–71. The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy entry "Copernicus" (S. Rabin) confirms it: "Copernicus translated into Latin the letters of ... Theophylactus Simocatta (MW 27–71)", where MW is Rosen's Minor Works. I found no English translation made directly from the Greek. I could not check whether P. A. Rosenmeyer's Ancient Greek Literary Letters: Selections in Translation (Routledge 2006) includes any of these letters.

- Latin: Copernicus (Kraków: J. Haller, 1509), from the Aldine Epistolographi of 1499; reprinted by Hipler, Spicilegium Copernicanum (1873).
- German: possibly in the Nicolaus Copernicus Gesamtausgabe (Opera minora volume), with the Latin text; not verified.

item_096.source_text: Public domain: R. Hercher, Epistolographi Graeci (Paris: Didot, 1873), which contains Theophylact's letters; the colleague's archive.org copy is https://archive.org/details/epistolographoih00hercuoft (I did not re-open it). Other public-domain sources are J. F. Boissonade's edition of the Quaestiones physicae and Epistolae (Paris 1835; not re-verified) and the Aldine editio princeps (1499). The standard modern edition is G. Zanetto, Theophylacti Simocatae epistulae (Leipzig: Teubner, 1985), which is in copyright (now De Gruyter). Copernicus's 1509 Latin and Hipler's 1873 reprint are public domain and useful for comparison.
item_096.research_yield: First complete Russian translation with commentary. Possible articles: Theophylact as the last writer of Alciphron/Aelian-style fictional letters (ethopoeia, rotating ethical, rustic and hetaira types); classical paideia at Heraclius' court; links to the History and the Dialogue; Copernicus's Latin version set against the Greek.
item_096.recommendation: Keep, but only as a Russian target, at lower priority: an English version would only be the first made directly from the Greek, since Rosen's 1985 English already covers all 85 letters. Best first unit: the complete collection (about 8,000 words), translated fresh from Hercher and checked against Zanetto, Miller's 19 letters and Copernicus/Rosen; the 66 letters missing in Russian are the minimum.

item_097.title_short: Dio Chrysostom, Kingship Orations 1–4 (unit: Or. 4, Alexander and Diogenes)
item_097.ru_found:
The claim that Or. 1–4 have no Russian translation is partly wrong. Or. 1 is translated in full: В. Т. Звиревич, «Дион Хризостом. О царской власти», Известия УрФУ, сер. 3, 2012, № 3, с. 147–159 (https://elar.urfu.ru/handle/10995/20967). A previous agent read that PDF; it covers 1.1–84 only.

No Russian translation was found for Or. 2, 3 or 4, so the proposed unit, Or. 4, still appears untranslated.

The key evidence is Данилова В. Ю., «Политическая философия Диона Хризостома», ΣΧΟΛΗ 17.1 (2023), с. 263. I re-read the PDF in this session (https://classics.nsu.ru/schole/assets/files/17-1-danilova.pdf). Of Or. I–IV, LVI and LXII she says only the first kingship oration (Звиревич 2012) and Or. 62 (Сидаш 2012, с. 103–107) are in Russian, and she worked from the Cohoon English. Because she cites Сидаш's «Кинические речи» by page, this largely settles the earlier worry that Or. 4 might be in that book (Нестор-История 2012; Квадривиум 2021). I still could not see the book's table of contents.

Other checks:
- Russian Wikipedia «Дион Хрисостом» (re-fetched today): translations listed only for Or. 6–12, 18, 21, 36, 51, 53, 55, plus Скифия/Индия excerpts, Сидаш 2012 and Межерицкая (Or. 29, 2017). Nothing for 1–4.
- Нахов, «Антология кинизма» (1984/1996): Or. 6, 8, 9, 10 only.
- CyberLeninka catalogue, 4 Russian queries («Дион Хрисостом о царской власти», «Дион Хрисостом перевод», «Дион Хризостом», «Диона Хрисостома»): no translation of Or. 2–4. One 2025 article (ИЯКФ) says its quotations are the author's own translations.
- ancientrome.ru: no Dio Chrysostom section.
- The Литпамятники № 760, «Вифинские речи» (Межерицкая; Ладомир–Наука 2024), is confirmed in the ru.wikipedia series list. Its title points to the Bithynian orations; the appendices were not checked.

Not checked: elibrary; Soviet хрестоматии (Струве 1953, Утченко 1962, Кузищин 1987), which may carry short excerpts; «Антология мировой политической мысли» т. 1 (1997); Вальденберг 1926–27; Шалимов 2000 (monograph, translations not mentioned in its abstract).

Method caveat: WebSearch was unavailable because the shared budget of 200 calls per turn was used up. Evidence comes from direct fetches, catalogue APIs and the project's cached verification (research/raw/alexander.json).
item_097.en_found: J. W. Cohoon, Dio Chrysostom vol. I (Discourses 1–11), Loeb Classical Library 257 (1932; reprinted, ed. Henderson, 2002). It has complete Or. 1–4. It is freely online at LacusCurtius (https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Dio_Chrysostom/Discourses/4*.html, also 1*, 2*, 3*), which says it is US public domain because the copyright was not renewed. Danilova 2023 also cites it. I found no other modern English version of the whole set, and I did not need one: English is already full.

Confirmed in Open Library and in Danilova's bibliography.

item_097.source_text:
- Best open text: H. von Arnim, Dionis Prusaensis quem vocant Chrysostomum quae exstant omnia, vol. I (Berlin: Weidmann 1893). Public domain, on archive.org.
- Digital TEI of the same text: Perseus canonical-greekLit, urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0612.tlg001.perseus-grc2, CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://github.com/PerseusDL/canonical-greekLit/tree/master/data/tlg0612/tlg001). item_097.research_yield: Alexander–Diogenes encounter (Or. 4) against Plutarch, Diogenes Laertius and the Alexander Romance; Or. 2, Homer as royal poet; Cynic three-daimones typology; Alexander as mirror for Trajan; completing the kingship tetralogy in Russian with Звиревич's Or. 1.
item_097.recommendation: Keep, but narrow it to Or. 2–4 as a first Russian translation: Or. 1 already exists in Russian (Звиревич 2012), and full English, Italian, Spanish and German versions mean it is not a world first. Best first unit is Or. 4 (about 6,400 words), followed by Or. 2.

item_098.ru_found:
The claim that there is no Russian translation is REFUTED. A complete Russian translation exists, and so do older excerpts.

(1) О. В. Смыка, «Флавий Филострат. Диалог о героях», in О. В. Смыка, «Переводы. Черновики переводов» (М.: Новый хронограф, 2023; 560 с.; signed to press 23.10.2023; print run 100 copies), pp. 470–544. It sits in the book's section «Черновики переводов». The book is free online as a PDF: https://smyka.persona.msu.ru/tr3.pdf, listed on https://smyka.persona.msu.ru/.
- I downloaded and text-extracted the PDF this session. It begins with the vinedresser–Phoenician dialogue (1.1) and runs without a break to the dialogue's last words (58.6). Every chapter 1–58 is present, using de Lannoy section numbering, about 25,300 Russian words.
- The proposed pilot unit (opening frame and the Protesilaus section) is therefore fully covered, as are the Palamedes/Odysseus/Homer chapters and the Leuke and Amazons chapters (56–57).
- It is a bare translation: no introduction, no notes, and the Greek edition used is not named. It has draft-level typos (e.g. «Пентесилая» for Протесилая).
- Russian Wikipedia does not list it, which is why the sweep missed it.

(2) Excerpts. From the project's earlier cached verification, not re-fetched this session: П. И. Прозоров's translation of «Рассказ о героях», in Латышев, «Известия древних писателей… о Скифии и Кавказе». It covers the Leuke and Amazons sections and was reprinted in ВДИ 1948 № 2 and in Scythica et Caucasica (1992).

(3) А. В. Белоусов quotes passages in his own translation in ИЯКФ XII (2008) and in his monograph (ПСТГУ, 2012).

Search limits: the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so I could not run fresh RU/EN keyword searches. I used the project cache (research/raw/odyssey.json, research/raw/ru_series_crosscheck.json) and verified the key evidence by fetching the primary sources directly.

- The standard modern editions are in copyright: L. de Lannoy (Teubner 1977), whose chapter numbering all modern translations use, and S. Follet (CUF 2017).
item_098.research_yield: Low as a first translation, since the work is complete in RU, EN, FR, DE, IT and ES. Remaining options: a critical annotated Russian edition that improves on Smyka's unannotated draft; articles on the Protesilaus cult, Homer criticism, and Palamedes/Odysseus revisionism alongside Dictys and Dares.
item_098.recommendation: Drop it as a Neoscholia first-translation candidate. Smyka 2023 gives a complete Russian translation (chapters 1–58, free PDF), which covers the proposed pilot unit, and English plus all major European languages have full versions. At most, keep it as a low-tier idea for an annotated Greek–Russian edition that reviews Smyka's draft.

item_099.title_short: Aelius Aristides, Or. 2–4 (Platonic orations; pilot Or. 4 To Capito)
item_099.ru_found:
No Russian translation of Or. 2, 3 or 4, whole or excerpted, turned up in the sources I could check. Under Dindorf's numbering Or. 2 = XLV "О риторике" and Or. 3 = XLVI "О четверых". Caveat: the shared WebSearch budget was already used up, so I ran none of the required 4+4 searches. I checked these sources instead:
(1) ru.wikipedia "Элий Аристид", fetched directly. It names XLV and XLVI only as works and lists no translation of them. Its translations list covers: Межерицкая (Священные речи and Похвала Риму, ЛП 2006 with Гаспаров; Надгробные речи and Монодии, ЛП 2017; Египетская речь, ВДИ 2016; Smyrnaean orations, Мнемон 2018 and ВДИ 2020; hymns, Новый Гермес 2020; Or. 29, Аристей XVI 2017); Шульц 1985 (2nd Sacred Tale); Турцевич 1907 (To Rome); and the anthologies of 1960 (Or. 22, Or. 44) and 1964 (Or. 29).
(2) aristeas.ru, archive and home page through vol. XXXII (2025). Its only other Aristides item is Межерицкая's Or. 33 / Against the Dancers (vol. XXV, 2022).
(3) The project's ru_series_crosscheck.json, which matches the above.
Risk: research/01_landscape.md flags Aristides as "занят" because С. И. Межерицкая is translating him actively and systematically, so a collision is possible.
item_099.en_found:
Full, and translated more than once. en.wikipedia and de.wikipedia, both fetched directly, confirm:
- M. Trapp, Loeb, Greek with facing English. Vol. 1 is LCL 533 (2017, Or. 1–2); vol. 2 is LCL 545 (2021, Or. 3–4).
- C. A. Behr, The Complete Works, vol. I (Brill 1986; Or. 1–16).
- Behr's earlier Loeb vol. I (1973). Its contents are Or. 1–2 according to my memory; the pages I fetched do not list them.
item_099.other_found: I could not verify any version in another language. The de.wikipedia and it.wikipedia bibliographies list no French, German, Italian or Spanish translation of Or. 2–4. The colleague's "Italian and French versions of Or. 2" stays unconfirmed: I could not search for it, so treat it as unknown.
item_099.source_text:
Public domain:
- W. Dindorf, Aristides, vols. I–III (Leipzig: Reimer, 1829). Scans exist on archive.org, but I have not checked the exact URL or volume. The Platonic orations are Dindorf Or. 45–46; check Dindorf's number for To Capito.
- S. Jebb, Oxford 1722–30.
Keil 1898 covers only Or. 17–53, so it does not include these orations.

In copyright:
- The standard critical text, Lenz–Behr, Opera quae exstant omnia I.1–4 (Brill 1976–80), which TLG uses.
- Trapp's Loeb Greek text (2017/2021).

Plan: translate from Dindorf and use Lenz–Behr or Trapp only for collation and checking.
item_099.research_yield: Second-Sophistic reception of the Gorgias; the rhetoric-versus-philosophy quarrel; Pericles and the Four in imperial memory; Porphyry's lost reply and Olympiodorus' In Gorgiam (a sibling candidate). Useful for the Russian Platonist and rhetoric community, but these would be Russian-only firsts.
item_099.recommendation: Keep only as a low-priority Russian-only candidate (P4). English is full, with a Loeb that has facing Greek, and Межерицкая is actively translating Aristides, so ask her before starting. If kept, pilot Or. 4 To Capito from Dindorf; better, pair Or. 2 with Olympiodorus' In Gorgiam.

item_100.ru_found:
The "untranslated" claim could not be refuted beyond what the sweep already found. Russian coverage is 4 of 51 pieces:
(1) Decl. 1, Апология Сократа, tr. М. А. Райцина, in Суд над Сократом, ed. А. В. Кургатников (СПб.: Алетейя, 1997).
(2) Decl. 28, in Поздняя греческая проза (М.: ГИХЛ, 1961), pp. 596–604, credited to М. Е. Грабарь-Пассек.
(3) Decl. 26 and 29, in Памятники позднего античного ораторского и эпистолярного искусства, ed. Грабарь-Пассек (М.: Наука, 1964). The translator is not named on the page.
Source: ru.wikipedia «Либаний», fetched today.
The project's cached cross-check of the Belgorod series (КВТ, Мир поздней античности, Аристей, vostlit) has Libanius orations and letters only (Шабага on Or. 19–23, Шестаков, Болгова/Болгов on the letters) and no further declamations.
CAVEAT: the WebSearch budget for this run was exhausted. The planned 4+ Russian searches were therefore not run, and elibrary, cyberleninka and the dissertation catalogues were not searched for journal translations of single declamations.
item_100.en_found:
(1) D. A. Russell, Libanius: Imaginary Speeches. A Selection of Declamations (London: Duckworth, 1996). BMCR 2013.02.38 n.1 confirms it is a selection. The contents per ru.wikipedia are Decl. 1, 2, 6, 12, 22, 25, 26, 27, 31, 32, 33, 39, 42; I did not confirm this list independently.
(2) M. Johansson, Libanius' Declamations 9 and 10 (Göteborg, 2006): text, translation and commentary.
(3) Heath 1995 (Hermogenes On Issues) and Ogden 2002 (Magic, Witchcraft and Ghosts sourcebook). Per ru.wikipedia, these two together with Johansson cover Decl. 9, 10, 36, 41, 44. Which piece is where, and whether Ogden's are excerpts, is unverified.
In total about 18 pieces exist in English. There is no complete English version, and Decl. 3–4 have not been found in English.
item_100.other_found:
German: U. Lempp, Libanios: Musterreden, BGL 78 (Stuttgart: Hiersemann, 2015), 317 pp. Per the Google Books description it translates 15 pieces: Decl. 1, 5, 6, 12, 25–28, 30–32, 39, 41, 42, 46.

French: NEW and missed by the sweep. Libanios, Apologie de Socrate suivie de Socrate condamné au silence [= Decl. 1–2], vol. 1, Paris: Les Belles Lettres, 2024, XXIV+304 pp. Text by P.-L. Malosse, translation and commentary by B. Schouler (per fr.wikipedia). This looks like the start of a full Budé edition of the declamations, so later volumes may close the gap in French.

Older Latin versions exist (Morel 1606–27; Reiske 1791–97), but they are not modern-language translations.

Italian and Spanish: unknown, not searched because the budget was exhausted.

Combined, the known RU, EN, DE and FR coverage is about 23 pieces: 1, 2, 5, 6, 9, 10, 12, 22, 25–33, 36, 39, 41, 42, 44, 46. That leaves about 28 pieces apparently untranslated: 3, 4, 7, 8, 11, 13–21, 23, 24, 34, 35, 37, 38, 40, 43, 45, 47–51.
item_100.source_text:
The best public-domain text is R. Foerster, Libanii opera, Teubner:
- vol. V (1909): Decl. 1–12
- vol. VI (1911): Decl. 13–30, plus Gregory of Cyprus' antilogia
- vol. VII (1913): Decl. 31–51, plus a second antilogia of Gregory
Foerster died in 1922, so the edition is public domain. The sweep says archive.org has scans; my fetch of one guessed identifier returned 404, so locate the scans before use. Reiske's edition (Altenburg, 1791–97) is also public domain.
Copyright status: the new Budé edition (Malosse/Schouler 2024, so far Decl. 1–2 only) is in copyright, as are Russell 1996 and Lempp 2015. For the untranslated pieces, Foerster is still the standard edition.
item_100.research_yield: Possible articles: Homeric embassy speeches (Decl. 3–4) and Troy in the late-antique classroom; Demosthenes, Philip and Alexander in Libanius' declamations; Gregory of Cyprus' Byzantine antilogiai; the first Russian survey of the 51-piece corpus.
item_100.recommendation: Keep as a Russian-first candidate at priority 3 (5 = highest). The English gap is only partial, and Budé has begun a French edition. Best first unit: the pair Decl. 3–4 (Menelaus' and Odysseus' embassy speeches to Troy, titles to confirm in Foerster V); second choice: a Demosthenes/Macedon piece from Decl. 13–24 other than 22. Check Italian/Spanish translations and Budé vol. 2 first.

item_101.title_short: Syrianus, In Hermogenem commentaria (On Ideas commentary, Rabe I; On Issues commentary, Rabe II)
item_101.ru_found:
No full or partial Russian translation of either commentary was found. Excerpts only:

(1) Е. В. Афонасин, «Горгий Леонтийский. Фрагменты и свидетельства», ΣΧΟΛΗ 14.2 (2020), DOI 10.25205/1995-4328-2020-14-2-756-8, https://cyberleninka.ru/article/n/gorgiy-leontiyskiy-fragmenty-i-svidetelstva
- It gives Russian translations of five passages from Syrianus' On Ideas commentary:
  - Rabe I 10.9–16 and 11.20–23 (Dionysius, On Imitation frs. 4–5).
  - I 90.12–16.
  - I 90.17–91.16 (the Gorgias Epitaphios citation).
  - I 91.16–19.
- Two of these (I 10–11) fall inside the proposed pilot range.

(2) О. В. Алиева, «Паренеза: философская и риторическая традиция», Вестник ПСТГУ сер. III (2011), https://cyberleninka.ru/article/n/pareneza-filosofskaya-i-ritoricheskaya-traditsiya
- It gives a few lines in Russian: the definition of paraenesis from the On Issues scholia (Walz RG IV 763).

Checked, nothing found:
- LitRes catalogue API. «Сириан» returns only Антонов's 2026 Metaphysics commentary; «Гермоген» returns nothing relevant. So Antonov's LLM-style LitRes series has not reached the Hermogenes commentaries as of October 2026.
- CyberLeninka API with 10 queries: Сириан, Сириана, Сириан Гермоген, Гермоген, Гермогена, Гермоген Тарсский, Об идеях Гермоген, риторика статусов, теория статусов, неоплатоники риторика.
- ancientrome.ru author index: no entry for Syrianus, Hermogenes, Sopater, Marcellinus or Aphthonius.
- ru.wikipedia «Сириан»: lists only the Metaphysics translations.
- Cached project sweeps: the full ΣΧΟΛΗ archive 2007–2026, plus Аристей, Philologia Classica, ИЯКФ, Литпамятники and Античная библиотека. None has Syrianus on Hermogenes.

Not checked (the WebSearch quota was exhausted): «Античные теории языка и стиля» (1936/1996) on paper, Лосев ИАЭ, the RSL/NLR catalogues.

Hermogenes' On Ideas itself seems to have no Russian translation (no ancientrome entry); this is unverified.
item_101.en_found:
Partial: prefatory material only.

- D. Baltzly & M. Share, Hermias: On Plato Phaedrus 257C–279C, with 'Syrianus': Introduction to Hermogenes on Styles. Ancient Commentators on Aristotle series, Bloomsbury 2025, ISBN 9781350363779.
  - J. Dillon's review (BMCR 2025.10.46, https://bmcr.brynmawr.edu/2025/2025.10.46/) says the introduction is "not by Syrianus himself" but by the later Alexandrian Phoebammon, dedicated in Syrianus' name to Alexander.
  - It corresponds to the prefatory matter of Rabe vol. I. That is the short dedicatory prooemium (I 1.4–2.11) and/or the longer spurious 'Syriani quae fertur praefatio' (c. I 97–112).
  - The exact Rabe range is unconfirmed because bloomsbury.com could not be fetched.
- The lemma commentary on On Ideas (Rabe I c. 2–96) and the On Issues commentary (Rabe II) have no English translation found.
  - The ACA author list (ancientcommentators.org.uk) shows no Syrianus-on-Hermogenes volume, published or forthcoming.
  - Open Library (all 19 Syrianus works) and en.wikipedia list none.
- Scattered English excerpts probably exist but are unverified. Likely places: Heath, Hermogenes On Issues (OUP 1995); Rutherford, Canons of Style (1998); the Gorgias and Dionysius testimonia in Laks–Most, Early Greek Philosophy VIII (Loeb 2016).
item_101.other_found:
This refutes the sweep's "None found".

On Issues, French, full scholarly translation:
- Syrianus, Sur les états de cause, texte établi et traduit par Michel Patillon. CUF série grecque no. 555, Les Belles Lettres, 2 June 2021, XXVIII + 580 pp., Greek–French, ISBN 9782251006413. https://www.lesbelleslettres.com/livre/9782251006413/sur-les-etats-de-cause
- It contains the scholia-commentary on the first two chapters of De statibus, plus a separate treatise defining fourteen staseis.
- A Gnomon review (2023), quoted by the publisher, calls it "la première en langue moderne".

Related Patillon CUF volumes:
- Hermogenes' commentators: Sopatros 2019, Pseudo-Sopatros 2022, Eustathius 2018, Georgius Monachus 2018.
- Corpus Rhetoricum IV (CUF 491, 2012): Hermogenes, De ideis, with "Prolégomènes au De Ideis" and a "Synopse des exposés sur les ideai". It is unverified whether these include the Syrianus/Phoebammon preface or extracts from Syrianus.

On Ideas: no French, German, Italian or Spanish translation found.
- Belles Lettres catalogue: 'Syrianus' returns that single title.
- Open Library: none.
- de/it/fr Wikipedia: cite Rabe only.
- Possible Italian excerpts of the Dionysius On Imitation fragments transmitted by Syrianus, in Battisti 1997: unverified.
item_101.source_text:
H. Rabe, Syriani in Hermogenem commentaria, 2 vols, Leipzig: Teubner 1892–93. Public domain (Rabe died 1932); archive.org marks it NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT.

Vol. I (On Ideas): https://archive.org/details/syrianiinhermog01rabegoog (PDF and djvu.txt)
- Genuine short prooemium: I 1.4–2.11.
- Book 1 lemmata: c. pp. 2–70.
- Book 2: c. pp. 70/71–96.
- Spurious longer praefatio: c. pp. 97–112.
- Rabe's best witness is Venetus Marc. gr. 438.

Vol. II (On Issues): https://archive.org/details/syrianiinhermog00rabegoog

Other sources:
- Lace raw Greek OCR of vol. I is linked from en.wikipedia "Syrianus".
- The OCR is noisy (accents, θ read as ϑ, Latin letters), so it needs re-OCR or manual cleaning.
- Walz, Rhetores Graeci IV (1833), has the reworked On Issues scholia (public domain).

Standard edition status:
- On Ideas: Rabe is still the standard edition, and it is public domain.
- On Issues: Patillon's CUF 2021 edition is now standard and is in copyright.
item_101.research_yield: Platonist theory of style in Proclus' school; canonisation of Hermogenes; fragments of lost critics (Dionysius' On Imitation, earlier rhetors); Syrianus/Phoebammon prooemium attribution; Gorgias/Demosthenes reception; Byzantine rhetorical curriculum. Supports 2–3 specialist articles.
item_101.recommendation: Keep, but narrow the scope to the On Ideas commentary (Rabe I) and drop On Issues, which already has Patillon's Greek–French CUF edition (2021). Best first unit: the Book 2 commentary (Rabe I c. 70–96, from ἀφέλεια to δεινότης, about 9k words), or Book 1 at pp. 2–40 without the prooemium, which is now in English.

item_102.title_short: Sopater, Division of Questions (Diaireseis zetematon), themes 1-10
item_102.ru_found: No Russian translation found. I could not run the required Russian searches because the session's WebSearch budget (200 calls) was already used up, so I used only direct page fetches. ru.wikipedia "Сопатр" covers only Sopater of Apamea, the Neoplatonist; it does not mention the Diaireseis and cites only Eunapius in Russian and Losev's ИАЭ VII. The РСКД entry on ru.wikisource lists the rhetor's works only as reprinted in Walz, Rhet. Gr. IV, V and VIII, with no translation. The ancientrome.ru antlitr index shows no Sopater; the page was partly garbled. The project's own wave-1 sweep found "nothing in Russian for ... Syrianus or Sopater" in ΣΧΟΛΗ, Аристей and Russian Wikipedia. Russian has no translation of Hermogenes' Περὶ στάσεων either, as far as I know (not verified), which makes an earlier Sopater translation very unlikely. Not checked: elibrary/cyberleninka, the Античные теории языка и стиля anthology (1936/1996), RSL catalogue.
item_102.en_found: No full or continuous English translation is known. BMCR 1998.03.13 (Rutherford, reviewing Heath's Hermogenes On Issues, 1995) calls Innes & Winterbottom, Sopatros the Rhetor: Studies in the Text of the Διαίρεσις Ζητημάτων (BICS Suppl. 48, 1988) a "massive contribution to understanding" the text. It does not call it a translation. As I recall (not verified this session), that book gives textual studies and notes with English renderings of the passages discussed and summaries of themes. It is not a running translation; its exact extent is still unverified, and if it is larger the verdict should be 'partial'. Further English excerpts are likely in D. A. Russell, Greek Declamation (CUP 1983) and M. Heath, Hermogenes On Issues (OUP 1995). These come from my own knowledge and were not checked by search.
item_102.other_found: None found. Checked: de.wikipedia (the "Sopatros (Rhetor)" article does not exist), it.wikipedia disambiguation ("Sopatro di Atene, commentatore di Ermogene", no bibliography), en.wikipedia "Sopater of Apamea" (mentions the Diairesis as 81 themes, citing OCD, and names no translation). I know of no CUF/Patillon "Corpus rhetoricum" volume, Teubner, Tusculum, BUR or Gredos version of the Diaireseis, but I could not confirm this by search.
item_102.source_text: Ch. Walz, Rhetores Graeci vol. VIII (Stuttgart/Tübingen: Cotta, 1835). The Diaireseis opens the volume, about pp. 1-385 by my recollection; the page range is to be checked. It is public domain and scanned on Google Books / archive.org according to the earlier sweep, but no exact URL was verified (a guessed archive.org ID returned 404). Walz is still the only complete edition. Innes & Winterbottom 1988 (ICS/BICS Suppl. 48) is in copyright and essential for emendations; the editor should get a copy before translating. I found no newer critical edition.
item_102.research_yield: Stasis theory applied to whole cases, which has no primary text in Russian. Late-antique school memory of classical Athens and Demosthenes, and possibly Alexander-era themes such as the demand for the orators (to check). Comparison with Libanius' declamations. A Russian stasis glossary.
item_102.recommendation: Keep it at priority 3 as a specialist but unique candidate. RU is almost certainly untranslated, EN has only excerpts or studies. Before committing, get Innes & Winterbottom 1988 to measure how much English it already gives. The best first unit is themes 1-5 (about 8-10k words) from Walz VIII, with the I&W emendations and a stasis glossary; it could be swapped for the themes on Demosthenes or the Macedonians if those prove contiguous.

item_103.title_short: Himerius, Orations (10 school orations not in older Russian anthologies)
item_103.ru_found: REFUTED: a full Russian translation exists. I.V. Denisova (И.В. Денисова), «Гимерий, софист 2-й пол. IV в., и его речи», in Византийский клуб. Альманах 2022, ed. N.N. Bolgov (Belgorod, BelGU, 2022, ISBN 978-5-6049008-8-8), pp. 110–232. It is an open PDF at if.bsuedu.ru (URL cached in research/raw/ru_series_crosscheck.json). I extracted the text and checked it myself. The introduction says it is the first complete Russian translation ("полный перевод сохранившегося наследия Гимерия", for information only). It covers every surviving oration I–LXXIV in Colonna's numbering, including X, XX, XL–XLVIII, LIV, LIX–LXIX and LXXIV, plus fragments 1–17; lost items are marked "не сохр.". The proposed pilot unit (school orations such as LIV, LIX–LXV, LXVIII, LXIX, LXXIV) is therefore fully covered. The titles, bracketed glosses, source sigla (Exc. Phot., Exc. Neapol., Lex. Lopad., cod. R) and notes closely follow Penella's English, so the version was probably made from or with Penella's English rather than directly from the Greek. An earlier instalment of the same version appeared as «Гимерий. Речи XI–XX» in Классическая и византийская традиция 2021 (Belgorod), pp. 251–262; I checked that PDF, and no translator is named. Older partial translations: Or. 1, 3, 23 in «Поздняя греческая проза» (М., 1960); Or. 12, 17, 18, 24 and Ecl. 17 in «Памятники позднеантичного ораторского и эпистолярного искусства» (М., 1964), per Russian Wikipedia and Denisova's own list. Scythian/Caucasian excerpts are in Latyshev, «Известия» I. The web-search quota ran out, so no new searches could be run. The evidence comes from the project cache plus direct reading of the primary PDFs.
item_103.en_found: R.J. Penella, Man and the Word: The Orations of Himerius (Berkeley: University of California Press, 2007; Transformation of the Classical Heritage 43). It is a complete annotated translation, cited by Russian Wikipedia and in Denisova's 2022 bibliography. Denisova's Russian version follows the same I–LXXIV plus Fr. 1–17 structure and apparatus, which supports completeness. I could not reach the UC Press page directly, and no new searches were possible.
item_103.other_found: German, complete: H. Völker, Himerios, Reden und Fragmente: Einführung, Übersetzung und Kommentar (Serta Graeca 17, Wiesbaden: Reichert, 2003). Cited by Russian Wikipedia and Denisova. Latin versions accompany the older editions: Wernsdorf, Göttingen 1790, and Dübner, Didot, Paris 1849. Italian, French and Spanish were not verified because the search quota was exhausted. Denisova's bibliography lists only Italian studies, not translations.
item_103.source_text: Standard edition: A. Colonna, Himerii Declamationes et orationes cum deperditarum fragmentis (Rome: Typis Publicae Officinae Polygraphicae, 1951). Treat it as in copyright, although the 20-year Italian protection for critical editions might apply; this is unverified. Public-domain texts: G. Wernsdorf, Himerii sophistae quae reperiri potuerunt (Göttingen, 1790) and F. Dübner, Himerii sophistae Declamationes (Paris: Didot, 1849, with Latin). Neither has the Neapolitan excerpts or the Lexicon Lopadiotes fragments published by H. Schenkl (Hermes 46, 1911), nor the papyrus fragments in P. Osl. inv. 1478 (1956). Photius cod. 243 is in Henry's Budé edition (vol. VI, 1971), which is in copyright.
item_103.research_yield: Low for Neoscholia. It is fully translated into Russian, English and German. The only possible articles are a critique of the 2022 Russian version, which appears to be relayed through Penella's English, or a retranslation from the Greek of select orations. Neither fits a first-translation mandate.
item_103.recommendation: Drop. The whole corpus and the proposed school-oration unit are already translated into Russian (Denisova 2022, open access), English (Penella 2007) and German (Völker 2003). Revisit only as a possible future retranslation from the Greek.

item_104.title_short: Maximus of Tyre, Dissertationes (Or. 11, Τίς ὁ θεὸς κατὰ Πλάτωνα)
item_104.ru_found:

- Or. 2: С. Полякова, «Поздняя греческая проза» (1961).
- Or. 36: Ю. Шульц, same 1961 volume; reprinted in «Антология кинизма» (1996).
- Or. 5: И. Ковалева, «Античность в контексте современности» (1990).
- Or. 14 = old Diss. IV: «Максима Тирского рассуждение IV», «Трудолюбивая пчела», July 1759 (ru.wikisource; 1759 numbering).
- Or. 18–19: А.В. Гараджа, Платоновские исследования 13.2 (2020) 334–353, DOI 10.25985/pi.13.2.16. I read the full text.
- Or. 20–21: Гараджа, ΣΧΟΛΗ 15.1 (2021) 422–435.
- Or. 8–9: Гараджа, ΣΧΟΛΗ 16.1 (2022) 317–333.
- Or. 8–9 again: Г.С. Беликов, ВДИ 2023 №2 (from the project's cache; vdi.igh.ru refused connection).
Partial material:
- Or. 12.2–5: А.В. Серёгин, Платоновские исследования 13.2 (2020) 138–156. A study; whether it contains a translation is unverified.
- Or. 15–16: quotations in the author's own translation, Беликов, ΣΧΟΛΗ 18.1 (2024). I read the full text.
That leaves about 31 orations with no complete Russian version.

UNIT, Or. 11: no Russian translation found. The only Russian text is two sentences, 11.2 and 11.6, in Беликов's own translation, plus a paraphrase of 11.2–12 («Композиционная техника Максима Тирского», Индоевропейское языкознание и классическая филология 24, 2020, 987–998; I read the full text). He cites no existing Russian version of Or. 11. Гараджа (2020) says only "a few" 20th-century translations exist, all based on Hobein.

Checked:
- ru.wikipedia «Максим Тирский».
- Tables of contents of ΣΧΟΛΗ vols 17–20 (2023–2026): no Maximus translations.
- Tables of contents of Платоновские исследования, issues 14–24 (2021–2026): no Maximus.
- Crossref and OpenAlex for «Максим Тирский» and «Максима Тирского», and by author Беликов / Гараджа.
- ru.wikisource full-text search, including the Motonis author page.
- ancientrome.ru index: no Maximus.

WebSearch was unavailable because the session quota was used up. I used direct fetches, bibliographic APIs and the project's cache instead.

Residual risks:
- ВДИ 2024–26 (site unreachable).
- A possible Беликов dissertation with a translation appendix.
- Ковалева's 1990 dissertation (may contain translated passages).
- 18th-century «Ежемесячные сочинения». Old Diss. I = Or. 11, and Motonis translated Diss. IV, so the 1750s are worth one catalogue check.
item_104.en_found:
There are three complete English translations, and each includes Or. 11:
(1) Thomas Taylor, The Dissertations of Maximus Tyrius, London 1804. Public domain, on archive.org as dissertationsma00taylgoog. I checked the full text: old Dissertation I is "What God is according to Plato", i.e. Or. 11.
(2) M.B. Trapp, Maximus of Tyre: The Philosophical Orations, Oxford: Clarendon 1997. Or. 11 is the chapter "Plato on God", DOI 10.1093/oso/9780198149897.003.0010 (Crossref).
(3) W.H. Race, Maximus of Tyre: Philosophical Orations, Loeb Classical Library, 2 vols, 2023. Confirmed in en.wikipedia; the Loeb site returned 403.
English studies of Or. 11 also exist: Reydams-Schils, "Maximus of Tyre on God and Providence" (OUP 2017), and Domaradzki & Bednarek in Erga-Logoi (2021).
item_104.other_found:
Complete translations:
- Italian: S.I.S. Brumana, Massimo di Tiro, Dissertazioni, Bompiani 2019, Greek facing text. Cited by Гараджа 2020.
- Spanish: J.L. López Cruces & F.J. Campos Daroca, Máximo de Tiro, Disertaciones filosóficas, Gredos, 2 vols, 2005.

- French: J.-I. Combes-Dounous, 1802, on Gallica. There is also a 1764 Leiden version.

Selections that include Or. 11:
- French: B. Pérez-Jean & F. Fauquier, Maxime de Tyr, Choix de conférences, Les Belles Lettres 2014. Contains Or. 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, 38 and 41.

Sources: the project cache (odyssey.json verification) and the bibliographies of Беликов and Гараджа.
item_104.source_text:
Best public-domain text: H. Hobein, Maximi Tyrii Philosophumena, Teubner 1910. On archive.org as maximi-tyrii-philosophumena (Google scan from the University of Michigan; metadata checked). Its numbering matches Trapp's.
Caveat: Гараджа (2020) faults Hobein's stemma, which leads to wrong choices of reading.
Standard modern editions, both in copyright (use them to check readings, do not reproduce them):
- M.B. Trapp, Dissertationes, Teubner 1994.
- G.L. Koniaris, Philosophumena–Dialexeis, De Gruyter 1995.
Other public-domain texts, all in the old numbering where Or. 11 = Diss. I:
- Dübner, Didot 1840, Greek and Latin.
- Reiske, 1774–75.
- Davis & Markland, 1740.
Taylor's 1804 English translation (public domain) can serve as a comparison text.
item_104.research_yield: Or. 11 against Alcinous, Did. 10 and Apuleius, as school theology turned into a lecture (the three ways of knowing God); the 11.5 consensus passage and "pagan monotheism"; the Symposium ascent; Homer versus the Platonic god. It would complete a Russian theological dossier alongside Or. 2, 8 and 9.
item_104.recommendation: Keep as a Russian-only candidate; the "ideally untranslated" test fails, since it has three English translations and complete Italian, Spanish and German ones. Best first unit: Or. 11, optionally paired with Or. 41 (theodicy), also untranslated into Russian. Correct the count to 10 of 41 in Russian, and contact Гараджа and Беликов first, as both are actively translating Maximus.

item_105.ru_found:
No Russian translation of any progymnasma found, of the whole collection or of the proposed unit (fables and narrations). This check is limited. The WebSearch budget for this turn (200 calls, shared by all agents) was already used up, so none of the required Russian or English searches could run, and I did not query site search engines as a workaround. Direct page fetches and project caches instead:
(1) ru.wikipedia «Либаний» bibliography lists Shestakov's orations (Kazan 1912–16; reprint Квадривиум 2014), Ranovich 1935, Polyakova 1961, Grabar-Passek 1961 and 1964 (orations, Decl. 28, letters), Rabinovich 1985 (Or. 18), Raitsina 1997 (Decl. 1) and Shabaga, Аристей XI 2015 (Or. 19–23). The only progymnasmata translation listed is Gibson (English, 2008). It counts 144 progymnasmata.
(2) ru.wikisource «Либаний»: only the orations and «Суд над Сократом».
(3) ru.wikipedia «Экфрасис», «Афтоний», «Терсит»: nothing relevant. «Прогимнасмы» and «Этопея» have no article.
(4) Smyka's collected translations (smyka.persona.msu.ru/tr3.pdf, 2023, text extracted): no Libanius, including in his 1971–2023 publication list.
(5) The project cache ru_series_crosscheck.json, which checks against about 900 Russian translations (Belgorod МПА/КВТ, ΣΧΟΛΗ, Аристей, ВДИ, philology journals, vostlit, Smyka), has no conflict for item_105. The cached Alexander verification found no Russian translation of Chreia 1 or Descr. 25/27.
Not checked: elibrary, dissertations, Gasparov's fable anthologies (the Aesopic fables exist in Russian, but not Libanius' elaborations), art-history source books such as «Мастера искусства об искусстве», and 18th–19th-c. seminary rhetorics.
item_105.en_found:
Confirmed: Craig A. Gibson, Libanius's Progymnasmata: Model Exercises in Greek Prose Composition and Rhetoric (SBL Writings from the Greco-Roman World 27; Atlanta: SBL, 2008), ISBN 978-1-58983-360-9. Greek facing English, covering all of Foerster VIII pp. 1–571, spuria included. I extracted the full text of the free SBL PDF at https://www.sbl-site.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/Gibson.pdf. Gibson says the collection "as a whole" had never been translated into a modern language. BMCR 2012.03.31 (Pirovano) calls it the first complete modern translation.
Contents: 144 pieces in total, comprising 3 fables, 41 narrations, 4 anecdotes, 3 maxims, 2 refutations, 3 confirmations, 5 common topics, 9 encomia, 8 invectives, 5 comparisons, 27 speeches in character, 30 descriptions, 3 theses and 1 introduction of a law.
Earlier partial English translations: Hock & O'Neil, The Chreia and Ancient Rhetoric: Classroom Exercises (SBL 2002) 140–97, all four anecdotes; Ratzen & Ferngren, JHM 48 (1993) 163–70, Common Topics 3; A. Stewart, Faces of Power (1993) 383–84 and 397–400, Descr. 25 and 27.
For the proposed unit (fables and narrations), Gibson lists no earlier modern translation, so Gibson 2008 is its only English version.
item_105.other_found:
From Gibson's own lists of prior translations and BMCR 2012.03.31:
- German: B. Hebert, Spätantike Beschreibung von Kunstwerken (Diss. Graz 1983). Text, German translation and commentary for Descr. 2–4, 12–20, 22–23 and 25–28.
- German: K. Pichler, Byzantinisch-neugriechische Jahrbücher 11 (1934–35). Speech in Character 11 and 27.
- Italian: A. Stramaglia, "Amori impossibili", in Studium declamatorium (Leipzig: Saur 2003) 235–36. Speech in Character 27.
- Italian: G. Ventrella, in F. De Martino (ed.), Medea in via Arpi (Bari 2005). Speech in Character 1 (Medea).
- French: J.-P. Callu, Ktèma 19 (1994) 272–73. Descr. 25.
- Spanish: none found. Ureña Bracero (2007) is on authorship only.
The de, it, fr and es Wikipedias list no progymnasmata translation. For the fables and narrations, no translation in any other language was found. Post-2008 publications could not be searched.
item_105.source_text:
Foerster's Teubner edition remains the standard critical text and is public domain: R. Foerster, Libanii opera VIII: Progymnasmata, Argumenta orationum Demosthenicarum (Leipzig: Teubner 1915).
- Scan: archive.org/details/foerster-libanii-opera, file "Foerster (1915), Libanii opera 8.pdf" (30.6 MB), Public Domain Mark 1.0. The Greek OCR is poor, so work from the page images.
- Gibson 2008 reprints Foerster's Greek with its deviations noted. That edition is © SBL, all rights reserved, but the free PDF is a useful check. Its Greek font does not extract as text.
- Parallels for Ps.-Nicolaus and Severus: Walz, Rhetores Graeci I (1832, public domain).
item_105.research_yield: Russian studies possible: school mythography in the narrations (against Ovid and Apollodorus); Ps.-Nicolaus authorship; Odysseus and Homeric ethopoeiae (links to the Odyssey dossier); the Antioch and Alexandria ekphraseis, including the Tychaion and Alexander Ktistes; progymnasmata in Russian seminary rhetoric.
item_105.recommendation: Keep at priority 3 as a Russian-only candidate; the English version adds nothing, since Gibson's is complete and free. The proposed unit is mostly spurious (Norman rejects all 41 narrations and the fables; Foerster–Münscher accept only Narr. 1–3 and the fables) and runs to about 4,500–5,000 English words, not 6,000; so either label it as the Libanian corpus or start instead with the Odysseus block: Encomium 2 plus Speech in Character 23–25, about 4,000 words.

item_106.title_short: Scholia vetera in Pindarum, Pythians (unit: Pythian 1)
item_106.ru_found:
LIMITATION: the WebSearch budget was already used up before this item, so no general web searches ran. Instead I used the project cache, direct page fetches and 5 Russian queries on the CyberLeninka API.

Findings:
(1) Gasparov 1980 (Пиндар, Вакхилид. Оды. Фрагменты, Литературные памятники, Наука), verified at ancientrome.ru/antlitr/pindar/:
- a full Russian translation of the Vita Ambrosiana (vita.htm). The Vita belongs to the scholia corpus (Drachmann vol. I) but is not part of the Pythians.
- the Pythian notes (pindar04.htm) quote or paraphrase only a few scholia. Quoted: P.3 (the Olympichus / Mother-of-Gods anecdote) and P.8 (Alcmaeon's shrine by Aristomenes' house). Paraphrased: P.4, P.5, P.9.
- For P.1 there is only a paraphrase: 'по объяснению схолиастов' Hieron suffered from kidney stones.
(2) Latyshev, Известия древних писателей о Скифии и Кавказе I (1890–1900; reprinted ВДИ 1947–48), pp. 327–333: Pontic excerpts from the Pindar scholia (project cache ru_series_crosscheck). These touch P.4 (Colchis/Phasis), not P.1. P.1 scholia have no Pontic content.
(3) Pindar, Пифийские оды, trans. Г.Г. Стариковский (HSE, Orientalia et Classica X, 2025). I saw only the 25-page preview (publications.hse.ru/pubs/share/direct/1145708831.pdf). The commentary on Ode I is by С.А. Степанцов, pp. 171–198. The intro cites the scholiasts, and the commentary probably translates single scholia, but this is unverified.
(4) CyberLeninka found articles that use the scholia piecemeal, with no systematic translation:
- Ахунова (Pyth. 5, 11, 12; ИЯКФ / Шаги 2018–2024)
- Можайский (Pyth. 8, Hypothekai 2021)
- Касьянова (Typhon/Arimoi, ИЯКФ 2008)
No Russian translation of any Pythian scholia set was found.
item_106.en_found:
BMCR 2010.08.39 (Bitto, reviewing the 2009 'Traduire les scholies de Pindare') calls the Besançon project 'the first one of its kind in a modern language'. BMCR 2014.12.27 (Prodi) calls Scholies à Pindare I 'the first complete translation of the scholia vetera to Pindar's first Olympian into any modern language'. Neither mentions an English translation. I found no English translation of the Pythian scholia or of the P.1 scholia.

Excerpts:
- The P.1 scholia cite Timaeus (Phalaris' bull; the mother of Deinomenes), Philistus, Artemon the historian (Hieron's golden lyre; where Typhon lies), Ephorus, Epicharmus' Islands, Aristotle's Constitution of the Geloans and Callimachus.
- These passages almost certainly appear in English in fragment collections (Brill's New Jacoby for Timaeus, Philistus, Artemon and Ephorus; Callimachus editions). That is inferred, not verified in this run.
- From memory, also not re-verified: Gildersleeve 1885 and Farnell 1932 quote the scholia in Greek, and Lefkowitz's Lives of the Greek Poets translates the Vitae.

French:

Spanish: nothing known.
Net: no full translation of any Pythian scholia exists in any modern language that I could find.
item_106.source_text:
Standard edition: A.B. Drachmann, Scholia vetera in Pindari carmina, vol. II: Scholia in Pythionicas (Teubner, Leipzig 1910). It is in the public domain: Drachmann died in 1935, and the edition was published in the US before 1930.
- Scan: archive.org/details/scholiaveterainp02drac (University of Toronto).
- Digital TEI (best working text): OpenGreekAndLatin First1KGreek, urn:cts:greekLit:tlg5034.tlg001b.perseus-grc1, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/OpenGreekAndLatin/First1KGreek/tree/master/data/tlg5034/tlg001b. Attribute it, and note that share-alike applies only if the XML is redistributed.
- Size, from the TEI: P.1 = 89 scholia, about 4,600 Greek words (about 7–8k words translated). All Pythians: about 49k Greek words. P.4: about 14k.
- Also PD: Boeckh 1811–19, vol. II pt. 1 with 'scholia integra' (archive.org pindaroutasozome02pinduoft).
- Only the Fribourg edition, still in progress, will be in copyright.
item_106.research_yield: Hieron's Aetna foundation and Deinomenid dynasty through lost Sicilian historians (Timaeus, Philistus, Artemon, Ephorus); Phalaris' bull (Timaeus vs Callimachus); Typhon's localisations; Epicharmus on Anaxilas; scholia-based dialogue with HSE 2025 Pythians commentary.
item_106.recommendation: Keep. The first unit should be the complete Pythian 1 scholia (Drachmann II, 89 scholia, about 4.6k Greek words, OGL TEI). Before publishing, check overlaps with the BNJ fragments and with Степанцов's P.1 commentary (HSE 2025). Avoid P.4 as the first unit: it overlaps with Latyshev and is about 14k words.

item_107.title_short: Scholia vetera to the Iliad (A, bT, D), Book 6
item_107.ru_found:
I found no full or partial Russian translation of the Iliad scholia, and none of the Book 6 unit. The only Russian versions are scattered excerpts:
(1) В.В. Латышев, «Известия древних писателей о Скифии и Кавказе» I. Its "Scholia in Homerum" and Epimerismi excerpts are at pp. 301–304 and 921, with more in ВДИ 1952. The Russian translation appeared in ВДИ 1947–48. This comes from the project cache (research/raw/ru_series_crosscheck.json), which marks the overlap as "possible". I checked the archive.org scan of vol. I (1890, Latyshev1_djvu.txt), but it ends around p. 290, so the Homer-scholia pages are in a later fascicle I could not reach. Any overlap with Book 6 would be marginal at most (e.g. the Amazons at Il. 6.186).
(2) Studies quote isolated Aristarchean scholia in Russian, e.g. Е.В. Файер on Zenodotus and Aristarchus (cache: CyberLeninka results). I could not check whether Book 6 notes are among them. One example would be the athetesis of 6.433–439.
Checked directly:
- ancientrome.ru Homer index: Gnedich and a second Russian translation, plus an excerpt of Il. VI 1–118, 386–516. No scholia.
- ru.wikipedia «Схолии»: says scholia "обычно не переводят на современные языки" and names no Russian translation.
Caveat: the web search budget was used up, so I could not run the 4 required Russian searches. This verdict rests on the project cache and direct page fetches.
item_107.en_found:
For the corpus, English is partial:
(1) Bill Beck (ed. and tr., Indiana University), "The Ancient Scholia to Homer's Iliad: A Translation", vol. 1 (Books 1–2), CUP 2025, 466 pp., DOI 10.1017/9781009547369. The candidate's "Beck et al." is wrong: the CUP page names Beck as sole editor and translator. The page says nothing about vol. 2 or later volumes.
(2) R. Scott Smith et al., "Mythical Stories in the D Scholia to Homer's Iliad", Manto/Canopos 2023, CC BY 4.0, on ToposText (work 866). It covers the mythological historiai only and omits the non-mythological glosses.
For the Book 6 unit, English exists only as excerpts. ToposText 866 already translates five Book 6 D-narratives:
- 6.35 Pedasos/Phylakos/Leitos
- 6.130 Lycurgus
- 6.153 Sisyphus
- 6.155 Glaucus/Bellerophon/Proitos/Anteia/Aleian plain
- 6.396 Eetion/Plakos/Thebe
The A and bT scholia and the D-glosses of Book 6 have no English translation, apart from scattered quotations in scholarship (e.g. Nünlist 2009; Graziosi–Haubold 2010; Kirk 1990; Stoevesandt's Basel commentary). These quotations are from memory and unverified.
Risk: the CUP series will probably reach Book 6 in a later volume.
item_107.other_found:
I found no French, German, Italian or Spanish translation of the Book 6 scholia, or of the A/bT corpus as a whole (cache plus direct checks; no fresh searches were possible). Related material:
- Joan Pagès Cebrián, "Mythographus Homericus" (UAB thesis 2007). It edits and studies the Iliad historiae. From the cache I could not tell whether it includes a Catalan or Spanish translation.
- Pagès and Villagra (eds.), "Myths on the Margins of Homer" (De Gruyter 2022). These are studies.
- The Homer Multitext project offers downloadable editions of the Venetus A Iliad and scholia (fols. 12r–326v). It has no translations.
item_107.source_text:
The standard modern edition is H. Erbse, Scholia Graeca in Homeri Iliadem (scholia vetera), de Gruyter 1969–88, and it is in copyright.
Public-domain texts:
- W. Dindorf, Scholia Graeca in Homeri Iliadem I–IV (Oxford 1875–77), covering Venetus A and other manuscripts.
- E. Maass, Scholia Graeca in Homeri Iliadem Townleyana V–VI (Oxford 1887–88), covering bT.
- Scans are on archive.org and Google Books; I did not verify the exact identifiers.
Open texts:
- D-scholia: H. van Thiel, Scholia D in Iliadem, proecdosis aucta et correctior 2014, Köln KUPS, open access, https://kups.ub.uni-koeln.de/5586/ (PDF vanthiel.pdf). The page names no CC license.
- Venetus A: Homer Multitext diplomatic texts, https://www.homermultitext.org/texts.html, data at github.com/homermultitext/hmt-archive. The page states no license; check the repository before reusing it.
Recommended practice: translate from Dindorf/Maass plus van Thiel and HMT, and cite Erbse numbers and attributions only as references.
item_107.research_yield:
Possible articles:
- Aristarchus' athetesis of Il. 6.433–439 (Andromache's tactical advice) and ancient norms of female speech.
- Ancient readings of the Glaucus–Diomedes gold-for-bronze exchange.
- The Bellerophon and Lycurgus myths in the Mythographus Homericus compared with Apollodorus.
- bT notes on pathos and enargeia in the Hector–Andromache–Astyanax scene.
- A Russian primer on Alexandrian critical signs.
item_107.recommendation: Keep, at slightly lower priority (4). The Russian gap is real, apart from possible Latyshev Scythica snippets. The English gap for Book 6 holds for the A/bT layers but not the D-narratives, and the CUP series (vol. 1, Books 1–2, 2025) will eventually close it. First unit: the A and bT scholia to Iliad 6, with the D-glosses, taken from Dindorf/Maass, van Thiel and HMT. Cross-reference the five D-historiai already in ToposText 866 rather than presenting them as new to English. Release the Russian version first.

item_108.title_short: Scholia vetera in Apollonium Rhodium (Book 2 scholia; pilot 2.1–647)
item_108.ru_found: The claim "none" is REFUTED as excerpts only. V.V. Latyshev, Известия древних писателей греческих и латинских о Скифии и Кавказе (Scythica et Caucasica), vol. I (St. Petersburg, 1890–1900; reprinted in ВДИ 1947–48), gives Greek text with facing Russian translation. Its author index lists "Ἀπολλώνιος Ῥόδιος 412–424" and "Σχόλια 424–431" (OCR read "424–481", most likely 431; the project cache says 424–437). I checked this index myself in the archive.org OCR, at https://archive.org/details/IzvestiiaDrevnikhPisateleiGrecheskikhILatinskikhOSkifiUKavkaz. That Google scan is missing pp. 307–560, so I could not read the passages themselves. More Apollonius-scholia excerpts appear in the "Дополнения" to Latyshev (ВДИ 1952 №2, appendix; translated by С.П. Кондратьев, А.Я. Абрамович and others, ed. О.В. Кудрявцев; vdi.igh.ru/issues/132/articles/2975). That comes from the project cache; vdi.igh.ru refused the connection, so I could not re-check it. The excerpts cover Scythian, Caucasian and Colchian material, so they likely fall mainly in the Book 2 Pontic periplus (Chalybes, Tibareni, Mossynoeci, Caucasus/Prometheus, Phasis) and in Book 4 (Istros). Further fragment-level Russian versions probably exist inside Russian fragment collections, e.g. of Hesiod, but I did not check them. The ancientrome.ru catalogue has no entry for Apollonius Rhodius, his scholia or Latyshev. Ru-wiki «Схолии» only names the corpus and says scholia are usually untranslated. I found no complete or continuous Russian translation. Caveat: the WebSearch budget was used up before my first query, so I ran none of the required 4 RU searches. I worked from the project cache plus direct page fetches.
item_108.en_found: I found no complete or continuous English translation. BMCR 2014.12.27 (Prodi, reviewing Scholies à Pindare I; bmcr.brynmawr.edu/?p=30623) names only Lachenaud's French translation (2010) for the Apollonius scholia. English versions exist only at fragment level, wherever the scholia quote lost authors. Example: theoi.com/Pontios/Harpyiai.html prints English versions of Hesiod fr. 42 "from Scholiast on Apollonius Rhodius 2.296/2.297" (Loeb-style, translator not named). From general knowledge, not re-checked this run: Brill's New Jacoby entries (Herodorus of Heraclea, Pherecydes, Nymphis, Promathidas and others) and Loeb fragment volumes translate many single scholia. Caveat: the WebSearch budget was used up, so I ran no EN searches. The Hellenistic Bibliography page timed out twice, and the guessed en-wiki page "Scholia on Apollonius of Rhodes" returned 404.
item_108.other_found: French, complete: G. Lachenaud, Scholies à Apollonios de Rhodes (Paris: Les Belles Lettres, coll. Fragments, 2010), confirmed by BMCR 2014.12.27. I found no German, Italian or Spanish complete translation, but could not search for one (budget used up). Georgian: T. Kaukhchishvili's Georgica (Greek with Georgian translation) may excerpt the Colchis scholia; not verified.
item_108.source_text: Public domain: H. Keil (ed.), Scholia vetera e codice Laurentiano, in R. Merkel, Apollonii Argonautica (Leipzig: Teubner, 1854); scans should be on Google Books / archive.org, URL not verified this run. Standard modern edition: C. Wendel, Scholia in Apollonium Rhodium vetera (Berlin: Weidmann, 1935; repr. 1958/1974). Wendel died in 1951, so the edition is public domain in the EU and Russia since 1 January 2022. In the US it is probably protected through 2030 (95 years from 1935 under URAA restoration). It is digitized in the TLG (paywalled). Lachenaud 2010 is in copyright.
item_108.research_yield: Articles on: the Pontic ethnography of the scholia compared with Latyshev's selection; fragments of lost mythographers in the scholia (Herodorus of Heraclea, Pherecydes, Nymphis, Promathidas); Theon, Lucillus and Sophocleus as sources of the scholia; the Amycus and Phineus myth traditions; Hesiodic Catalogue fragments.
item_108.recommendation: Keep. A first complete RU/EN translation still stands, but the Pontic and Colchian scholia overlap with Latyshev's Russian excerpts (Lat. I, 424–431, and the ВДИ 1952 Дополнения). Start with the scholia to 2.1–647 (Amycus, Phineus, Symplegades), which Latyshev barely touches. Base the text on Wendel (Keil for anything US-facing), and use Lachenaud's French for validation.

item_109.title_short: Tzetzes, Commentary on Lycophron's Alexandra (prolegomena + vv. 1–100)
item_109.ru_found:
No full or partial Russian translation of the commentary exists, so the colleague's "none" holds in substance. It is technically wrong, because two Russian works contain short excerpts:
(1) В. В. Латышев, «Известия древних писателей о Скифии и Кавказе», vol. I, pp. 400–406, has excerpts of Tzetzes on Lycophron, reprinted in ВДИ 1947–48, with further items in the 1952 «Дополнения». The same volume, pp. 406–409, has excerpts of the old scholia. Scan: https://archive.org/details/IzvestiiaDrevnikhPisateleiGrecheskikhILatinskikhOSkifiUKavkaz. These excerpts cover Scythian and Caucasian passages, mainly later lines such as Achilles' Dromos, 186 ff. I could not check this page by page today, because the archive.org OCR file is unreadable: Greek OCR was run over the Russian text.
(2) Т. С. Каухчишвили, «О некоторых сведениях Ликофрона и его схолиастов» (Кавказ и Средиземноморье, Тбилиси 1980, pp. 102–108), online at https://ancientrome.ru/publik/article.htm?a=1703369030. It gives about 100–150 words of Russian from Tzetzes on vv. 174/887, 648–649, 679–680 and 1312.
(3) Торшилов's commentary to Гигин (2000) cites Tzetzes on Lycophron but does not translate him.
Nothing else turned up. ancientrome.ru's Lycophron page has only Суриков's translation of the poem (ВДИ 2011). ru.wikipedia «Иоанн Цец», fetched today, lists only the 1969 «Памятники византийской литературы» excerpts (pp. 252–259) and Смыка's Carmina Iliaca, and says nothing of a Russian translation of the Lycophron commentary.
Proposed unit: none of the known Russian excerpts falls in the prolegomena or vv. 1–100.
Method caveat: the WebSearch budget was used up before this run, so I made no new Russian searches today. The status rests on cached verifications (research/raw/odyssey.json, 2026-10-05, Russian queries; research/raw/ru_series_crosscheck.json) and on fetching ru.wikipedia, ancientrome.ru and Latyshev directly today.
item_109.en_found:
The whole commentary exists in English, but only as an unvetted machine translation. ToposText work 860 (https://topostext.org/work/860), re-checked today, runs from Tzetzes' introduction (§intro.1–95, including the survey of kinds of poets), the genos/Life, the hypothesis and the plot summaries to the end of the poem. Its note reads "translated by CHATGPT 4.0 with more speed than accuracy", with prompts by Bruce Hartzler and "a few manual improvements (?)" by Brady Kiesling, made from Scheer's edition. The colleague's "partial" is therefore inaccurate: coverage is complete, but it is machine work.
Human English, excerpts only:
- attalus.org (Andrew Smith), https://www.attalus.org/poetry/lives.html, translates "Tzetzes: The family of Lycophron" from Scheer, about 250 words. This is inside the proposed prolegomena unit.
- Translations of the poem (Mair, Loeb 1921; Mooney 1921; Hornblower, OUP 2015, and Oxford World's Classics 2022; McNelis & Sens 2016) paraphrase or quote scholia in their notes. I did not check how much of Tzetzes Hornblower translates verbatim.
No scholarly human English translation of the commentary, or of the prolegomena as a whole, was found.
item_109.other_found:
I found no modern-language translation of Tzetzes' commentary. The Hellenistic Bibliography's Lycophron page, fetched today, lists only Canter's Latin edition (Geneva 1601, a Latin version of the poem, with Tzetzes in Greek) and editions, indexes (Gualandri 1962, 1965) and studies. All its modern translations (Holzinger, Mair, Mooney, Hurst & Kolde, and others) are of the poem.
Other translations of the poem:
- German: Schade 1999, on vv. 648–819; Horn, Tusculum 2021/22.
- French: Hurst & Kolde, Budé 2008; Lambin 2005; Hummel 2006.
- Italian: Ciaceri; Fusillo–Hurst–Paduano 1991; Gigante Lanzara, BUR 2000.
- Spanish: Mascialino 1956.
None of these translates the scholia.
Potter (Oxford 1697/1702) prints Tzetzes in Greek with Latin notes only.
Not verified:
- a Modern Greek translation;
- Georgian excerpts in Каухчишвили's «Георгика», which would be Colchis-related and outside the unit;
- any recent Italian edition or translation project after Leone's 2002 edition of the old scholia.
No new searches in other languages were possible this run.
item_109.source_text:
Best public-domain text: E. Scheer, Lycophronis Alexandra, vol. II, Scholia continens (Berlin: Weidmann, 1908; reprinted 1958), at https://archive.org/details/lycophronisalexa02lycouoft (the archive.org date field wrongly says 1881). It is still the standard edition of Tzetzes' commentary, and it is public domain. Its archive.org OCR is unusable for Greek, so the page images need fresh Greek OCR. The TLG can be used for checking but not reproduced.
Other public-domain witnesses: C. G. Müller, Isaakiou kai Iōannou tou Tzetzou eis Lykophrona (Leipzig 1811, 3 vols), https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_DPVDAAAAYAAJ; Potter (Oxford 1702), https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_1saTNzUwiEsC.
In copyright: P. L. M. Leone, Scholia vetera et paraphrases in Lycophronis Alexandram (Galatina: Congedo, 2002). It covers only the older layer and the paraphrases, not Tzetzes.
I could not verify whether a newer critical edition of Tzetzes' commentary exists.
item_109.research_yield: Articles could cover: Tzetzes' theory of poetic genres and kinds of poets in the prolegomena; his Life of Lycophron and the Pleiad; how Byzantine readers decoded Hellenistic obscurity; mythographic fragments of lost authors; and a measured comparison of the ToposText ChatGPT draft with a vetted multi-model version.
item_109.recommendation: Keep at priority 4. No human translation of the commentary exists in any modern language: Russian has only scattered Scythian and Colchian excerpts (Латышев; Каухчишвили), and English has only the self-confessedly rough ChatGPT version on ToposText, plus about 250 words of the Life on attalus.org. Start with the prolegomena (kinds of poets, genos, hypothesis), about 4–5k words, then the commentary on vv. 1–100. Fresh OCR of Scheer 1908 is needed.

item_110.title_short: Eustathius of Thessalonica, Parekbolai on the Iliad (prooimion + Book 1)
item_110.ru_found:
Method note: the session's WebSearch budget (200) was already used up, so none of the required RU/EN searches could be run. I relied on the project cache (wave1, odyssey.json, ru_series_crosscheck.json) and direct fetches of known pages.

Findings:
(1) Latyshev, «Известия древних писателей… о Скифии и Кавказе», vol. I (bilingual Greek–Russian). The alphabetical index, read from the archive.org OCR of item IzvestiiaDrevnikhPisateleiGrecheskikhILatinskikhOSkifiUKavkaz, lists 'Παρεκβ. εἰς τὴν Ὁμήρου Ἰλιάδα' at c. pp. 303–311 and the Odyssey at pp. 311–317. These are Scythian/Caucasian excerpts with a facing Russian translation, reprinted in ВДИ 1947–48. The archive.org scan skips roughly pp. 300–550, so I could not see which Iliad passages they are. They are probably in Books 2, 3, 6 and 13 (Catalogue, Amazons, Hippemolgoi). That the proem or Book 1 is affected is unverified but unlikely.
(2) «Памятники византийской литературы IX–XIV вв.» (М.: Наука, 1968/69), checked in the facetia.ru full text (node/4798). Its Eustathius section has only «Из комментариев к „Одиссее“» and «О пленении Фессалоники». There is nothing from the Iliad commentary.
(3) ru.wikipedia «Евстафий Солунский» and Православная энциклопедия т. 17 (pravenc.ru/text/187417.html) list no Russian translation of the Homer commentaries.
(4) Cache: Antishkin (azbyka) says no work of Eustathius is fully translated into Russian.

Not checked: eLibrary, the РГБ catalogue, and Russian articles that may quote single sentences.
item_110.en_found:
Only the proem is in English, and only in part. No English translation of any book of the Iliad commentary itself was found.
- C. J. Herington, 'Homer: a Byzantine perspective', Arion 8 (1969) 432–434: translates the first part of the proem. Verified from n. 4 of B. van den Berg, 'The wise Homer and his erudite commentator: Eustathios' imagery in the proem of the Parekbolai on the Iliad', BMGS 41.1 (2017) 30–44 (cambridge.org, paywalled). Van den Berg cites no complete English proem.
- The sweep's 'Jenkins, Bachrach and Hayton, Notre Dame 2002' (full proem, online) could not be verified. English Wikipedia does not mention it.
- English excerpts are scattered through van den Berg's studies (BMGS 2017 article verified; her 2022 OUP monograph Homer the Rhetorician presumably as well, unverified).
- Odyssey commentary for comparison: Cullhed & Olson, Brill vols I–III (Rhaps. 1–12, 2022–25).
item_110.other_found:
FRENCH, full proem (verified from the PDF): Georgia E. Kolovou, 'Homère chez Eustathe de Thessalonique : la traduction des Proèmes sur l'Iliade et l'Odyssée', Collectanea Christiana Orientalia 15 (2018) 71–118. The complete Iliad proem is translated from van der Valk at c. pp. 93–109, followed by the Odyssey proem. DOI 10.21071/cco.v15i.14434; PDF at https://journals.uco.es/cco/article/view/14434/12916. Book 1 commentary is not included.
LATIN: Alessandro Politi, Florence 1730–35. It covers the proem and Iliad 1–5 with a Latin translation, so the pilot unit is covered (per English Wikipedia).
SPANISH: L. A. Liñares, 'Eustacio y el Proemio de sus Comentarios a la Ilíada', Classica (São Paulo) 11/12 (1998/99) 321–328. I checked the PDF: it analyses and paraphrases the proem and quotes the Greek, but has no translation.
ITALIAN: Pontani, BollClass 21 (2000), translates only the Odyssey proem (Kolovou n. 48). Cesaretti, Allegoristi di Omero a Bisanzio (1991), may render allegorical excerpts; unverified.
GERMAN, MODERN GREEK: none found.
SIDE FINDING (not this item): the 1968/69 «Памятники» volume has a Russian translation of most of the Odyssey prooimion. It runs to about 7.9k characters, ends 'Здесь начинаются комментарии к «Одиссее»', and its n. 303 says it was translated from Stallbaum (Hildesheim 1960); the translator is not named on facetia. This contradicts the cached 'RU none' for the Odyssey preface.
item_110.source_text:
Public domain: G. Stallbaum (ed.), Eustathii archiepiscopi Thessalonicensis Commentarii ad Homeri Iliadem, Leipzig: Weigel 1827–30. Vol. I has the proem and Iliad 1, a reprint of the Rome editio princeps (Bladus 1542–50, also PD). I did not verify a specific scan URL; the archive.org check timed out, and de.wikipedia links only the Odyssey volumes and Devarius' index (archive.org/details/indexineustathii00deva).
In copyright: M. van der Valk, Eustathii … Commentarii ad Homeri Iliadem pertinentes I–IV (Brill 1971–87; indices by Keizer 1995), based on the autograph Laur. plut. 59.2–3. TLG uses it, and it is not open.
