item_150.research_yield:
Possible articles:
- Varro's Stoic etymological method (V.1–10)
- the Argei sacraria list and Roman topography (V.45–54)
- gods and priesthoods (V.57–86)
- Roman calendar and festival terms (VI.12–34)
- Sabine words
- Varro as a source for fragments of Ennius, Naevius, Plautus and the Salian carmen (VII)
- Latin etymological terminology in Russian
item_150.recommendation: Keep as a Russian-gap candidate. It will not be first-ever, because English (Kent; de Melo), Italian, French and Spanish translations exist. Before committing, identify the contents of Karakulakova's 1975 Kalinin excerpt and check the Хрестоматия. Better first unit: Book VI (about 6.3k words: time and festivals), or V.1–74 rather than all of Book V (about 11k words).

item_151.title_short: Lactantius Placidus, Commentary on Statius' Thebaid (Book 1)
item_151.ru_found: The claim of no Russian translation is refuted, but only for fragments. В. В. Латышев, «Известия древних писателей греческих и латинских о Скифии и Кавказе», т. II (Латинские писатели), СПб. 1904, prints a section «SCHOLIA IN STATIVM / Схолии к Стацию» starting on printed p. 221, with Latin and Russian on facing pages. I checked this in the archive.org full text (item Latyshev2, scan leaf 226). It is based on Jahnke's 1898 edition and gives about 19 one-line notes, all on Scythian, Caucasian and Colchian matters: Theb. 1.275, 1.419, 2.421, 3.352, 4.304, 4.506, 4.658, 4.678, 5.145, 5.335, 5.390, 5.458, 5.475, 7.174, 7.524, 8.290, 8.437, 10.288 and Achill. 397. Two of these fall inside the proposed Book 1 unit (1.275, 1.419), but together they are only a few lines. The project crosscheck says Latyshev's Latin authors were reprinted in ВДИ 1949; I did not check that here. There is no ru.wikipedia article on Лактанций Плацид. I could not reach ancientrome.ru (connection reset). Both WebSearch calls were refused because the shared search budget was used up, so I ran none of the required Russian searches. I found no complete or partial Russian translation, but that is not confirmed by searching.
item_151.en_found: No complete or published scholarly English translation found; en/de/fr/it/es Wikipedia list none. de.wikipedia links an amateur work-in-progress page, hellenicfaith.com/lactantius-placidus/ (translator credited as "Ɔ. Martiana", no licence). It has about 32 theological excerpts across Books 1–11, roughly 2–2.5k words. Book 1 items include 1.205–206, 1.258, 1.615–616 and the Mithras note on 1.717–720. The Mithras scholion is probably also translated in English Mithraism studies, but I did not verify that. WebSearch was unavailable, so I could not run the required English searches (e.g. for dissertations).
item_151.other_found: German: B. Bunte, «Lateinische Mythographen übersetzt», Heft 1 «Lactantius Placidus» (Bremen 1852; archive.org bub_gb_HZqBkNiBT9kC). de.wikisource lists it under translations, but the title page and preface show it translates the Ovid summaries (Argumenta / Narrationes fabularum), not the Statius commentary, so it does not count. I found no French, Italian or Spanish translation in Wikipedia, Wikisource, Wikidata or Open Library; Open Library lists only Latin editions. Scholarship: Brugnoli 1988, Sweeney's Prolegomena, Berlincourt 2013 on the exegetical tradition. Not checked by search: Budé, Valla, Gredos and Tusculum catalogues.
item_151.source_text: Best public-domain text: R. Jahnke (ed.), «Lactantii Placidi qui dicitur Commentarios in Statii Thebaida et Commentarium in Achilleida», Leipzig: Teubner 1898. It is on archive.org as https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_fYj9nL6HlREC (Public Domain Mark 1.0, 542 scans) and on Google Books as id fYj9nL6HlREC. There is also Kohlmann's older partial edition of Thebaid 3.1–323 (archive.org). The standard modern edition is R. D. Sweeney, «Lactantii Placidi in Statii Thebaida commentum» vol. I, Teubner, Stuttgart/Leipzig 1997 (ISBN 3-8154-1823-2), still in copyright. Its fuller manuscript-based text differs from Jahnke's, so variants should be checked against it and only cited. digilibLT (digiliblt.uniupo.it, author AUT000120, work DLT000323) hosts a Latin text, but the site was unreachable, so its edition basis and licence are unknown.
item_151.research_yield: Articles on the Mithras scholion (Theb. 1.717–720) and the commentator's syncretistic theology, his mythographic sources compared with the Vatican Mythographers and Servius, citations of lost poets, the late-antique dating question, and medieval reception of Statius. Also the first Russian treatment of a major Latin commentary.
item_151.recommendation: Keep. Correct the Russian status to "excerpts only": Latyshev 1904 has about 19 Scythian notes, two of them from Book 1. Still pilot the full Book 1 commentary from Jahnke 1898, checking against Sweeney 1997 and crediting Latyshev for 1.275 and 1.419.

item_152.title_short: Scholia Bobiensia in Ciceronem (Pro Sestio + In Vatinium)
item_152.ru_found: No Russian translation found, but the check is incomplete. The session's web-search limit (200 calls per turn, shared across agents) was already used up, so none of the required Russian searches ran (the first query, "Боббиенские схолии Цицерон перевод", was refused). Direct checks: ancientrome.ru (the Asconius and Cicero index pages) could not be reached (connection reset, also through curl). ru.wikipedia has no article "Боббиенские схолии" and no page "Речь в защиту Публия Сестия" (404). Not checked: cyberleninka, elibrary, simposium, the Литературные памятники Cicero volumes and the РГБ catalogue. Unverified memory: the standard Russian translations of Pro Sestio and In Vatinium only cite the scholiast in their notes. The "none" claim is not refuted, but it still needs a proper search pass.
item_152.en_found: attalus.org/translate/bobiensia.html (translator not named, updated 29.02.16) gives excerpts from 11 speeches. Most of it covers the lost speeches: In Clodium et Curionem (30+ passages) and De aere alieno Milonis (25+), plus De rege Alexandrino (9) and Pro Flacco (13). For the proposed unit it has only one passage on Pro Sestio (the introduction) and nothing on In Vatinium. So the corpus is partially translated, but the proposed unit has only an introductory excerpt. Unverified memory: Crawford, Fragmentary Speeches (1984/1994), gives the scholia on the lost speeches with English translation. Kaster's Pro Sestio (2006) translates only the speech. The planned English searches did not run because of the search limit.
item_152.other_found: None found. The de- and it.wikipedia articles list editions (Mai 1814/1828, Ehrle facsimile 1906, Hildebrandt 1907, Stangl 1912) and studies (Shackleton Bailey, AJP 1983; P.L. Schmidt, HLL 5, 1989), but no translation into German, Italian or any other language. Their only translation is the attalus English excerpts. Budé, Tusculum, BUR, Gredos and Valla were not searched because of the search limit.
item_152.source_text: The standard edition is T. Stangl, Ciceronis orationum scholiastae, vol. 2 (Vienna/Leipzig 1912). It is public domain (Stangl died 1921), and no later critical edition exists. Also PD: P. Hildebrandt, Scholia in Ciceronis orationes Bobiensia (Teubner 1907). An open Latin text based on Hildebrandt with Stangl's page numbers is at attalus.org/latin/bobiensia3.html. On that page Pro Sestio is Stangl pp. 125–144 (with lacunae of 2, 2, 6 and 16 pages) and In Vatinium is pp. 145–152, complete to "EXPLICIT". The unit is about 28 Stangl pages, roughly 7–9k words.
item_152.research_yield: How reliable the late-antique scholiast is on 58–56 BCE (Sestius' tribunate, Clodian violence, Vatinius' career and lex Vatinia); interrogatio as a genre; school rhetoric (status theory) in Cicero commentary; comparing Bobiensia with Asconius and Kaster.
item_152.recommendation: Keep. Pro Sestio + In Vatinium (Stangl 125–152) is the least-translated part of the corpus in every language, so it is a sound first unit; In Vatinium alone (pp. 145–152, complete) makes a quick pilot. Re-run the Russian and English searches before committing.

item_153.ru_found: I could not run any web searches because the shared WebSearch budget for this turn was used up; both attempts returned no results. All findings below come from fetching specific pages directly. The 'none' claim is wrong. The ru.wikipedia article 'Боэций' that the colleague cited lists, in its 'Переводы' section: 'Комментарий к «Категориям» Аристотеля / Пер. А. В. Аполлонова // Антология средневековой мысли. Т. 1. СПб, 2001. С. 113—160.' I checked the raw wikitext of the article. The anthology was edited by S. S. Neretina and published by РХГИ. I could not see its table of contents, so I could not confirm which book or books the 48 pages cover. They are most likely Book I or a large part of it. If so, the proposed pilot unit is probably already in Russian. Other Russian items on the same page do not include this commentary: Nauka 1990/1996 (Porphyry commentary and tractates), Voprosy filosofii 1999 no. 1 (Introductio ad syllogismos categoricos), and Lebedev 2012 (De musica). I found no complete Russian translation of Books I–IV.
item_153.en_found: No English translation found. The SEP 'Boethius' article says the Categories commentary 'must still be read' in PL 64, and its translations list has no version of it. The SEP 'Medieval Theories of the Categories' bibliography lists only the Migne edition (PL 64:159–294, 1847; Brepols reprint 1979). The Ancient Commentators on Aristotle list on en.wikipedia has only Boethius on De interpretatione: Blank & Kretzmann 1998, and A. Smith 2010 and 2011. Because no searches were possible, a dissertation or partial translation could exist that I did not see.
item_153.other_found: No French, German, Italian or Spanish translation came up in the SEP bibliographies or on Wikipedia. I could not search Budé/CUF, Tusculum or Italian series because the search budget was used up, so this is unverified.
item_153.source_text: The best available text is Migne, Patrologia Latina 64, cols. 159–294 (Paris 1847; Brepols reprint 1979). It is public domain, and scans of PL 64 are on Google Books and archive.org. The text goes back to the Basel Opera omnia (Glareanus, 1570). There is no modern critical edition: SEP says M. Asztalos's edition has been in preparation for many years. Boethius's own translation of the Aristotle lemmata has a critical edition in Aristoteles Latinus I.1–5 (Minio-Paluello, 1961), which is still in copyright but useful for checking the lemmata. Pierre Hadot's 1959 article on a fragment of a lost second Categories commentary (cod. Bern. 363) is also relevant. The Migne text has errors, so the edition apparatus is weak.
item_153.research_yield: Articles could examine how Boethius used Porphyry's lost commentary to Gedalius and his intentio ('words signifying things'), how he formed Latin terms (substantia/subsistentia, accidens), the proposed second commentary, and how his reading compares with Simplicius and Dexippus. Interest is mainly specialist.
item_153.recommendation: Demote. Book I is probably already in Russian (Apollonov 2001, pp. 113–160), so the proposed pilot is unsafe. Keep the work only as an English-first project, or for the books Apollonov did not cover, once the anthology's contents have been checked: Book II is the most likely first unit.

item_154.title_short: Terentianus Maurus, De litteris (praefatio + De litteris, vv. 1–278)
item_154.ru_found: I found no Russian translation of the whole poem or of the proposed unit. The only Russian text I found is a proverb-style rendering of v. 1286 ("Pro captu lectoris habent sua fata libelli"), which lies outside the proposed unit. It appears on ru.wikipedia 'Habent sua fata libelli' with no translator named. Ru.wikipedia 'Теренциан Мавр' lists only Keil's edition and Malein's ЭСБЕ article, with no translations. The ЭСБЕ article by А. И. Малеин (ru.wikisource 'ЭСБЕ/Теренциан Мавр') names Lachmann 1836 and Keil 1874 and mentions no translation. LIMITATION: the shared WebSearch budget was used up before my first query, so none of the required 4 Russian searches ran. I could not check ancientrome.ru (connection reset), simposium, cyberleninka, elibrary, the RSL catalogue, or the 1936 anthology 'Античные теории языка и стиля' (Фрейденберг; Алетейя reprint 1996), which might contain excerpts on letters. Scattered quotations in handbooks such as Тронский's historical grammar are likely but unverified.
item_154.en_found: I found no English translation of the whole work or of the proposed unit. En.wikipedia 'Terentianus Maurus' lists the Santen 1825 and Keil editions and no translations; the Teuffel-Schwabe it cites is a literary history, not a translation. En.wikipedia 'Habent sua fata libelli' gives only Camden's 1607 rendering of v. 1286. Neither de.wikipedia nor it.wikipedia lists any English translation. English renderings of individual phonetic passages probably appear in handbooks such as W. S. Allen's Vox Latina, but that comes from memory and is unverified. None of the required 4 English searches could run because the WebSearch budget was used up.
item_154.other_found: German (partial, missed by the sweep): Jan-Wilhelm Beck, 'Terentianus Maurus, De syllabis. Hrsg., übers. und erl.', Göttingen: Vandenhoeck & Ruprecht 1993 (Diss. München 1991). It covers De syllabis only (vv. 279–1299 by my recollection), so it does not include the proposed unit; source is de.wikipedia and it.wikipedia. Italian (complete): Chiara Cignolo, 'Terentiani Mauri De litteris, De syllabis, De metris', Hildesheim: Olms 2002, 2 vols; vol. 1 holds the introduction, critical text and Italian translation, vol. 2 the commentary (source: it.wikipedia). The sweep's second Italian translation could not be identified. Portuguese (complete, annotated): Isabela Maia Pereira de Jesus, 'Terentiani Mauri De Litteris, De Syllabis, De Metris: estudo crítico e tradução anotada', MA thesis, UNESP 2020, https://repositorio.unesp.br/handle/11449/192861 (confirmed from the abstract). French ×1, as claimed by the sweep: unverified, because the thesis PDF that supposedly records it is 123 MB and I could not read it.
item_154.source_text: Public domain: H. Keil, Grammatici Latini VI (Leipzig: Teubner 1874). On ru.wikipedia, v. 1286 is cited as GL VI p. 363. It is digitised on archive.org, and the Keil text is also online in Musisque Deoque (https://www.mqdq.it/indici/autori/idAuthors/151), which lists Keil 1874 as its base. Older public-domain editions are K. Lachmann (Berlin: Reimer 1836) and L. Santen / J. van Lennep (1825, with commentary); the text is also printed in Gaisford's Hephaestion (Oxford 1855, archive.org enchiridion01heph and enchiridion02heph). The only manuscript (Bobbio, found 1493) is lost, and the text rests on the editio princeps (Milan 1497). The standard modern critical edition is Cignolo (Olms 2002, Collectanea Grammatica Latina) and is in copyright, as is Beck 1993 for De syllabis. Practical plan: translate from Keil and check against Cignolo's apparatus and line numbering.
item_154.research_yield: Ancient descriptions of Latin sounds (h, f, x, z, vowel quantity) compared with Marius Victorinus, Quintilian and Priscian; poetics of a didactic poem whose metres demonstrate themselves; Caesius Bassus tradition; African Latin and dating; reception of 'habent sua fata libelli'.
item_154.recommendation: Keep: no Russian or English translation of the proposed unit turned up. The sweep missed Beck's German De syllabis (1993), but that strengthens the choice of the preface (vv. 1–84) plus De litteris (vv. 85–278) as the first unit, since no German exists for those lines. Before committing, re-run the Russian and English searches the exhausted budget blocked, especially the 1936 'Античные теории языка и стиля' anthology and Google Books for English.

item_155.ru_found: I found no Russian translation of the Commenta Bernensia (CB) or the Adnotationes super Lucanum, whole or partial, and none of the Book 1 commentary. The checks were limited, though. The shared web-search budget was used up before my first query ran, so I made no searches at all, in Russian or in English, and worked only from pages I could open directly. ancientrome.ru would not load (connection reset), so its catalogue is not re-checked. What I could check: Russian Wikipedia 'Тевтат' and 'Езус' only retell the content of the scholia on 1.445 ('Вторая бернская глосса к Лукану (I, 445) прямо называет Тевтата Марсом'; Esus is cited to Usener 1869, p. 32), with no translation. 'Таранис' cites N. S. Shirokova, 'Галльский Юпитер Цезаря — кельтский Таранис Лукана' (in the Frolov Festschrift, СПбГУ 2008, pp. 354–360). It may quote the 1.445 scholium in Russian, but I could not confirm this. Russian translations of MacCulloch (Центрполиграф 2004) and Guyonvarc'h–Le Roux (2001) may also retell or quote this passage, also unconfirmed. The 1951 Литпамятники Lucan (Ostroumov/Petrovsky) has no scholia translation. Still to check: elibrary.ru, cyberleninka.ru and Shirokova's books (2000, 2004).
item_155.en_found: No full or continuous English translation of CB or the Adnotationes found. Confirmed excerpts: (1) the CB god-catalogue on Lucan 1.445 (Teutates, Esus, Taranis and their human sacrifices). English Wikipedia ('Teutates', 'Esus') gives it in English 'after the German' of Hofeneder 2008, vol. 2, p. 317. This passage is in the proposed Book 1 unit. (2) Shipley, Geographers of the Ancient Greek World, vol. 1 (CUP 2024), p. 270, translates a Timosthenes fragment found only in CB. (3) Shirley Werner, The Transmission and Scholia to Lucan's Bellum Civile (1998), edits and translates the scholia of Beinecke MS 673. That is a related, overlapping collection, not CB or the Adnotationes, and which books it covers is unknown. Koch & Carey's Celtic Heroic Age and similar Celtic sourcebooks probably include the 1.445 passage too (unverified).
item_155.other_found: German: Andreas Hofeneder, Die Religion der Kelten in den antiken literarischen Zeugnissen, vol. 2 (Wien: ÖAW 2008), translates the Celtic-related CB and Adnotationes passages, including 1.445 (p. 317). These are excerpts. P. Bachmann, 'Commenta und Adnotationes: Proben antiker Kommentierarbeit am Lukan (Buch I und IX)', a PhD thesis (Frankfurt a.M., 1974), covers exactly Book 1. Whether it includes German translations is unknown, and this is the main thing to check before choosing the Book 1 unit. Graf 1991 (Archäologie der Schweiz 14:136–143) discusses the 1.445 catalogue, and may give it in German (unverified). Italian: Paolo Esposito (ed.), Gli scolii a Lucano ed altra scoliastica latina (2004), and Esposito in Brill's Companion to Lucan (2011, pp. 453–463) are studies; I could not confirm any translation in them. French excerpts of 1.445 probably appear in druid and Celtic-religion books (Guyonvarc'h–Le Roux; unverified). No Budé, Tusculum, Valla or Gredos translation known.
item_155.source_text: CB: H. Usener, Scholia in Lucani Bellum civile, pars I: Commenta Bernensia (Leipzig: Teubner 1869; reprinted 1967). It is public domain; the 1869 scan is at https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_RJFfAAAAMAAJ (Public Domain Mark, PDF and full text, 325 pp.). It is still the standard and only complete edition of CB, but it is outdated (Werner 1994, HSCP 96:343–368). Adnotationes: J. Endt, Adnotationes super Lucanum (Teubner 1909), public domain by date (I found no digitized copy). G. A. Cavajoni, Supplementum adnotationum super Lucanum (1979/1984/1990), is in copyright. Both main manuscripts can be checked directly: Bern, Burgerbibliothek Cod. 370 and Cod. 45 on e-codices (https://www.e-codices.ch/en/searchresult/list/one/bbb/0370 and /0045).
item_155.research_yield: Possible articles: the Book 1 note on Celtic gods (1.445) set in its full context; late antique strata and sources (lost geographers such as Timosthenes; Livy and Caesar material); how CB compares with Servius on historical and geographical notes; and the ancient explanations of Lucan's astronomy and Stoic ideas.
item_155.recommendation: Keep, with the claim corrected. There is no full translation in any language, but English and German excerpts exist, including Book 1's 1.445 note. Start with CB Book 1 from Usener 1869 (public domain), checked against the Bern 370 manuscript, after checking the Bachmann 1974 thesis. A strong alternative unit for this editor is CB plus the Adnotationes on Book 10.1–52 (Alexander's tomb).

item_156.ru_found: This refutes the sweep's 'none'. No Russian translation of the whole work exists, but two coherent sections do. (1) А. В. Гараджа, «Халкидий о демонах: фрагменты "Комментария на Тимей Платона" (перевод и комментарии)», ΣΧΟΛΗ 17.2 (2023), 1109–1121, DOI 10.25205/1995-4328-2023-17-2-1109-1121, PDF at classics.nsu.ru/schole/assets/files/17-2-garaja.pdf. It translates chs. 120 and 127–136 (demonology) from Waszink 1975. I read the PDF. It cites no earlier Russian translation of Calcidius. (2) Е. В. Афонасин & А. С. Кузнецова, «Нумений из Апамеи. Фрагменты и свидетельства», ΣΧΟΛΗ I.1 (2007), at classics.nsu.ru/schole/1/schole_numenius_all.pdf. As fr. 52 des Places it gives a full Russian translation of Calcidius chs. 295–299 (Numenius on matter). I read the PDF. (3) Indirect excerpts: Dillon, «Средние платоники» (transl. Афонасин, СПб.: Алетейя, 2002), pp. 386–393, which discusses Calcidius; and Лосев, ИАЭ т. 8.1 (1992), pp. 127–176, which surveys him. Probably also scattered Chrysippean fate passages, such as ch. 144, in Столяров's «Фрагменты ранних стоиков» (SVF), but I could not verify this. The pilot unit, chs. 142–190 on fate: I found no Russian translation. Garadja's RSF project 23-18-00971 (2023–25, rscf.ru) lists only the demons installment, with no plan for the fate section. I scanned the contents pages of every ΣΧΟΛΗ issue from 2007 to 2026: the only Calcidius entries are (1) and (2). Caveat: the WebSearch budget was used up before any search ran, so this check rests on direct fetches only (ru/en/de/it/es Wikipedia, the ΣΧΟΛΗ archive, the two PDFs, the RSF page). I did not check Платоновские исследования, ВДИ, Вестник ПСТГУ or the RSL catalogue.
item_156.en_found: Full: John Magee, Calcidius, On Plato's Timaeus, Dumbarton Oaks Medieval Library 41 (Cambridge MA: Harvard UP, 2016), with Latin and facing English. The en, de, it and es Wikipedia articles all confirm it; the DOML list shows vol. 41. Partial: J. den Boeft, Calcidius on Demons (Commentarius ch. 127–136) (Leiden: Brill, 1977), which Garadja's bibliography lists as a translation. Den Boeft, Calcidius on Fate: His Doctrine and Sources (Brill, 1970) is a study of chs. 142–190; I did not verify whether it gives a running translation. Van Winden, Calcidius on Matter (1959) is a study. An undated online 'Blitz Latin' machine translation is linked from en.wikipedia.
item_156.other_found: French, full: B. Bakhouche (with L. Brisson), Calcidius, Commentaire au Timée de Platon, 2 vols (Paris: Vrin, 2011), critical edition with translation. Italian, full: C. Moreschini (with M. Bertolini, L. Nicolini, I. Ramelli), Calcidio, Commentario al «Timeo» di Platone (Milano: Bompiani, Il Pensiero Occidentale, 2003), Latin after Waszink with Italian facing. Spanish, full: Traducción y comentario del Timeo de Platón (Zaragoza, 2014, ISBN 978-84-7956-134-5); es/it Wikipedia do not name the translator, and I could not confirm one. German: no complete printed translation found; de.wikipedia links a web translation by Anton von Euw and 12koerbe.de (Timaeus translation part), both unverified in scope.
item_156.source_text: Public domain: J. Wrobel, Platonis Timaeus interprete Chalcidio cum eiusdem commentario (Leipzig: Teubner, 1876; reprinted Frankfurt 1963). Scans are generally available (Internet Archive, Google Books), but I did not verify a URL this pass. Older PD editions: Meursius 1617, Fabricius 1718. The standard edition, J. H. Waszink, Plato Latinus IV (London/Leiden: Warburg Institute/Brill, 1962; 2nd ed. 1975), is in copyright, as are the texts of Bakhouche 2011 and Magee 2016. Wrobel's text is inferior to Waszink's, so the translation should start from Wrobel and check Waszink's readings at doubtful places.
item_156.research_yield: Calcidius's fate doctrine (fate and providence, anti-Stoic polemic, astrology) against Ps.-Plutarch De fato, Nemesius and Alcinous; Latin fate terminology and Russian equivalents; Chartres reception. Complements Garadja's demons installment.
item_156.recommendation: Downgrade (priority 2 on the 1–5 scale, 5 = highest) but keep as a Russian-only gap. The work has full English, French, Italian and Spanish translations, and Garadja is translating Calcidius sections into Russian, so the editor should contact him or check his plans before starting. Best first unit: chs. 142–159 (the core fate and providence doctrine, about 4–5k words), from Wrobel checked against Waszink.

item_157.ru_found: I found no Russian translation, but the check is limited. The shared WebSearch budget for this run was already used up, so none of the planned Russian or English searches ran. I fetched pages directly instead. (1) ru.wikipedia, «Фабий Планциад Фульгенций»: gives the Russian title «О значении Вергилия в свете философии» but no translation. Russian translations are listed only for the Mitologiae: Гусейнов 1988 (partial, «Античность как тип культуры»), Можелян 2012/2014 and Болгов 2015–16 (Belgorod, «Классическая и византийская традиция»). (2) Gregory Hays's Fulgentius bibliography (uva.theopenscholar.com/gregory-hays/fulgentius-bibliography, latest dated entry 2023): the only Russian items are Гусейнов's 1987 and 1988 work on the Mitologiae; no Russian Continentia is listed. (3) ru.wikipedia «Энеида» mentions Fulgentius but no translation. ancientrome.ru did not respond (connection reset). I could not check cyberleninka, elibrary or the RSL catalogue, nor the 1970/1998 «Памятники средневековой латинской литературы» anthologies. Possible excerpts there or in post-2016 Belgorod volumes cannot be ruled out.
item_157.en_found: There are several complete English translations, per Hays's bibliography. (a) T.A. McVeigh, Fordham PhD dissertation 1964, appendix translation; Hays does not state the language, but McVeigh is cited as an English translator elsewhere. (b) Lynn C. Stokes, Tufts dissertation 1969, Helm's text with facing English. (c) Stokes, 'The Exposition of the Contents of Virgil', Classical Folia 26 (1972) 27–63, Latin with English. (d) L.G. Whitbread, Fulgentius the Mythographer (Ohio State UP 1971); Hays calls it 'all but worthless'. (e) O.B. Hardison Jr., in Preminger et al., Classical and Medieval Literary Criticism (New York 1974) 324–340. (f) G. Hays in Ziolkowski & Putnam, The Virgilian Tradition (Yale 2008) 660–672, abridged text and translation. (g) Hays has announced an OUP volume of all four authentic works with text and English translation; it is still forthcoming.
item_157.other_found: Italian: T. Agozzino & F. Zanlucchi, Fabio Planciade Fulgenzio. Expositio Virgilianae continentiae (Padova 1972), Helm's text with Italian translation and commentary. F. Rosa, Fulgenzio. Commento all'Eneide (Milano 1997), text, translation and notes. F. Bertini, Autori latini in Africa (1974), excerpt only (Helm pp. 90.20–93.19). French: É. Wolff, Fulgence. Virgile dévoilé (Presses universitaires du Septentrion 2009), the first French translation (confirmed by Venuti's BMCR review). Neither Hays nor BMCR lists a German or Spanish translation. Hays's German item (Stöcker) concerns De aetatibus.
item_157.source_text: The best source text, and the only critical edition, is R. Helm, Fabii Planciadis Fulgentii V.C. Opera (Leipzig: Teubner 1898), which is public domain. Scans are at archive.org/details/operafulg00fulguoft and archive.org/details/fabiiplanciadis00fulggoog, and at Google Books id 3d9QFqv1QJcC. The 1970 Teubner reprint adds J. Préaux's addenda, which are in copyright, but the text is unchanged. Agozzino, Rosa, Wolff and Hays all reprint Helm's text, so there is no copyrighted modern critical text. A digital text is at thelatinlibrary.com/fulgentius/fulgentius5.shtml. It has garbled characters, does not name its edition and may be truncated, so check it against the Helm scan.
item_157.research_yield: This would be the first Russian version of a key Late Antique reading of the Aeneid. It supports articles on: Fulgentius' moral allegory compared with Servius and Macrobius; the dialogue in which Vergil himself appears; and its reception in Bernardus Silvestris and Boccaccio. It also gives a test case for checking LLM output against four existing translations.
item_157.recommendation: Keep. The Russian gap holds as far as I could check, and the evidence for full English and other translations is stronger than the sweep stated. Translate the whole work from Helm 1898, using Rosa, Wolff and Stokes as control translations for Fulgentius' obscure Latin. Before publishing, run a quick Russian catalogue check (elibrary, the RSL catalogue, the «Памятники средневековой латинской литературы» anthologies).

item_158.title_short: John Philoponus, De opificio mundi (Book III pilot)
item_158.ru_found: Only excerpts are published, but a Russian translation is being prepared for publication, so the "untranslated" claim does not hold for planning. (1) G. I. Benevich, excerpts from «О сотворении мира», in Антология восточно-христианской богословской мысли, vol. 2 (Москва: Никея; СПб.: РХГА, 2009), pp. 55–62, confirmed via ru.wikipedia «Иоанн Филопон». (2) ΣΧΟΛΗ 20.2 (2026) has a cluster of three articles on Philoponus' Opif.: O. N. Nogovitsin, pp. 885–921, on IV.4; T. A. Shchukin, pp. 922–938, on VII.1–3; D. A. Chernoglazov, pp. 939–957, on V.1 (https://classics.nsu.ru/schole/page48.html; PDFs at https://classics.nsu.ru/schole/assets/files/20-2-*.pdf). All three quote long passages in an unpublished Russian translation by T. A. Senina. Nogovitsin n. 4: «Рус. пер. Т.А. Сениной под редакцией Д.А. Черноглазова» (full text of IV.4). Shchukin n. 3: «Здесь и далее рус. пер. Т. А. Сениной». Chernoglazov n. 3 says the edited Senina translation of Book V «в настоящее время готовится к публикации». All three are funded by the IMLI RAN grant «Русская и европейская классика в XXI веке: подготовка цифровых научных комментированных изданий» (agreement no. 075-15-2024-549, 2024). So at least Books IV, V and VII are translated and an annotated edition is on its way; the whole treatise, including Book III, is likely covered. The same group has published related studies: Nogovitsin & Shchukin 2021 (ESSE 6.1, Book I), Nogovitsin 2022, Shchukin 2020/2022, Baranov 2022, Varlamova 2017/2020. Caveat: the WebSearch budget for this turn was used up before my first query. So the required 4 Russian and 4 English searches were not run. Evidence comes from direct fetches of ru/en/fr/de/it Wikipedia, SEP, archive.org, the ΣΧΟΛΗ tables of contents and the full text of the three PDFs. azbyka.ru has no Philoponus entry.
item_158.en_found: No complete English translation found. en.wikipedia (De opificio mundi article and John Philoponus article) and the SEP Philoponus bibliography (Wildberg) list only Reichardt 1897 and Scholten 1997 (German). Short English renderings of key passages, such as the impetus imparted to the heavenly bodies in Opif. I.12, circulate in the scholarship. R. Sorabji, The Philosophy of the Commentators 200–600 AD: A Sourcebook (2005), vol. 2 (Physics), very probably includes some Opif. passages, but this is from memory and was not checked against the volume. No announced English translation was found, though the search was limited (see the RU caveat).
item_158.other_found: FRENCH, full translation, missed by the sweep: Jean Philopon, La Création du monde, trans. M.-C. Rosset and M.-H. Congourdeau, Paris: Migne, 2004 (cited on fr.wikipedia «Jean Philopon»). As far as I recall it is no. 87 in Les Pères dans la foi and covers all 7 books; neither detail was checked. GERMAN, full: C. Scholten, Johannes Philoponos, De opificio mundi / Über die Erschaffung der Welt, Fontes Christiani 23/1–3, Herder 1997, Greek–German (confirmed on de.wikipedia and in the ΣΧΟΛΗ bibliographies). ITALIAN: A. Longo & T. F. Ottobrini (eds.), L'esegesi aristotelica alla prova dell'esegesi biblica. Il De opificio mundi di Giovanni Filopono (Edizioni di Storia e Letteratura, 2023) is a volume of studies, not a translation. Spanish: none found (not searched). So the work already has two complete modern-language translations, French and German.
item_158.source_text: Public domain: W. Reichardt (ed.), Joannis Philoponi De opificio mundi libri VII, Leipzig: Teubner, 1897, 372 pp. Full-text PDF, djvu and txt at https://archive.org/details/joannisphiliponi00philuoft. The standard modern text is C. Scholten, Fontes Christiani 23 (Herder 1997), which is in copyright. Current scholarship cites Opif. by Scholten's page and line (e.g. 380.5–382.20). A Neoscholia translation would need a Reichardt-to-Scholten concordance and a check of Scholten's textual changes.
item_158.research_yield: Book III's critique of the tabernacle cosmos of Theodore of Mopsuestia and Cosmas, the firmament and the waters above it, and impetus applied to celestial motion. The IMLI RAN group is already publishing intensively on this treatise, so there is little Russian-language novelty and strong competition.
item_158.recommendation: Drop from the Russian track: an IMLI RAN team (Senina/Chernoglazov/Nogovitsin) has an annotated Russian translation in preparation, and full French (2004) and German (1997) translations already exist. If kept at all, do an English-only Book III pilot, ideally only after asking Nogovitsin's group whether their edition covers Book III and when it will appear.

item_159.title_short: Anonymous, Commentary on Plato's Theaetetus (P.Berol. 9782), cols. I–XI pilot
item_159.ru_found: Limits: the shared WebSearch budget ran out on the first query, so I could not run the required 4 Russian and 4 English searches. I checked direct pages instead. (1) ΣΧΟΛΗ: I went through the tables of contents of all 40 issues, vols. I–XX (2007–2026), on schole.ru, plus the ΣΧΟΛΗ Supplements book series vols. I–VIII. The journal has no translation of the commentary. One incidental excerpt refutes a strict 'none'. E. V. Afonasin, 'Протагор из Абдеры. Фрагменты и свидетельства', ΣΧΟΛΗ 14.1 (2020) 309–338, DOI 10.25205/1995-4328-2020-14-1-309-338, translates P.Berol. inv. 9782 col. 2.3–8 (= CPF Protagoras 1T). That is one sentence, and it falls inside the proposed pilot unit (prologue). I confirmed it by extracting the PDF text. No other column of the papyrus appears there. (2) The Russian translation of Dillon, 'Средние платоники' (Е. В. Афонасин, 2002; confirmed through ru.wikipedia 'Средний платонизм') discusses the Anonymous and may quote short passages. I did not check this. (3) ru.wikipedia has no article on the commentary. ru.wikipedia 'Средний платонизм' does not mention it. Not checked: CyberLeninka, eLibrary, Платоновские исследования, ancientrome.ru and the RSL catalogue.
item_159.en_found: No published complete English translation was found. Unpublished: G. Boys-Stones, '(anon.) Commentary on the Theaetetus P.Berol. inv. 9782 draft translation', academia.edu, 2019 (listed on enwiki). It may be complete, but I could not check its coverage because academia.edu returned 403. Published excerpts: (a) Sedley 1996, 'Three Platonist Interpretations of the Theaetetus' (Form and Argument in Late Plato, OUP). Bonazzi 2008 quotes col. IV 17–27 as 'trans. Sedley'. (b) Boys-Stones, Platonist Philosophy 80 BC to AD 250 (CUP 2018). Enwiki cites its 'Epistemology' chapter, pp. 367–393, but the CUP page returned 403, so its contents are not verified. (c) Bonazzi, Laval théologique et philosophique 64.3 (2008) 597–605, gives English renderings of passages such as LXX 12–26. Long–Sedley, The Hellenistic Philosophers (1987), probably includes the oikeiosis and growing-argument passages, but this is not verified. The pilot unit, cols. I–XI with the oikeiosis digression, is the part most often excerpted in English.
item_159.other_found: Italian: G. Bastianini and D. Sedley, 'Commentarium in Platonis Theaetetum', CPF III (Firenze: Olschki, 1995) 227–562. Enwiki lists it as Greek with Italian. It is the standard edition with translation and commentary. German: B. Hene, Ein anonymer Kommentar zu Platons Theaitetos und seine philosophische Bedeutung (Diss. Leuven, 2018), per enwiki. Diels–Schubart 1905 (BKT II) has German front matter; I did not confirm whether it includes a German translation. Portuguese: R. Matoso, Revista Archai 27 (2019), is a study and cites only Diels–Schubart and CPF, no translation. No French, Spanish or modern Greek translation was found, but the search was not exhaustive.
item_159.source_text: Public-domain text: H. Diels and W. Schubart (with J. L. Heiberg), Anonymer Kommentar zu Platons Theaetet (Papyrus 9782), Berliner Klassikertexte II, Berlin: Weidmann, 1905. It is on archive.org as a PDF and text file: https://archive.org/details/anonymerkommenta00diel. It is public domain in the US. In the EU the 25-year right for scholarly editions (Germany §70 UrhG) has long expired. Schubart died in 1960, so his German prose may stay protected until the end of 2030 in 70-years-after-death countries. The archive.org Greek OCR is poor and will need re-keying. Standard edition: Bastianini–Sedley, CPF III (Olschki 1995). Its translation and commentary are in copyright. Italian law gives critical editions of public-domain texts only 20 years' protection (art. 85-quater L. 633/1941, from memory, not checked online), which would have expired in 2015. If so, the CPF readings could probably be used with credit, but this needs checking. The papyrus has gaps, so the translation should follow CPF readings and note where they differ from Diels.
item_159.research_yield: Articles on: the anti-Stoic critique of oikeiosis; Plato read as a dogmatist against sceptical Academics; how the lemmatic commentary genre took shape, including the commentator's lost commentaries on the Timaeus, Phaedo and Symposium; the reception of Protagoras' homo-mensura; Theodorus' irrationals; and the dating debate (Tarrant vs Sedley).
item_159.recommendation: Keep, at top priority for Russian. The only Russian is one sentence (col. 2.3–8, Afonasin 2020). English exists only as excerpts and an unpublished draft. First unit: cols. I–XI (prologue plus the oikeiosis digression, about 1.5k words), translated from CPF readings checked against Diels–Schubart 1905.

item_160.ru_found: No Russian translation found, but the check was limited. The WebSearch budget for this run was already used up on the first call, so the required 4 Russian and 4 English searches were not run. I checked these pages directly instead. item_160.en_found: A complete English translation exists: Dirk Baltzly and Michael Share, Hermias: On Plato Phaedrus, 3 vols, Bloomsbury Academic, Ancient Commentators on Aristotle series. Vol. 1 (227A–245E) is dated 2018 on Open Library; German Wikipedia gives 2020–2025 for the set. Vol. 2 covers 245E–257C. The proposed pilot unit (palinode, Phdr. 246a–249d) falls in vol. 2, so it is already in English. Related: Finamore, Manolea and Wear (eds.), Studies in Hermias' Commentary on Plato's Phaedrus (Brill 2019).
item_160.other_found: German: Hildegund Bernard, Hermeias von Alexandrien, Kommentar zu Platons 'Phaidros', Mohr Siebeck, Tübingen 1997, ISBN 3-16-146803-1. This is a complete translation, confirmed on German Wikipedia (the sweep had not verified it), so the pilot unit is also in German. Latin: Marsilio Ficino translated and used the commentary in the 15th century. Italian and French: not found, but I could not search, so both remain unknown. A 'Moreschini Italian translation' or a Budé volume may exist but is unverified.
item_160.source_text: Public domain: P. Couvreur (ed., published after his death by L. Bodin), Hermiae Alexandrini in Platonis Phaedrum scholia ad fidem codicis Parisini 1810 denuo collati, Paris: Bouillon 1901. Full scan and OCR on archive.org, marked NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT: https://archive.org/details/hermiaealexandr00couvgoog. It was reprinted at Hildesheim (Olms) in 1971 with an index by C. Zintzen, and its page.line numbers are the standard reference system. Standard modern edition: C. M. Lucarini and C. Moreschini, Hermias Alexandrinus, In Platonis Phaedrum scholia, Bibliotheca Teubneriana, De Gruyter 2012, ISBN 978-3-11-020115-4. It is in copyright. Translate from Couvreur and check Teubner readings without reproducing its text or apparatus.
item_160.research_yield: Russian studies of Syrianus' school: the four manias and inspiration, the soul-vehicle (ochema) in the chariot myth, Iamblichean fragments, Neoplatonic rhetoric, and the reception in Ficino. It would also set Russian terms for Neoplatonic exegesis. Newness is limited because full English and German versions exist.
item_160.recommendation: Keep it as a Russian-only gap candidate, lowered to priority 3, because complete English (Baltzly–Share) and German (Bernard 1997) translations already cover the whole work, including the pilot unit. The best first unit is the palinode commentary on Phdr. 244a–249d (the manias and the chariot), Couvreur pp. ~86–170, translated from Couvreur and checked against Teubner 2012 and Baltzly–Share vol. 2.

item_161.title_short: Hellenistic Jewish historians and Aristobulus, fragments (pilot: Artapanus frs. 1–3 and Demetrius)
item_161.ru_found: Correction to the sweep: Russian is not "none". (1) Clement, Stromata I, tr. E. V. Afonasin (SPb.: Изд. Олега Абышко, 2003; online at azbyka.ru/otechnik/Kliment_Aleksandrijskij/stromaty/), checked on the page. Strom. I.141.1 has Demetrius fr. 6. I.141.4 and I.153.4 have two Eupolemus fragments. I.150.1 has Aristobulus. I.154.2 has a short version of Artapanus fr. 3 (Moses' escape from prison). The Aristobulus fragments in Strom. V–VI are also translated there. N. Korsunsky's 1892 Stromata translation would also contain these passages, but this pass did not check it. (2) The Cleodemus Malchus fragment (Josephus, AJ I.239–241) is in the Russian Иудейские древности (standard Genkel translation). I confirmed the text on vehi.net. (3) Ezekiel's Exagoge (PE IX.28–29), tr. Z. A. Barzakh, Религия. Церковь. Общество, 2019. That article calls itself "the first Russian verse translation", and Ezekiel is outside this unit. (4) Praeparatio Evangelica in Russian: only Book XI, tr. A. O. Yastrebov (diploma work, 2000, on azbyka). That page says the rest is untranslated. Russian Wikipedia's list of Eusebius translations shows no PE. Its pages on Artapanus, Aristobulus, Alexander Polyhistor and Demetrius list studies only. No Russian translation was found of PE IX.17–39 as a block. That includes Artapanus frs. 1–3, Demetrius frs. 1–5, Eupolemus frs. 1–4 and the letters, Pseudo-Eupolemus, Theodotus, Philo the Epic poet and Aristeas, plus PE VIII.10 and XIII.12 (Aristobulus). Caveat: the 200-search web budget for this turn was already used up, so all 4 searches I ran (Russian) were refused and none returned results. These findings come from direct page fetches. Pravenc.ru and ancientrome.ru refused connections.
item_161.en_found: C. R. Holladay, Fragments from Hellenistic Jewish Authors: I Historians (1983), II Poets (1989), III Aristobulus (1995), IV Orphica (1996), SBL. Volumes and years confirmed on Open Library. Charlesworth (ed.), Old Testament Pseudepigrapha II (1985), includes J. J. Collins on Artapanus and the other fragments (confirmed via Wikipedia citations). E. H. Gifford, Eusebius Praeparatio Evangelica, Book IX, English translation (Oxford 1903), free at tertullian.org/fathers/eusebius_pe_09_book9.htm. It covers chs. 17–39: Eupolemus, Artapanus, Molon, Philo, Demetrius, Theodotus, Aristeas, Ezekiel, the Solomon–Vaphres–Souron letters. The Clement passages are also in the ANF translation.
item_161.other_found: German: P. Riessler, Altjüdisches Schrifttum außerhalb der Bibel (Augsburg 1928). Checked on de.wikisource: it covers Aristobulus, Artapanus, Demetrius, Eupolemus, Kleodemus, Philo the Elder and Theodotus, and the text is online there. Not verified here (search budget exhausted), from memory only: N. Walter, JSHRZ I/2 (1976), III/2 (1975), IV/3 (1983); French: Sources Chrétiennes 369 (PE VIII–X, Schroeder and des Places, 1991); Spanish: Díez Macho (ed.), Apócrifos del AT, vol. II. No Italian edition was identified.
item_161.source_text: Best public-domain text: Gifford, Evangelicae praeparationis libri XV (Oxford 1903). Book IX Greek is in Tomus I (archive.org/details/evangelicaepraep01euse), not in the 02euse item the sweep cited. Tomus II (evangelicaepraep02euse) starts at Book X and holds XIII.12 (Aristobulus). Book VIII.10 is in Tomus I. J. Freudenthal, Hellenistische Studien (1875), is PD. For the Clement passages, Stählin's GCS edition (1906) is PD. Copyrighted: Mras, GCS 43 (1954–56; 2nd ed. des Places 1982–83), the standard modern text; Jacoby FGrHist 722–737; Denis 1970; Holladay's text.
item_161.research_yield: Artapanus' Moses compared with the Alexander Romance (Nectanebo, Sesonchosis) and Josephus' Ethiopian campaign. Eupolemus' Solomon–Vaphres–Souron letters as Hellenistic royal epistolography. Demetrius' biblical chronography as early exegesis. Polyhistor's Peri Ioudaiōn and how Jewish history was received in Rome.
item_161.recommendation: Keep, but correct Russian to excerpts only (via Clement and Josephus); the core PE IX corpus is still untranslated into Russian. Best first unit: Artapanus frs. 1–3 (PE IX.18, 23, 27; about 2.5k words). Note Clement Strom. I.154 (in Afonasin's Russian) as a parallel. Demetrius frs. 1–5 come next.

item_162.title_short: Simplicius, Commentary on Epictetus' Enchiridion (prologue + ch. 1 / ch. 35)
item_162.ru_found: The claim that there is no Russian translation is REFUTED. Russian Wikipedia's article «Эпиктет» (ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/Эпиктет, section «Литература») lists this edition: «Эпиктет. Энхиридион (Краткое руководство к нравственной жизни); Симпликий. Комментарий на „Энхиридион“ Эпиктета / Перевод, статья, комментарий А. Я. Тыжова. СПб.: Владимир Даль, 2012. 399 с. ISBN 978-5-93615-287-0». The same article cites it again in note 7. The title gives the commentary with no limiting qualifier. At 399 pages, including the Enchiridion, an introductory article and notes, the book is consistent with a complete translation. However, I could not inspect the book or its annotation: vdal.ru, ancientrome.ru, simposium.ru and ozon.ru all returned connection resets, and Google Books and Open Library had no record for the ISBN. Completeness is therefore likely but not physically confirmed. The ru.wikipedia article «Симпликий» lists only the In Phys. I.1 (1998) and In De caelo II (2005) extracts, which is why the sweep missed Tyzhov. The ΣΧΟΛΗ front page has no relevant item. Search limitation: the WebSearch budget for this run was exhausted (200-call cap), so the required 4 Russian and 4 English keyword searches could NOT be run. Findings come only from direct fetches of known pages. No pre-1917 Russian translation of Simplicius was found; Poletika's 1759 translation covers the Enchiridion only.
item_162.en_found: Confirmed as complete. Charles Brittain and Tad Brennan, Simplicius: On Epictetus Handbook 1–26 and 27–53, 2 vols, Ancient Commentators on Aristotle (Duckworth, London 2002; ISBN 0-7156-3068-7 and 0-7156-3069-5; later Bloomsbury reissue). Both de.wikipedia and en.wikipedia list them. There is also an old complete English translation by George Stanhope (1694; four editions in the early 18th century, e.g. 1722), which is public domain.
item_162.other_found: French: Ilsetraut Hadot, Simplicius, Commentaire sur le Manuel d'Épictète, Les Belles Lettres (CUF), tome I, 2001 (ISBN 2-251-00493-9), Greek text with French translation of chapters I–XXIX. Per fr.wikipedia, tome II has not appeared. Latin: complete translation by Angelus Caninius (Venice 1546) and by Hieronymus Wolf (Basel 1563); Perotti translated the prologue in 1451. German: no translation found; Christian Vogel, Stoische Ethik und platonische Bildung (Heidelberg: Winter 2013), is a study, not a translation. Italian and Spanish: not verified, because search was unavailable.
item_162.source_text: The standard critical edition is I. Hadot, Simplicius: Commentaire sur le Manuel d'Épictète (Brill, Philosophia Antiqua 66, Leiden 1996; ISBN 90-04-09772-4), with a CUF tome I (2001); both are in copyright. Public-domain Greek: J. Schweighäuser, Epicteteae philosophiae monumenta vol. IV (Leipzig 1800), and F. Dübner's Didot edition (Paris 1840); I did not verify archive.org identifiers for either. Correction: the archive.org link in the candidate file (bub_gb_72SHc8S-I5sC) is NOT Schweighäuser or Dübner. It is the Leiden 1640 edition (Heinsius/Salmasius, with Wolf's Latin; 774 pp.), marked Public Domain Mark 1.0.
item_162.research_yield: Low for Neoscholia, because complete Russian (Tyzhov 2012) and English (Brennan–Brittain 2002) translations exist. The only remaining angles are a critical review of Tyzhov's translation against Hadot's 1996 text, or a study of the ch. 35 anti-Manichaean theodicy. A new translation is not needed for either.
item_162.recommendation: DROP. A Russian translation of the whole commentary exists (A. Ya. Tyzhov, SPb.: Vladimir Dal', 2012), and a complete modern English one exists too. Before closing the item, have someone open the Tyzhov volume to confirm it is complete; even if it is partial, the item stays dropped.

item_163.title_short: Hierocles the Stoic, Elements of Ethics + Stobaean excerpts (whole corpus; pilot Stob. 4.27.23 'circles')
item_163.ru_found: I found no Russian translation. Limitation: the shared WebSearch budget was already used up, so I could not run the required RU and EN keyword searches. I relied on direct page fetches instead. (1) ruwiki «Гиерокл (стоик)» lists no translation; its only sources are Gellius, Long's Stoic Studies and Stobaeus. (2) ΣΧΟΛΗ: I downloaded every issue page 2007–2026 (vols I.1–XX.2) from classics.nsu.ru/schole and grepped for Hierocl/Гиерокл/Иерокл/oikei/ойкей. The only hits were for Hierocles of Alexandria (the Neoplatonist): Afonasin 15.2 (2021) on Damascius, and a note in IX.2 (2015) on the Commentary on the Golden Verses. One issue page, VI.1 (2012), would not download. (3) The project's own crosscheck (raw/ru_series_crosscheck.json) found no Hierocles translation in ΣΧΟΛΗ, Платоновские исследования 1–24, Историко-философский ежегодник or Вестник РХГА. (4) The earlier sweep also found nothing in CyberLeninka. Not checked: Russian popular-Stoicism books translated from English, which may quote the 'circles' passage second-hand, and the ВДИ, Philologia Classica and Hyperboreus archives. Do not confuse this author with the Neoplatonist Hierocles of Alexandria, who has Russian material. Treat RU 'none' as likely but not exhaustively proven.
item_163.en_found: Full: I. Ramelli, Hierocles the Stoic: Elements of Ethics, Fragments, and Excerpts, trans. D. Konstan (SBL, Writings from the Greco-Roman World, 2009). It has Greek text with a facing translation and covers both the papyrus and the Stobaean fragments (cited on en/es/fr Wikipedia). Excerpts (the Stobaean fragments only): T. Taylor, 'Ethical fragments of Hierocles, preserved by Stobaeus', in Political Fragments of Archytas... (Chiswick 1822), pp. 75–115; K. S. Guthrie, 'Hierocles, the Ethical Fragments', Pythagoras Source Book and Library (1919/20), pp. 157–175. Both are on en.wikisource, Author:Hierocles (fl. 2nd century). Sourcebook selections: B. Inwood, Later Stoicism 155 BC to AD 200 (CUP 2022), pp. 480–504 (cited on frwiki). Key passages are also in Long & Sedley, The Hellenistic Philosophers (1987), from memory and not re-checked here. The English side offers nothing new.
item_163.other_found: Italian, full papyrus: G. Bastianini and A. A. Long, 'Hierocles', Corpus dei Papiri Filosofici Greci e Latini I.1** (Olschki 1992), pp. 268–451, a critical edition with Italian translation and commentary (confirmed on dewiki). Italian, the Stobaean excerpts: probably also in I. Ramelli's Italian volume (Stoici romani minori, Bompiani 2008), from memory, not verified. von Arnim's BKT IV (1906) is a Greek edition with German introduction, not a translation. I could not check French, German (e.g. a Tusculum Stoa anthology) or Spanish versions, because the search budget was exhausted. None of the dewiki, eswiki or frwiki articles lists one.
item_163.source_text: Public domain: H. von Arnim, Hierokles, Ethische Elementarlehre (Papyrus 9780) nebst den bei Stobäus erhaltenen ethischen Exzerpten aus Hierokles, BKT IV (Berlin 1906). It is on archive.org at https://archive.org/details/coo.31924022696045 under a Public Domain Mark 1.0, which I confirmed, and it contains both the papyrus and the Stobaean excerpts. For the excerpts there is also Wachsmuth–Hense, Ioannis Stobaei Anthologium (1884–1912, public domain). The 'circles' passage is Stob. 4.27.23, Hense IV p. 671ff. The standard modern editions are Bastianini–Long, CPF I.1** (1992), and Ramelli 2009; both are in copyright. Use von Arnim as the base text and check the papyrus supplements against Bastianini–Long (cited, not reproduced).
item_163.research_yield: Articles: the first Russian annotated Hierocles; oikeiosis and self-perception (synaisthesis) compared with Chrysippus and Seneca's Ep. 121; the 'circles' and Stoic cosmopolitanism; household and marriage ethics alongside Musonius and the Stobaean marriage dossier; supplementing papyrus lacunae with LLMs.
item_163.recommendation: Keep, as a first Russian translation only. The English version brings nothing new (Ramelli–Konstan 2009, plus Taylor, Guthrie and Inwood). Start with the Stobaean 'circles' excerpt (Stob. 4.27.23, under 1k words) from von Arnim's public-domain text, then the papyrus columns 1–11.

item_164.ru_found:
No continuous Russian translation of the Placita, or of any whole book, was found. Russian has only scattered lemmata, so "excerpts_only" is a better label than the sweep's "partial".

Limits of this check:
- None of the required searches ran. The shared WebSearch budget was already used up, and my first two Russian queries were refused: «Псевдо-Плутарх "О мнениях философов" перевод» and «Аэций "Мнения философов" перевод».
- These sites were unreachable (connection reset or 403): ancientrome.ru, simposium.ru, the CyberLeninka API, search.rsl.ru, nlr.ru and nsu.ru.

What I did check, by direct fetch:
- ru.wikipedia «Аэтий (доксограф)»: names only Diels and Mansfeld–Runia, with no Russian translation. The article on the Placita is a red link.
- ru.wikipedia «Псевдо-Плутарх»: lists «Мнения философов» (De placitis) with no translation.
- ru.wikipedia «Плутарх», section on Russian translations: no Placita.
- ru.wikipedia «Доксография», «Лебедев, Андрей Валентинович» and «Маковельский»: no hits.
- ru.wikisource «Автор:Плутарх»: no hits.
- Cached ΣΧΟΛΗ tables of contents, vols 1.1–20.2 (2007–2026), scanned for Aëtius, Placita and Ps.-Plutarch: no translation of the work. Afonasin's fragment collections do quote Ps.-Plutarch and Stobaeus variants: Diogenes of Apollonia (3.2, 2009, quoted "in full"), Heraclides of Pontus (13.1–13.2, 2019), Protagoras and Gorgias (14.1–14.2, 2020), Antiphon (15.1, 2021).

Other excerpts, from standard collections that I did not re-check this session: Маковельский «Досократики» (1914–19); Лебедев ФРГФ ч. 1 (1989); Лурье «Демокрит» (1970); Столяров «Фрагменты ранних стоиков» (1998–2010).

Open lead: «Нравственные и философические сочинения Плутарха» (trans. И. Алексеев, СПб., 1789, listed on ru.wikipedia). Its contents are unknown. If it followed Amyot's collection, it could include the Placita, so check it before claiming a first Russian translation.
item_164.en_found:
There are two full English versions:

1. A 17th-century "several hands" version as revised by W. W. Goodwin, "Sentiments Concerning Nature with which Philosophers were Delighted" (Plutarch's Morals, 1870s). It is public domain and online as Project Gutenberg #3052, "Complete Works of Plutarch, Vol. 3: Essays and Miscellanies". I confirmed it in the e-text: Books I–V are complete, about 24.5k English words, and Book II has all 32 chapters in about 4.3k words. The e-text names no translator; the Goodwin attribution is the standard one. It is old and loose, and Greek words are omitted.
2. Mansfeld & Runia (eds.), Aëtiana V (4 vols), "An Edition of the Reconstructed Text of the Placita with a Commentary and a Collection of Related Texts" (Brill, 2 July 2020, DOI 10.1163/9789004428409, checked via Crossref). It is the scholarly English translation of the reconstructed Aëtius. I did not open the Brill page to confirm the translation is included (the page returned 403/405).

There is no Loeb volume.
item_164.other_found:
French, full:
- J. Amyot (1572). Confirmed: the full text is on ABU, abu.cnam.fr/cgi-bin/donner_html?opinions3, with Amyot's marginal notes.
- An older French version on remacle.org ("Œuvres morales, Tome IV", translator not named on the page).
- Lachenaud, CUF (Budé) 1993, Œuvres morales XII.2. I believe this exists but did not open it.

Italian, full (both listed in it.wikipedia «Aezio (filosofo)»):
- L. Torraca, "I Dossografi greci", the Italian version of Diels' Doxographi Graeci (Padova: CEDAM, 1961).
- "Opinioni dei filosofi sulla natura", in Plutarco, Tutti i Moralia, ed. E. Lelli & G. Pisani (Bompiani, 2017), pp. 1675–1760.

German: Daiber, Aetius Arabus (1980), a German translation of Qusta ibn Luqa's Arabic version. I know it from memory and did not re-check it. An older German Moralia translation may include the Placita; also unverified.

Spanish: unknown.
item_164.source_text:
Best public-domain text: H. Diels, Doxographi Graeci (Berlin: Reimer, 1879), with Ps.-Plutarch printed next to Stobaeus. archive.org/details/doxographigraec00dielgoog has PDF and OCR text and is flagged NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT; I checked this via the archive.org metadata API. Bernardakis' Teubner Moralia V (1893) is another public-domain option, but I did not verify it.

Modern editions, all in copyright:
- Mau, Teubner (1971)
- Lachenaud, CUF (1993)
- Mansfeld–Runia, Aëtiana V (Brill, 2020). This is a reconstructed Aëtius, not the Ps.-Plutarch epitome itself, and it does not appear to be open access.

So translate the Ps.-Plutarch epitome from Diels, and cite Aëtiana V only for checking.
item_164.research_yield: Possible articles: Russian vocabulary for Greek cosmology. Ps.-Plutarch versus Stobaeus in the astronomical chapters of Book II. Presocratic theories of the sun, moon and eclipses as doxographic constructs. Later use of the epitome (Eusebius, Theodoret, Qusta ibn Luqa). A concordance of the existing scattered Russian versions.
item_164.recommendation: Keep it, but only as a first continuous Russian translation, at priority 3. Drop any "untranslated" claim, because full public-domain English plus English, French and Italian versions exist. Best first unit is Book II (32 chapters, about 3k Greek words rather than the sweep's 6k), from Diels' public-domain text, with each lemma linked to its DK, SVF or Usener number and to the existing Russian excerpts. Re-run the Russian searches, including the 1789 Алексеев volume, before announcing it.

item_165.title_short: Pseudo-Pythagorean ethical treatises (Ps.-Archytas, Metopus, Theages, Euryphamus, Hippodamus, Hipparchus; Thesleff/Centrone set)
item_165.ru_found: No Russian translation of the ethical unit found. The wider corpus has only partial Russian coverage, all checked directly: Timaeus Locrus, translated by A. S. Afonasina (ΣΧΟΛΗ 7.1, 2013; cyberleninka); her partial translation of Theano's letter to Eubule (ΣΧΟΛΗ 11.2, 2017, pp. 524–535); and Afonasina's letters of Melissa and Myia (ΣΧΟΛΗ 12.1, 2018, pp. 276–286). ru.wikipedia «Стобей» lists Stobaeus IV.7 «Наставления о царской власти» (Исторический вестник 26 [182], Runivers 2018, pp. 280–306); the article names no translator. IV.7 holds the kingship texts (Diotogenes, Sthenidas, Ecphantus), not the ethical ones. I checked the ΣΧΟΛΗ tables of contents for 2009 (vol. 3.1, the Neopythagoreans issue: Moderatus, Nicomachus, Numenius, Theologoumena only), 2014–2017 and 2018–2026: none contain Ps.-Archytas, Metopus, Theages, Euryphamus, Hippodamus, Hipparchus, Crito, Polus or Callicratidas. ru.wikipedia «Архит Тарентский» lists no Russian translation of the pseudo-Archytan works; Lebedev's ФРГФ (1989) covers only the genuine fragments. The Afonasina 2013 bibliography cites no Russian versions of these treatises. The WebSearch budget for this run was used up, so I fetched known pages directly. I could not search elibrary, the RSL catalogue, the Soviet anthologies (e.g. Антология мировой философии 1969) or a possible recent Afonasin/Afonasina collection, so a small risk of a missed Russian version remains.
item_165.en_found: REFUTES the sweep's 'EN partial / no complete English'. Thomas Taylor, 'Iamblichus' Life of Pythagoras... Accompanied by Fragments of the Ethical Writings of Certain Pythagoreans in the Doric Dialect' (London: Valpy, 1818; archive.org/details/b29318610; also on en.wikisource) translates exactly the pilot set. It contains Hippodamus On Felicity, Euryphamus On Human Life, Hipparchus On Tranquillity, Archytas On the Good and Happy Man, Theages On the Virtues, Metopus On Virtue, and Clinias. It also has Crito On Prudence and Prosperity, Polus On Justice, and Archytas On Ethical Erudition, On Disciplines and On Wisdom (I checked the full-text OCR, about pp. 193–256). Taylor's 'Political Fragments of Archytas, Charondas, Zaleucus and other ancient Pythagoreans' (Chiswick 1822; archive.org/details/b29349187; Wikisource index) covers Hippodamus On a Republic, Archytas On Law and Justice, Diotogenes, Sthenidas, Ecphantus, Charondas, Zaleucus, Callicratidas On the Felicity of Families and Perictione. These are reportedly reprinted in Guthrie's Pythagorean Sourcebook (1920; Phanes 1987); I did not verify that. The Taylor versions are public domain but archaic and pre-critical. I found no modern annotated English version of the ethical treatises.
item_165.other_found: Italian: Bruno Centrone, 'Pseudopythagorica ethica: i trattati morali di Archita, Metopo, Teage, Eurifamo' (1990). Open Library confirms the title and the year; I recall it as Bibliopolis, series Elenchos, but did not verify that. It is a full scholarly text, translation and commentary of the core of the pilot unit. Hippodamus On Felicity and Hipparchus are not in it. French: Delatte (1942) covers the kingship treatises; I recall this and did not re-verify it. Pythagorean women's texts have English versions (Pomeroy 2013, Plant 2004); I did not re-verify these either. I found no German or Spanish translation of the ethical set; that was not exhaustively searched.
item_165.source_text: Public domain: Stobaeus, Anthologium, ed. Wachsmuth–Hense (Berlin 1884–1912; archive.org), where the treatises sit in Stob. II–IV (e.g. Theages and Metopus in III.1; Hippodamus and Euryphamus in IV.39; Hipparchus in IV.44). Also Mullach, Fragmenta Philosophorum Graecorum II (1867); Orelli, Opuscula Graecorum veterum sententiosa (1819–21); Gale, Opuscula mythologica (1688). Taylor 1818 is listed as English and Greek, which may mean a facing Greek text. The standard modern editions are in copyright: Thesleff, The Pythagorean Texts of the Hellenistic Period (Åbo 1965), and Centrone 1990.
item_165.research_yield: First Russian corpus of Hellenistic Pythagorean ethics. It would support studies of Peripatetic and Platonic mesotes and eudaimonia (virtue plus external goods) in Doric dress, dating and authenticity (Thesleff vs Centrone), reception in Philo and Iamblichus, and the link to the kingship treatises.
item_165.recommendation: Keep as a Russian-only, first-ever candidate at priority 3, and drop any 'no English' claim: Taylor 1818 already translated the whole pilot set. Best first unit: Ps.-Archytas On the Good and Happy Man plus Metopus and Theages On Virtue (Stob. III.1), using Wachsmuth–Hense and checking against Centrone.

item_166.title_short: Proclus, In Rem publicam (Essay 16, Myth of Er)
item_166.ru_found: No Russian translation of Essay 16 found. For the work as a whole, Russian coverage is partial. Checks were limited: the session's web-search budget (200 calls) was already used up, so the first Russian WebSearch returned nothing and the required 4+4 searches could not be run. I fell back to fetching known pages directly. ru.wikipedia «Прокл Диадох» lists only two items, both by А. В. Петров: (1) «О способе создания божественных мифов» (part of Essay 6) in «Академия», вып. 1, СПб. 1997, pp. 252–278; (2) «Из комментариев Прокла к „Государству“ Платона» in «Феномен теургии», СПб.: РХГИ/СПбГУ 2003, pp. 292–314. The 2003 excerpts are unverified and could touch Essay 16, for example its daemonological or theurgic passages. ru.wikipedia «Государство (Платон)» does not mention Proclus. ancientrome.ru gave a connection error and platonic-studies.ru did not resolve. Possible unverified excerpts: paraphrases in Losev, ИАЭ т. VII. Still unchecked: elibrary/cyberleninka, Платоновские исследования, ΣΧΟΛΗ.
item_166.en_found: Baltzly, Finamore and Miles, 'Proclus: Commentary on Plato's Republic' (CUP). item_166.source_text: W. Kroll, Procli Diadochi In Platonis Rem publicam commentarii, vol. II (Teubner 1901), public domain. The archive.org item https://archive.org/details/inplatonisrempu00krolgoog is Vol. II: its title page reads VOL. II and it opens with Essay 13, the Muses' speech. Essay 16 starts in the same scan (εἰς τὸν ἐν Πολιτείᾳ μῦθον, addressed to Marinus) around Kroll II p. 96. The OCR is poor, so work from the page images or another clean source. Kroll remains the standard edition with no later critical edition; Abbate reprints Kroll's Greek. The Greek text has no copyright problem.
item_166.research_yield: Proclus' defence of Er's twelve-day 'death' against Colotes' Epicurean critique, and his dossier of revival and apparent-death stories (Clearchus, Naumachius, Philinnion/Phlegon, Polykritos). Also Numenius and Porphyry on the myth, the cosmology of the spindle and Necessity, the choice of lives, and Neoplatonic theory of myth.
item_166.recommendation: Keep as a Russian-first candidate. Essay 16 has no known Russian version, but it already exists in French (1970) and Italian (2004), and possibly in English, so its novelty is mainly for Russian readers. Best first unit: the opening section on Colotes' objections and the apparent-death stories (roughly Kroll II 96–125, about 8–10k words), which stands on its own and is rich for articles. Before committing, run the Russian searches again with a fresh search budget.

item_167.title_short: Alexander of Aphrodisias, De fato (whole treatise)
item_167.ru_found: I found no complete or partial Russian translation of the treatise. Russian Wikipedia's article on Alexander lists only Solopova's "О смешении и росте" (Наука, 2002) and an online fragment, «Ответы на возражения Ксенарха» (annales.info; the site refused connections). I checked the available contents pages of ΣΧΟΛΗ (22 of 40 issue pages, the rest returned 404) and found nothing on De fato. ancientrome.ru also refused connections. Likely excerpts: the Chrysippean passages from Alexander's De fato that are in SVF II (fate fragments, SVF II 912–1007) should be translated in А. А. Столяров, «Фрагменты ранних стоиков» т. II ч. 2 (Хрисипп, физические фрагменты, Греко-латинский кабинет, 2002). The volume itself is confirmed via ru.wikipedia (Хрисипп); that it contains the Alexander passages is my inference from the SVF numbering, not checked against the book. The WebSearch budget ran out before my first query (limit shared across agents), so I ran 0 of the required Russian searches. elibrary.ru, cyberleninka.ru, RSL/NLR catalogues and Russian dissertations were not searched.
item_167.en_found: Confirmed: R. W. Sharples, Alexander of Aphrodisias On Fate: text, translation and commentary (London: Duckworth, 1983), cited by SEP (Dorothea Frede, "Alexander of Aphrodisias") and by en/ru Wikipedia. Earlier but unverified this session: A. FitzGerald, The Essay on Fate of Alexander of Aphrodisias (London: Scholartis Press, 1931), from memory only. Passages also appear in Long and Sedley, The Hellenistic Philosophers (1987), from memory.
item_167.other_found: French: P. Thillet, Alexandre d'Aphrodise, Traité du destin, Budé/CUF (Les Belles Lettres, 1984; reprinted 2002), per SEP and ru.wiki. German: A. Zierl, Alexander von Aphrodisias, Über das Schicksal (Berlin: Akademie Verlag, 1995), Greek text with translation and commentary, per de.wiki. Italian: C. Natali (with E. Tetamo), Alessandro di Afrodisia, Il destino (Milano: Rusconi, 1996; 2nd ed. Academia Verlag, Sankt Augustin, 2009), per de.wiki and it.wiki. Also A. Magris (ed.), Trattati antichi sul destino (Brescia: Morcelliana, 2009), with Cicero and Ps.-Plutarch; it.wiki lists it, presumably including De fato. Latin: Moerbeke's medieval version (ed. Thillet, Vrin 1963), plus early modern versions by Grotius (1648) and Schulthess. Spanish: unknown.
item_167.source_text: Public domain: I. Bruns (ed.), Alexandri Aphrodisiensis praeter commentaria scripta minora, Supplementum Aristotelicum II.2 (Berlin: Reimer, 1892), De fato pp. 164–212, https://archive.org/details/alexandriaphrodi00alex. The archive.org page has no rights statement, but an 1892 Berlin edition is public domain. Orelli's edition (Zürich, 1824) is also public domain. The standard modern editions are in copyright: Thillet's Budé text (1984), Sharples' text (1983), and the Greek texts in Zierl (1995) and Natali (1996/2009). Use Bruns as the base text and note Thillet's departures in the apparatus.
item_167.research_yield: A first full Russian De fato with commentary would support articles on Russian terminology for τὸ ἐφ' ἡμῖν and ἐνδεχόμενον, on Alexander against Chrysippus compared with Cicero's De fato and Plotinus Enn. III.1, and on its reception (Nemesius, Arabic versions, Grotius). Its novelty for article-writing is modest because the text is heavily studied in the West.
item_167.recommendation: Keep at reduced priority: it is the first Russian translation of a key text (only SVF excerpts likely exist), but it is fully translated into English, French, German and Italian. Best first unit is the whole treatise (about 14k words), or chapters 1–6 plus 22 as a pilot. Before committing, run the Russian checks (elibrary, cyberleninka, RSL) that this session could not do.

item_168.ru_found: I could not refute the claim, but I also could not test it properly. The shared web-search budget (200 per turn) ran out before my first query, so none of the 4 Russian and 4 English searches the task requires actually ran. The only direct fetch that worked was Russian Wikipedia ("Олимпиодор Младший", wikitext checked). Its Russian-translations list names only Gasparov's Life of Plato (in the Diogenes Laertius volume, Mysl 1979, pp. 445–448). It also cites "Памятники византийской литературы IV–IX веков" (ed. L. A. Freiberg, Nauka 1968, p. 147), but without saying which Olympiodorus text is printed there. This is one page, so it is an excerpt at most, and it must be checked to see whether it comes from the Gorgias commentary. The Russian Wikipedia articles on the Gorgias do not mention Olympiodorus. ancientrome.ru, simposium.ru and the ΣΧΟΛΗ site (nsu.ru) refused the connection (ECONNRESET). The platonic-studies.ru domain did not resolve. Not checked: CyberLeninka, elibrary.ru, the ВДИ and ΣΧΟΛΗ contents lists, Платоновские исследования, the RSL catalogue, and dissertations.
item_168.en_found: Full English translation: R. Jackson, K. Lycos, H. Tarrant, Olympiodorus: Commentary on Plato's Gorgias, Leiden: Brill 1998, ISBN 90-04-10972-2. Confirmed by English Wikipedia (footnote) and two Open Library records (1998, English). From memory, not re-checked: it is in the Philosophia Antiqua series, has full notes and an introduction by Tarrant, and is based on Westerink's text.
item_168.other_found: Italian: Elena Gritti, Il vero nel mito: teoria esegetica nel commento di Olimpiodoro Alessandrino al "Gorgia" (Rome: Aracne 2012, series Atene e Gerusalemme 4, ISBN 9788854854758, 315 pp.; Open Library edition record OL23453118W). It is a study of how Olympiodorus reads the myth, which is the proposed pilot unit. The catalogue subject "Early works to 1800" suggests it may include Greek text or an Italian translation of passages, but I could not confirm this because the publisher page returned "page does not exist". I found no French, German or Spanish translation, though I could not search for one properly.
item_168.source_text: Two Teubner editions: W. Norvin, Olympiodori philosophi in Platonis Gorgiam commentaria (Leipzig: Teubner 1936), and the standard edition by L. G. Westerink, Olympiodori in Platonis Gorgiam commentaria (Leipzig: Teubner 1970). The bibliographic details are from memory and the item file, not re-checked. Norvin died in 1940 (from memory), so his edition has probably been public domain in the EU since 2011. In the US it is probably still protected until about 2031 (an estimate, assuming 1990s copyright restoration applies). I could not confirm that any scan of Norvin is openly available. Westerink 1970 is in copyright and is the text the TLG and the 1998 English translation use. Practical approach: translate from Westerink, cite by Westerink's lecture and section numbers, and compare against Norvin.
item_168.research_yield: First Russian version of the only surviving ancient Gorgias commentary. Possible articles: Alexandrian Neoplatonist exegesis of the eschatological myth; the grades of virtue and political philosophy; how Socrates is portrayed to pupils in Christian Alexandria; comparison with Proclus; how rhetoric was taught in the 6th-century curriculum.
item_168.recommendation: Keep as a priority-3 candidate that fills a Russian-only gap, since the full English translation (Brill 1998) rules out an EN first. Pilot on Lectures 46–50 (the final myth), but first find out what p. 147 of the 1968 Nauka anthology contains and whether Gritti 2012 translates those lectures.

item_169.title_short: Philodemus, On Frank Criticism (PHerc. 1471; final columns Ia–XXIVb)
item_169.ru_found: No Russian translation found, but the check was incomplete. The WebSearch budget for this turn (200 calls, shared across agents) was already used up, so none of the required RU/EN keyword searches ran. I only fetched pages directly. (1) ru.wikipedia "Филодем из Гадары": the work is listed as «О прямодушии (Об откровенной критике)», PHerc. 1471, and the 1914 Olivieri edition is noted.
