(2) Afonasin's Index Academicorum translation (Respublica Literaria 2021, cyberleninka) mentions no Russian version of Peri parrhesias. (3) ru.wikipedia "Парресия" does not mention Philodemus. It cites the Russian translation of Foucault's Berkeley lectures, «Дискурс и истина» (Логос 2008 №2(65); PDF at intelros.ru, which did not load). Foucault discusses Philodemus there and in «Герменевтика субъекта» (RU 2007), but only as paraphrase, not a translation. ancientrome.ru and intelros.ru did not respond (ECONNRESET). Still unchecked: elibrary, ΣΧΟΛΗ, Аристей, РГБ, and the works of Шахнович and Афонасин on Epicureanism.
item_169.en_found: Full translation: D. Konstan, D. Clay, C. E. Glad, J. C. Thom, J. Ware, Philodemus: On Frank Criticism. Introduction, Translation and Notes (SBL Texts and Translations 43, Graeco-Roman 13; Atlanta: Scholars Press/SBL, 1998; SBL reprint ISBN 1-58983-292-2). It has Greek text and English translation of all fragments and columns, including the final columns. Confirmed by en.wikipedia and de.wikipedia "Philodemos von Gadara".
item_169.other_found: ITALIAN, full: Filodemo di Gadara, Sulla franchezza, ed. S. Ghisu (Saonara/Roma: Il Prato, 2015), 127 pp., ISBN 9788863362954. Open Library: "Greek text with parallel Italian translation; critical matter in Italian" (it.wikipedia, "Sulla libertà di parola"). Also M. Gigante, «Filodemo sulla libertà di parola», in Ricerche filodemee (Napoli: Bibliopolis, 1983), pp. 55–113. This is a study, and whether it translates passages was not verified. FRENCH: fr.wikipedia's list of Philodemus works in the Pléiade «Les Épicuriens» (Delattre & Pigeaud, 2010) does not include this treatise. I found no other French translation, but did not search. GERMAN, SPANISH: unknown, not searched.
item_169.source_text: Public domain: A. Olivieri, Philodemi Περὶ παρρησίας libellus (Leipzig: Teubner, 1914), full scan and text at https://archive.org/details/philodemiperipar00philuoft. The usable modern text is the Konstan et al. 1998 edition (SBL), which revises Olivieri and is in copyright. Ghisu 2015 is also in copyright. As far as I could tell there is no newer critical edition, but I did not verify this. For difficult readings, check the papyrus images (PHerc. 1471, Biblioteca Nazionale di Napoli / Chartes) against Olivieri and Konstan.
item_169.research_yield: Russian articles: Epicurean psychagogy and correction; parrhesia from Philodemus to Foucault (with a Russian corrective to Foucault's reading); Philodemus and Pauline community discipline; the vocabulary of friendship and confession; fragmentary-papyrus translation method with AI.
item_169.recommendation: Keep, at moderate priority, as a first Russian translation only. It is translated in full into English (Konstan et al. 1998) and Italian (Ghisu 2015), and the text is fragmentary. Best first unit: the continuous final columns Ia–XXIVb, translated from Olivieri and checked against Konstan's revised readings.

item_170.title_short: Stobaeus, Anthology IV.22–24 (marriage, marital precepts, children)
item_170.ru_found: CAVEAT: the shared WebSearch budget ran out before my first query, so I did NO Russian keyword searches. I checked only by fetching pages directly. ru.wikipedia «Стобей» (fetched): the only Russian chapter it lists is Anth. IV.7 («Наставления о царской власти», Исторический вестник 26 [182], 2018, pp. 280–306), and it says the whole work is untranslated. I found no Russian translation of IV.22–24 as a compilation. Individual excerpts do exist in Russian under their authors' names. Semonides fr. 7 (the women iambus, which comes down to us through Stob. IV.22): the ru.wikipedia article links a Russian version, «Различно женщин нрав…», and I believe from memory it is Veresaev's. From memory, not checked here: Hesiod and Homer; Democritus' ethical fragments (Лурье 1970); Menander and Euripides fragments; Plutarch's «Наставления супругам». Not settled: Stolyarov, «Фрагменты ранних стоиков» т. III (2010?, ГЛК), which probably includes Antipater's Περὶ γάμου (SVF III Ant. 62–63). ru.wikipedia «Стоицизм» lists only тт. I–II. A Russian Musonius XIII–XV is unknown: ru.wikipedia «Музоний Руф» lists only Lutz. I found no Russian Hierocles (ru.wikipedia «Гиерокл (стоик)»). ancientrome.ru refused the connection.
item_170.en_found: There is no English translation of IV.22–24 as an ordered compilation (en.wikipedia Stobaeus, fetched; its "never translated" claim is tagged citation needed). Many excerpts are translated in separate author editions. I checked these online: Hierocles "On wedlock" (Stob. IV.22a.21–24), translated by T. Taylor, Political Fragments of Archytas… and Ethical Fragments of Hierocles (1822, public domain, Wikisource), and by K. S. Guthrie, Pythagoras Source Book (1919, Wikisource ch. 26). Taylor 1822 also gives Phintys "On the temperance of a woman" (Stob. IV.23). Musonius XIII–XV (marriage; raising every child): Lutz 1947/2020 (Yale) and C. King 2011. Antipater "On Marriage": W. Deming, Paul on Marriage and Celibacy, Appendix A, pp. 221–226 (text and translation). From memory, not checked: Ramelli and Konstan, Hierocles (SBL 2009); Gerber, Loeb Greek Iambic (1999) and Lloyd-Jones 1975 for Semonides 7; Pomeroy, Pythagorean Women (2013); Loeb Plutarch Coniugalia praecepta; Loeb comic and tragic fragments. The proposed pilot IV.22a (philosophical prose) is the most translated part in English.
item_170.other_found: There is no complete translation into any modern language (both Wikipedias). All of the following is from memory and was not checked this session. Latin: Conrad Gesner's 16th-c. version, and Grotius' verse renderings of the poetic excerpts (Dicta poetarum quae apud Stobaeum exstant, 1623). Italian: Ramelli's Musonio (Bompiani 2001) and Ierocle. French: Jagu's Musonius (1979). German: Nickel's Tusculum Stoic and Musonius volumes. I know of no Italian, Spanish, French or German translation of the chapters themselves.
item_170.source_text: Wachsmuth and Hense, Ioannis Stobaei Anthologium, vol. IV, ed. O. Hense (Berlin: Weidmann, 1909). It is still the standard critical edition and is public domain (Hense died 1931). The scan is at https://archive.org/details/adw8682.0004.001.umich.edu (Univ. of Michigan; the metadata gives the 1884 set date, and the identifier marks vol. 4). IV.22 runs from about p. 494; Antipater is at 507–512. Older public-domain editions are Gaisford (1822) and Meineke (Teubner 1855–57), which number these chapters as Florilegium tit. 67–77. The excerpt count is probably above the stated 200: IV.22 alone runs to at least 193 (Semonides is IV.22.193).
item_170.research_yield: Articles could study how Stobaeus arranges the case for and against marriage (IV.22a against 22b–g). They could re-read the Stoic marriage debate (Antipater, Musonius, Hierocles) against 1 Cor 7, or the household ethics of the Pythagorean women. They could also trace misogynist topoi from Semonides to Menander. The Russian value lies in the dossier as a whole.
item_170.recommendation: Keep as a Russian-first project framed as the first translation of the Stobaean marriage dossier as a compilation, not as first translations of its authors; for English the novelty is low. The first unit should be all of IV.22a in Stobaeus' order, verse and prose together. Before claiming any first, check Stolyarov's т. III for Antipater and look for a Russian Musonius.

item_171.title_short: Philo of Alexandria, De vita Mosis I–II (pilot: Book I or Mos. II 1–65)
item_171.ru_found:
I could not refute "none", but the check is incomplete. The shared WebSearch budget was used up before this task started, so all of the required 4 RU and 4 EN searches were blocked. The checks below are direct page fetches plus the project cache.
(1) ru.wikipedia «Филон Александрийский», section «Тексты и переводы». De Vita Mosis appears only in the treatise list, with no Russian translation. The list of Russian translations has: Гедеон 1783 (De spec. leg. II, on feasts); Браш 1907 (De aeternitate); Смирнов 1909 / Елизарова 1971 (De vita contemplativa); Левинская 1994 (Flacc., Legat.); Макаров, ВДИ 1999; «Толкования Ветхого Завета» (Греко-латинский кабинет 2000); Матусова 2003 (Quod Deus); Афиногенов, ВДИ 2003 (De ebrietate).
(2) The project cache (ru_series_crosscheck.json) has systematic sweeps of ВДИ, Историко-философский ежегодник, ΣΧΟΛΗ and Платоновские исследования. Its Philo items are Makarov 1999, Afinogenov 2003, Matusova 2003 (Quod Deus) and 2012 (De gigantibus), and Afonasin 2025–26 (De aeternitate, complete). None is De vita Mosis. This also shows the ruwiki list is incomplete.
(3) The most likely place for an excerpt of the Septuagint legend (Mos. II 25–44) is Афонасин, «Moses Attikidzon», ΣΧΟΛΗ 16.1 (2022) 276–294, https://classics.nsu.ru/schole/16/16-1-afonasin.pdf. It is a dossier of testimonia on the Library and the Septuagint. I decoded its font-garbled PDF. It translates Aristeas, Aristobulus, Clement, Tertullian, Josephus, Syncellus, Tzetzes, P.Oxy. 1241, Seneca/Gellius/Dio/Orosius/Plutarch and Ammianus, but not Philo, Mos. II.
(4) The ruwiki «Литературные памятники» list (to the end of the page) has no Philo volume. The candidate sheet's note «проверить том Ладомира» is therefore unconfirmed: I found no such volume.
(5) The ruwiki «Септуагинта» article paraphrases Philo's legend and cites Вевюрко 2013 (ПСТГУ). Its note 31, «О созерцательной жизни II 7, 37–41», is evidently a mislabel for Mos. II 37–41. That monograph may quote Mos. II in Russian, so excerpts are possible but unverified.
Not checked: RSL/NLR catalogues, eLibrary, Богословские труды, Вестник ПСТГУ, amateur online versions.
Pitfall: Gregory of Nyssa's «О жизни Моисея законодателя» exists in Russian, so catalogue hits for «О жизни Моисея» usually mean Gregory, not Philo.
item_171.en_found:
FULL, several times over.
(1) C. D. Yonge, The Works of Philo Judaeus, vol. 3 (London: Bohn, 1855). It is public domain, with Mos. II split into Books 2–3. It is digitized as First1KGreek tlg0018.tlg022.1st1K-eng1 (cts metadata checked) and at earlyjewishwritings.com/philo.html.
(2) F. H. Colson, Philo VI, Loeb Classical Library (1935). This is per the ruwiki and frwiki Loeb lists. Colson died in 1943, so it is public domain under life+70. US status depends on copyright renewal (not checked).
(3) Jeffrey M. Hunt, Philo of Alexandria, De vita Mosis (Book I): An Introduction with Text, Translation, and Notes (Ancient Christianity and its Contexts; Baylor UP, 2023). This is cited in the de.wikipedia «Kommentare» section; I did not see the book itself.
item_171.other_found:
FR: Les Œuvres de Philon d'Alexandrie, vol. 22, De vita Mosis / De la vie de Moïse (Cerf, 1967, 324 pp.), per fr.wikipedia. The translator team is not named there; from memory it is Arnaldez, Mondésert, Pouilloux and Savinel (unverified).
DE: Die Werke Philos von Alexandria in deutscher Übersetzung (Cohn, Heinemann, Adler, Theiler; Breslau 1909–38, Berlin 1964). The series is confirmed by de.wikipedia. From memory, «Über das Leben Mosis» is in Bd. 1 (1909), translated by B. Badt (volume and translator unverified).
ES: from memory, J. M. Triviño, Obras completas (Buenos Aires, 1975–76), and the Trotta Obras completas ed. J. P. Martín (2009–) include Vida de Moisés (unverified this session).
IT: Italian versions are known to exist, e.g. «Vita di Mosè» (Rusconi/Bompiani tradition); translator and year not verified.
Hebrew: unverified.
item_171.source_text:
The standard critical edition is still L. Cohn, Philonis Alexandrini opera quae supersunt IV (Berlin: Reimer, 1902), Mos. I–II. Cohn died in 1915, so it is public domain; no newer critical edition supersedes it, and the Cerf and Loeb texts rest on Cohn.
Open digital text: First1KGreek / OGL, urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0018.tlg022.1st1K-grc1, TEI XML from Cohn 1902, with Yonge's English alongside: https://github.com/OpenGreekAndLatin/First1KGreek/tree/master/data/tlg0018/tlg022 (the project is normally CC BY-SA).
The archive.org scan cited in the sheet (philonisalexandr0004leop) exists, but IA notes "most of the text is cut-off due to tight binding". Use First1KGreek or another scan for work.
In-copyright modern aids: Cerf vol. 22 (1967) and Hunt 2023. Colson's 1935 Loeb is public domain outside the US.
item_171.research_yield: Moses as nomos empsychos/philosopher-king (Mos. I 148–162, II 1–7) set against Hellenistic peri basileias texts and Alexander ideology; Philo's Septuagint legend (II 25–44) versus Aristeas (extends Afonasin 2022); Philo, Artapanus, Exagoge, Josephus; reception in Gregory of Nyssa's De vita Moysis (both already in Russian).
item_171.recommendation: Keep at priority 3: it is a first Russian translation only, since EN/FR/DE/ES versions are full. Start with Mos. II 1–65 (king, lawgiver, Septuagint legend; c. 5–6k words), then Book I. Before publishing, run the RSL, eLibrary and Вевюрко 2013 checks that the exhausted search budget blocked.
